papers.title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $\alpha$, LP-$\alpha$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$\alpha$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $\xi$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $\xi$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $\phi$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $\phi$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $\alpha$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $\xi$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $\phi$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $\xi$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.

papers.title: Near-Horizon Scalar-Wave Sampling: Rindler Bounds and Schwarzschild Comparison
papers.abstract: We study classical reconstruction of an outgoing scalar-wave component from radial-shell observations. Starting from the noncompact-time Rindler metric, we construct Klein--Gordon evolution by closed quadratic forms and reduce the massless characteristic dynamics to translation in optical distance. For an initial optical interval of length $L$, a shell of width $d$, and recording time $T$, the optimal squared observability bounds are $A(T,L)=\min\{d,(T-L)_+\}$ and $B(T,L)=\min\{d,T\}$. At $T=L$, the Rindler observation map is injective with nonclosed range. Discrete shell observations form a spatial fusion frame precisely when their transported regions cover the initial interval; we compute optimal uniform-grid bounds and characterize robustness under profile erasures. Finite-resolution reconstruction separates localization error, approximation error and noise amplification. For fixed Schwarzschild mass and angular momentum, we compare the scalar-wave observation operator with its Rindler limit. Anchored finite-energy preparation permits arbitrary prescribed outgoing $L^2([-L,0])$ profiles without a zero-integral condition. The operator error is explicitly $O(e^{-2\kappa a})$ as an apparatus of fixed optical size is translated toward the horizon; whenever $T>L$, positive Rindler bounds transfer to Schwarzschild for all sufficiently large $a$. A positive Schwarzschild lower bound is impossible at or below the optical travel time, for every translation. These results concern classical observation and reconstruction, not quantum information or dissipative horizon evolution.

papers.title: Ideal balanced pairs in n-exangulated categories
papers.authors: Peiyu Zhang, Zhuolin Zheng, Li Wang, Dajun Liu
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to ideal approximation theory in $n$-exangulated categories. We define ideal balanced pairs and explore their properties and equivalent characterizations. We prove that any complete ideal cotorsion triple $(\mathcal{I},\mathcal{K},\mathcal{J})$ satisfying suitable assumptions yields an ideal balanced pair $(\mathcal{I}, \mathcal{J})$, and the converse holds under additional hypotheses. We further show that for an ideal balanced pair, it is equivalent to an additive subfunctor with enough projective morphisms and enough injective morphisms.

papers.title: Wavelet covariances under fixed finite observations: dilation symmetry breaking and distinct endpoint limits
papers.abstract: For a centered homogeneous generalized Gaussian field with spectral weight $C|\omega|^{-\gamma}$, we prove two-endpoint recovery of normalized posterior wavelet covariances under fixed finite admissible observations. Global dilation symmetry holds if and only if all observation functions vanish. The nonzero wavelet and the observation functions are real Schwartz functions with $M\geq1$ vanishing moments, with $C>0$ and $\gamma<2M+1$. Noise is Gaussian and field-independent, and total observation covariance is positive definite. Under simultaneous dilation of target scales and positions, multiplication by $\lambda^{-\gamma}$ recovers the prior covariance as $\lambda\downarrow0$ and $\lambda\uparrow\infty$, uniformly on every fixed compact target set. If a nonzero observation function exists, additional finite first nonzero Fourier orders $m_\psi,m_i$ at zero of the wavelet and nonzero observation functions yield compact-uniform recovery bounds $O(\lambda^{2m_\psi+1-\gamma})$ and $O(\lambda^{-(2\min_i m_i+1-\gamma)})$, with leading coefficients and cancellation-dependent improvements. The bounds are exact leading orders when their coefficients are nonzero. For the Mat\'ern-type spectrum $S(\omega)=C(\kappa^2+\omega^2)^{-p}$, $\kappa>0$, $1/2<p<M+1/2$, fixed finite noisy point observations yield distinct compact-uniform limits: the homogeneous $C|\omega|^{-2p}$ kernel after multiplication by $\lambda^{-2p}$ at small scales, and the constant-spectrum $S(0)$ kernel without normalization at large scales. A projection-norm criterion treats fixed closed observation subspaces; Mexican-hat formulas illustrate the finite-observation results.

papers.title: The Geometry of Wigwag and Reversal Linework in Blown Glass
papers.abstract: Wigwag and reversal linework in blown glass produces periodic wave, spiral, and radiating patterns by twisting longitudinal stripes in alternating directions and then reorganizing the patterned tube. Although glassworkers have developed many consistent techniques and identifiable pattern forms, these patterns do not appear to have been widely described within a common coordinate framework. This paper presents one way of modeling these patterns mathematically. Periodic linework is defined on a cylinder, represented on a sphere, and read relative to a switched axis. The switched pattern may then be re-formed into cylindrical or circular configurations and further manipulated into square, rectangular, or compound forms. The circular case provides a particularly simple radial representation of the switched spherical field. This sequence describes the characteristic organization of a reversal, with the same geometry extending to stacked encalmo sections and other compound structures. The goal is to provide a concise mathematical language for interpreting this broad family of patterned glass forms.

papers.title: Triangulation, Volume, and Symmetries of the Dihedral Group Analogue of the Permutohedron
papers.abstract: We study the analogue of the permutohedron for the dihedral group, which we call the dihedral permutohedron. We determine the facet structure of the dihedral permutohedron, use the facet structure to construct a triangulation, and determine a nice combinatorial formula for the volume of the dihedral permutohedron. Lastly, we find a family of interesting unimodular affine symmetries of the odd dihedral permutohedron.

papers.title: OFFER (One-Formula-Facilitates-Every-Relation) for Calculus
papers.abstract: The large number of calculus formulas makes learning calculus heavily memory-dependent and can scare away many students. Based on Issac Newton's idea of prediction, this paper shows that calculus students need to master only one critical formula: his proposition that, given boundary data, one can predict the interior and vice versa. We can treat other formulas as consequences of the formula for this proposition. In 1-, 2-, and 3-dimensional spaces, this formula corresponds to the fundamental theorem of calculus, Green's theorem, and the divergence theorem. This approach is summarized as OFFER (one-formula-facilitates-every-relationship) for calculus education. This paper demonstrates the method and advantages of the OFFER pedagogy. The OFFER approach can accelerate the pace of calculus teaching, provide deeper insight into calculus, inspire questions from students, and naturally facilitate the inclusion of real-world data, artificial intelligence (AI), and computer coding in the calculus series. Consequently, OFFER may serve as a way to modernize calculus curricula in the era of AI and the digital economy.

papers.title: An Asymptotic for Non-Wieferich Numbers
papers.abstract: A cyclic number is a positive integer $n$ such that $\gcd(n, \varphi(n)) = 1$. Erd\H{o}s showed that the number of cyclic numbers up to $x$, $C(x)$, has $C(x) \sim e^{-\gamma}x/\log_3(x)$ asymptotically as $x$ tends to infinity. We define Wieferich numbers to be odd, positive integers $n$ such that $(n, (2^{\ell(n)}-1)/n) > 1$, where $\ell(n)$ is the smallest positive integer with $2^{\ell(n)} \equiv 1 \mod n$. Franco and Pomerance showed that non-Wieferich numbers have density zero among the odd integers. We show that the counting function of $n \leq x$ in the symmetric difference of non-Wieferich numbers and cyclic numbers is $O(x/(\log_3(x))^2)$, under a mild assumption on the counting function of Wieferich primes.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Eventual Stability Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to the eventual stability conjecture over number fields and classify for power maps.

papers.title: Approximating the Ellipse Perimeter by "Bending the Line": The ELIP Closed-Form Family
papers.abstract:
The perimeter of an ellipse is expressed exactly through the complete elliptic integral of the second kind, motivating accurate closed-form approximations. We introduce ELIP (Ellipse Linear Interpolated Perimeter), a family built by correcting the straight line joining the two exact normalized endpoint values. Two branches are developed: logarithmic-power corrections with optional deformation and exponential modulators, and rational-logarithmic corrections incorporating the exact asymptotic behavior of highly elongated ellipses. The framework distinguishes coefficients fixed analytically by Maclaurin matching from parameters optimized numerically by minimax fitting.
  Compact rationalized formulas achieve maximum relative errors of approximately 6.84, 3.57, 0.904, and 1.596 ppm. An ELIP R5,2 + 3 log formula with three fitted degrees of freedom has a certified maximum relative error below 0.001623 ppm. For ELIP R5,3 + 3 log, all rational-core coefficients are determined by exact Maclaurin matching. A one-parameter multiplicative correction, 1 - A*h^12*(1-h)^(7/4), reduces the certified global error bound to below 0.000452 ppm. This formula matches the exact perimeter series through h^8, while the correction starts at order h^12. The results provide a systematic approach combining exact endpoint geometry, local series constraints, elongated-limit logarithmic asymptotics, and low-dimensional numerical optimization.

papers.title: A Duality of the F Distribution
papers.authors: Zifeng Zhang, Peng Ding, Wen Zhou, Chenlu Shi
papers.abstract: The F distribution arises naturally in linear regression or analysis of variance. Elementary textbooks state the result in terms of the standard normal random vector and fixed projection matrices. More advanced textbooks and research articles have extended the result to spherically symmetric random vectors. We complement the literature with a dual result that the F distribution arises with a fixed vector and random projection matrices generated by a left-spherical random matrix.

papers.title: Two q-Deformations of Narayana Polynomials: Rogers Moments, Hankel Positivity, and q-Narayana Kernels
papers.abstract:
We study two $q$-deformations of the continuous interpolation between type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana polynomials, both constructed from the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) functional. The first consists of affine moments of ordinary powers. For fixed $0<q<1$ and $-1<\beta<1$, we prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity in the polynomial variable by a continuant comparison criterion. We also determine leading continuants, Hankel determinants, and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors.
  The second deformation uses Askey--Wilson basis products and yields a basic-hypergeometric Narayana kernel. We give two independent moment evaluations and prove that its row polynomials have simple negative zeros and are $\gamma$-positive after palindromic normalization. An Askey--Wilson integral with base $q^2$ gives a continuous-parameter extension and a moment proof of the Krattenthaler--Wachs super $q$-Narayana expansion, including its integrality. An ordinary-power expansion also proves Pan's Touchard identity.
  For fixed $0<q<1$ and $\theta>-1$, we prove total positivity of the kernel triangle by a Jackson $q$-Bessel--Edrei factorization and strict total positivity of its associated square by a discrete moment representation. This gives a simultaneous $(\theta,q)$-extension of Wang--Yang's theorems for type $A$ and type $B$ Narayana triangles and squares. We further establish coefficientwise total nonnegativity in $q$ through order two for the endpoint triangles. An exact triangular change of basis links the two deformations and explains their common classical limit.

papers.title: A Structure-Preserving Scheme for Computing the Gradient of the Eikonal Equation
papers.abstract: We propose a first-order, structure-preserving method for directly computing the normalized traveltime gradient of the eikonal equation in smooth first-arrival regions. The method combines analytical derivatives of spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) in a Godunov-type upwind discretization with spherical forward Euler (SFE) pseudo-time integration. This construction gives a tangent residual and keeps every iterate on $\mathbb{S}^2$ without projection or normalization. The SLERP discretization exactly preserves a family of curved orientation equilibria. Removing the background discretization bias improves absolute orientation accuracy near these equilibria, allowing a prescribed error tolerance to be reached on a coarser grid. We prove the equilibrium-preservation property and, separately, a smaller angular error for SFE than normalized Euler in a one-cell relaxation under the stated step-size condition. Two- and three-dimensional experiments examine convergence, geometric preservation, and computational cost. Comparisons with gradient recovery from scalar traveltimes show more accurate directions on the same grid in the curved media considered. The method provides direction fields for wave propagation and geometric optics, with potential use in adjoint-based inverse problems.

papers.title: Low-Dimensional Reduction of Mean-Field Coupled Dynamical Systems with Units Described by Two Real Variables: Classification and Applications
papers.abstract: Low-dimensional reduction is crucial for understanding network systems with many units. In a recent advance, Martens and Dharmavaram developed a theory of exact low-dimensional reduction for a general class of mean-field coupled dynamical systems characterized by a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure. In this paper, we classify mean-field coupled dynamical systems with a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, where each unit is described by two real variables. Our classification is based on Gonz\'alez-L\'opez, Kamran, and Olver's local classification of Lie systems on the plane near generic points and yields 28 types of mean-field coupled dynamical systems. For mean-field coupled systems with units described by two real variables, we first present a general theory on classification and low-dimensional reduction based on the mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, and then discuss applications to populations of coupled oscillators. We show that low-dimensional reduction is possible for a broad class of populations of limit-cycle oscillators, extending the previously reported reducible class of populations of Stuart-Landau oscillators to include many new models.

papers.title: Outer automorphisms of HNN extensions of abelian groups
papers.authors: Naomi Andrew, Sam Hughes, Motiejus Valiunas
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a commensurating HNN extension of a finitely generated free abelian group. We characterise when $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ is finitely generated and derive structural information about the group. We give soluble and non-soluble examples of commensurating HNN extensions of finitely generated free abelian groups with outer automorphism group not finitely generated.

papers.title: Sharp quantitative stability of the Hong--Krahn--Szeg\H{o} inequality
papers.abstract: We establish sharp quantitative stability estimates for the Hong--Krahn--Szeg\H{o} inequality for arbitrary open sets of positive finite measure in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. In dimensions $d\ge3$, the optimal stability exponent is $(d+2)/2$, while in dimension two the sharp stability modulus is $t^2/\log(e/t)$. These results improve the quantitative stability estimate of Brasco and Pratelli~\cite[Theorem 3.5]{BP} and resolve Open Problem 7.56 of Brasco and De Philippis~\cite[Open Problem 7.56]{BDP}.

papers.title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
papers.authors: Yucheng Liu, Leonardo T. Rolla, Yuliang Shi
papers.abstract:
We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$.
  On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge11$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.

papers.title: Sch\"affer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$
papers.authors: Imin Chen, Stephen Choi, James Houle
papers.abstract: In 1956, Sch\"affer made a conjecture on the whole number solutions to the Diophantine equation $S_k(x):=1^k+2^k+\cdots+x^k=y^n$. In this paper we show how for even $k$, we can descend to a long list of three coupled equations of the form $Ax^p-By^p=1$, where $A,B\in\mathbb{Q}$. To this system, we apply the modular method, linear forms in logarithms, and local methods. As a result, we prove Sch\"affer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$.

papers.title: A quaternary Diophantine inequality with prime numbers of a special form (II)
papers.authors: Yuhua Zhao, Jinjiang Li, Linji Long, Min Zhang
papers.abstract:
Let $N$ be a sufficiently large real number. In this paper, it is proved that, for $1<c<\frac{5179}{3909}$ and for any arbitrary large number $E>0$, the Diophantine inequality \begin{equation*}
  \big|p_1^c+p_2^c+p_3^c+p_4^c-N\big|<(\log N)^{-E} \end{equation*} is solvable in prime variables $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ such that each of the numbers $p_i+2\,(i=1,2,3,4)$ has, counted according to multiplicity, at most $[\frac{31250}{5179-3909c}]$ prime factors, which constitutes a large improvement upon the previous results of Dimitrov [13] and Li-Xue-Zhang [22], respectively.

papers.title: Low-degree filtrations in ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology
papers.abstract:
We prove the Hilbert-series formulas conjectured by Reiner--Tudose and by the Polymath Jr. Grassmannian group for the subalgebras of ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology generated in bounded degree. We determine the finite coefficient images underlying the proofs, together with the kernels of the coefficient and cancellation maps. We also construct bases adapted to the auxiliary ideal filtrations and identify the cancellation layers, as modules, with shifts of finite complete-intersection algebras. First-order deformations give the derivative inclusions needed to recover the filtration increments.
  We disprove the two ordinary basis conjectures of the Polymath group. For every $r\ge 2$, the span of each prescribed family has codimension one in weight $3r+2$ of $H^{2*}(\operatorname{Gr}(2,3r+1);\mathbb Q)$; replacing one index gives a basis in each of these components. More generally, each prescribed two-row family has codimension at most one in every weight. Weights are half the cohomological degrees, and all coefficients are rational.

papers.title: A relative Schinzel-Zassenhaus bound for the polynomial $T^2 - 1$
papers.abstract: For $f(T) = T^2 - 1$, we establish a lower bound for the relative dynamical house of wandering algebraic integers. This bound depends on the degree over the maximal abelian extension of the rationals. Our proof follows Dimitrov's approach to the Schinzel-Zassenhaus Conjecture and its generalization by Habegger-Schmidt.

papers.title: Spherically Supported Sets with Variable Radii
papers.abstract: We study closed sets for which, at every boundary point, there exists a containing supporting ball whose prescribed radius may vary from point to point. This extends the notion of spherical support from constant to variable radii. The variable-radius setting presents a new difficulty: unlike the constant-radius case, the intersection of the supporting balls need not be strongly convex with respect to the prescribed radii. We overcome this difficulty by associating with every such set a canonical set and an induced radius function determined by the active supporting balls. For continuous prescribed radii, our main result establishes a geometric dichotomy: the original set either coincides with the canonical set and is strongly convex with respect to the prescribed radii, or it is contained in the boundary of the canonical set, which is strongly convex with respect to the induced radii. An example shows that the induced radii cannot, in general, be replaced by the prescribed ones in the second alternative. We also recover the constant-radius theory and characterize variable-radius strong convexity in terms of the spherical support of the boundary.

papers.title: Closedness of bounded strength and partition rank loci
papers.abstract: We show the existence of a quartic form of strength $3$ in the closure of the strength at most $2$ locus, answering a question of Ballico--Bik--Oneto--Ventura in the negative. In the analogous setting of partition rank as introduced by Naslund, we further show that the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $2$ is closed, but the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $3$ is not. Together with a suspension lemma, this answers for all $r$ whether the locus of forms/tensors of strength/partition rank at most $r$ is Zariski-closed.

papers.title: Deflation-Based Spectral Preconditioning for the Conjugate Gradient Method on Perturbed Systems
papers.authors: Youssef Diouane, Selime G\"urol, Oussama Mouhtal, Dominique Orban
papers.abstract: We consider sequences of large symmetric positive-definite linear systems in which spectral information from a reference matrix $A$ is reused to accelerate the solution of a nearby system with perturbed matrix $A(t)=A+tE$, where $E$ is symmetric, $\|E\|_F=1$, and $t\geq0$ is the perturbation size. We compare deflated conjugate gradient (deflated CG) with preconditioned CG (PCG) equipped with a scaled spectral preconditioner constructed from the same spectral information of $A$. First, we derive an energy-norm error characterization of deflated CG. We then use perturbation analysis to show that, after one additional PCG iteration, the squared PCG error is bounded, up to terms of order $t^2$, by an explicit multiple of the squared deflated CG error. This result clarifies the role of the scaling parameter in the preconditioner. Experiments show that the scaled spectral preconditioner recovers much of the convergence improvement provided by deflation while requiring fewer products with $A(t)$.

papers.title: The moduli space of maps from hypersurfaces and its Goodwillie tower
papers.abstract: We define a moduli space of continuous maps from smooth hypersurfaces varying in an ample linear system. To study its topology, we construct a scanning map to an appropriate section space and investigate its effect on homology. Our main innovation is a general argument based on Goodwillie calculus and applicable to various moduli spaces of maps. Along the way, we compute the Goodwillie tower of the section space functor based at any retractive space.

papers.title: Embeddings of Relative Dimension Groups for Zero-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Let $\pi:(X,T)\rightarrow(Y,S)$ be a factor map between zero-dimensional dynamical systems, and let $X_0$ and $Y_0$ be quasi-sections with $\pi(X_0)=Y_0$. We study the homomorphism $\pi^*:K^0(Y|Y_0,S)\rightarrow K^0(X|X_0,T)$, $[f]\mapsto[f\circ\pi]$, between the corresponding relative dimension groups, and identify it with the homomorphism induced by the premorphism between Bratteli--Vershik realizations associated with $\pi$. Generalizing a result of Glasner and Weiss for minimal Cantor systems, we show that if $Y_0$ is quasi-simple, then $\pi^*$ is an injective unital order-preserving homomorphism, and that if $X_0=\pi^{-1}(Y_0)$, then $\pi^*$ is a unital order embedding; the latter condition is characterized in terms of the premorphism. Examples show that quasi-simplicity cannot be dropped, and that without the condition $X_0=\pi^{-1}(Y_0)$ the map $\pi^*$ need not be an order embedding.

papers.title: A Matroidal Framework for Random Access in Linear Codes
papers.authors: Daniella Bar-Lev, Hiram H. L\'opez, Gretchen L. Matthews, Flavio Salizzoni
papers.abstract: We study random access in linear codes when codeword symbols are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement. A code is recovery balanced if the expected number of samples required to recover a codeword coordinate is the same for every coordinate. We express the recovery expectations in terms of the associated matroid and derive a coordinatewise identity relating these values for a code and its dual. This proves that a linear code is recovery balanced if and only if its dual is recovery balanced, establishing a conjecture of Gruica et al. We further define the recovery balance for arbitrary matroids and show that asymptotically almost every sparse paving matroid is not recovery balanced.

papers.title: Short sums of the M\"obius function over function fields
papers.authors: Etienne Fouvry, Igor E. Shparlinski, Ping Xi
papers.abstract: We develop a new method which allows us to estimate, with a power saving, sums of the M{\"o}bius function over function fields $\F_p(X)$. The sums run over monic polynomials with all other coefficients in short intervals, of length below the P\'olya--Vinogradov threshold $p^{1/2}$. A classical result of L.~Stickelberger (1898) reduces this question to bounding character sums with polynomial discriminants which are inhomogeneous multivariate polynomials. Variants of Burgess's method with non-linear shifts {\it {\`a} la carte} are introduced to go beyond the P\'olya--Vinogradov range, combined with a stratification result of J. Xu (2020) for complete character sums.

papers.title: Free boundary minimal hypersurfaces of Morse index one in Eucildean half-space
papers.abstract: We prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a half-space of RN, with nonempty boundary is a higher-dimensional half-catenoid. We also prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a quarter-space is the higher-dimensional quarter-catenoid.

papers.title: A counterexample to Gale's conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: It is known that for every partition of the sphere $S^2$ of unit diameter into four parts, the largest diameter of a part is at least $\sqrt{(3+\sqrt{3})/6} = 0.88807\dots$, and this bound is attained. The conjecture of D.~Gale (1953) asserts that no set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a larger ratio. In this paper, we construct a $101$-point set $V\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every partition of $V$ into four parts contains a part of diameter greater than $0.88928 \, \operatorname{diam} V$.

papers.title: A smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain with incomplete Kobayashi distance
papers.abstract: We construct a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\C^3$ with $C^\infty$ boundary which is not Kobayashi complete. The domain has a smooth plurisubharmonic defining function, and its Carath\'eodory distance is also incomplete. We then prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain with $C^\infty$ boundary of finite D'Angelo type is Kobayashi complete. Consequently, every bounded pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary is Kobayashi complete. We also obtain quantitative lower estimates for the Kobayashi--Royden metric and the Kobayashi distance in the finite-type case.

papers.title: Subset sums of power values over Galois rings
papers.abstract:
Let $R=GR(p^m,p^{mf})$, where $p$ is prime, $q=p^f$, $m,f\geq1$, $d\geq2$ and $p\nmid d$. We count $n$-element subsets of $P=\{x^d:x\in R\}\setminus\{0\}$, the set of distinct nonzero $d$th-power values, with a prescribed sum. For fixed $m,d,n$ with $n\geq3$, the count equals \[
  q^{-m}\binom{|P|}{n}(1+O_{m,d,n}(q^{1-n/2}))
  \] as $q\to\infty$ through admissible prime powers, uniformly over all targets and with both $p$ and $f$ allowed to vary. For fixed $m,d$, we also classify uniform relative equidistribution at the remaining positive sizes: it fails at $n=1$, and at $n=2$ it holds along an admissible sequence if and only if, for all sufficiently large terms, $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$ and $(m\geq2\text{ or }p\ne2)$.

papers.title: On a conjecture of Velani
papers.abstract: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hat{\mu}(2^k)|^\sigma < \infty$ for any $\sigma > 0$, where $\mu$ is the Cantor measure.

papers.title: Methods for Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations from the Dynamics of Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Tuning of Low-Fidelity Optimization Models via High-Fidelity Feedback
papers.authors: Gonzalo E. Constante-Flores, Andr\'e H. Quisaguano-Paredes, Asha Ramanujam, Rishabh Gupta, Can Li
papers.abstract: Low-fidelity (LF) optimization models are widely used in large-scale operations because they can be solved efficiently and reliably, but they often exhibit systematic errors relative to high-fidelity (HF) formulations that better capture physical and operational constraints. Existing learning-based approaches typically rely on supervised or semi-supervised training with HF solutions, which are expensive to compute and may not align with HF operational objectives. We propose a self-supervised framework that parameterizes LF optimization models directly from HF feedback. The low-fidelity problem is embedded as a differentiable optimization layer and trained end-to-end, while a HF correction problem evaluates its solution and provides gradient information through its dual variables, without requiring HF solution labels. We evaluate the framework on optimal power flow, optimal gas flow, and pooling problems, spanning different sources of low- and high-fidelity mismatch. Across all three applications, the self-supervised approach improves objective quality and feasibility over untuned LF models and generally outperforms semi-supervised training. The learned parameterizations also generalize to unseen operating conditions and, for network applications with up to 30,000 nodes, to systems not encountered during training.

papers.title: From Wheel to Jahangir graphs: spectra and energy under structured edge deletion
papers.authors: Diego Bravo, Florencia Cubr\'ia, Annabella Zapattini
papers.abstract: The energy of a graph, introduced by Gutman, is defined as the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. In this work we study how the energy of the Wheel graph $W_n$ changes when a specific set of spokes is removed. The resulting graphs are precisely the Jahangir graphs $J_{m,n}$, where m divides n, and which may also be viewed as the Cycle graph $C_n$ together with an additional vertex adjacent to certain vertices of $C_n$ in a cyclic pattern. We determine the spectra of $J_{2,n}$, $J_{4,n}$, and $J_{6,n}$ by exploiting a factorization of their characteristic polynomials arising from equitable partitions. This yields explicit closed formulas for their energies. Moreover, under certain conditions, we establish the following monotonicity chain: \[\mathcal{E}(C_n) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{6,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{4,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{2,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(W_n).\]

papers.title: Kirszbraun's Intersection Property and Nonexpansive Extensions
papers.abstract: This paper aims to present the historical development of the extension problem of nonexpansive maps in Euclidean and Hilbert spaces, and to serve as a comprehensive guide to this specific area. Such extensions are based on a geometric property of the intersection of closed balls in Euclidean spaces, known as the Kirszbraun intersection property. Subsequently, a number of authors have extended this property to Hilbert and other spaces. All these results are discussed in this paper, but the paper itself is not a mechanical compilation of already known proofs. The material has been developed with an emphasis on the natural connections between all these results and the corresponding concepts involved in them. Furthermore, most of these results are presented with new simplified proofs. Last but not least, the paper also contains some new results related to this extension problem.

papers.title: Tree-independence number VIII. 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number
papers.authors: Maria Chudnovsky, Julien Codsi, Ajaykrishnan E S, Daniel Lokshtanov, Ilya Maier
papers.abstract: A three-path-configuration is a graph consisting of three pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths, the union of every two of which is an induced cycle of length at least four. A graph is 3PC-free if no induced subgraph of it is a three-path-configuration. We show that 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number, which is asymptotically best possible.

papers.title: Hecke Orbits on Globally Drinfeld-Uniformized Shimura Varieties Are $p$-adically Nowhere Dense
papers.abstract: Fix a projective unitary Shimura datum satisfying Varshavsky's global Drinfeld uniformization hypotheses at a place $v\mid p$ of its reflex field $E$. Let $\mathcal{S}h$ be the base change of the Shimura variety to $\mathbb C_p$ at a sufficiently small neat finite level. We prove that for every closed reduced algebraic subvariety $Z\subset\mathcal{S}h$ with $\operatorname{dim} Z<\operatorname{dim} \mathcal{S}h$, the $p$-adic closure of its full finite adelic Hecke orbit has empty interior in $\mathcal{S}h(\mathbb C_p)$. At certain compatible levels, the nowhere density theorem also holds for Shimura varieties associated with a related PEL datum having the same adjoint datum as Varshavsky's. Moreover, for every rational prime $p$ and every integer $d\geq2$, there is a projective unitary Shimura variety of dimension $d-1$ satisfying these uniformization hypotheses at a place above $p$ for which the nowhere density theorem holds.

papers.title: A sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines
papers.abstract: We construct a sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines in the real projective plane. It is obtained from the icosahedral arrangement $\mathcal{A}(21,2)$ by adjoining the $30$ images of the line $y+\sqrt{\varphi}\,z=0$ under the rotation group of the icosahedron, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. Its intersection multiplicities are $t_2=120$, $t_3=190$, $t_5=36$, and $t_6=15$, with all other $t_r$ zero. These counts give equality in Melchior's inequality and hence prove simpliciality. The arrangement is irreducible, belongs to neither of the two known infinite families of irreducible simplicial arrangements, and is not supersolvable. It therefore disproves the $37$-line bound for sporadic arrangements conjectured by Cuntz and M\"ucksch. We give explicit coordinates, a finite incidence certificate, a geometric explanation of the parameter $\sqrt{\varphi}$, and a standalone exact-arithmetic verifier.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Mixed Integer Programming Methods for Optimal Patch Antennas
papers.authors: Ruben Hoeksma, Jesse van Rhijn, Marc Uetz, Wick Wijnholds
papers.abstract:
Antennas come in various shapes and sizes, as their performance characteristics are very much dependent on their exact shape. Coming up with a shape that matches desired design characteristics has, up until this moment, been largely the domain of metaheuristics and local optimization methods. While these methods are convenient, they generally provide no performance guarantees and rarely allow to enforce hard design constraints.
  In this paper, we show how Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) can be used to optimize the shape of so-called patch antennas. The methodological focus is to show how underlying laws of physics allow to derive effective bounds on variables as well as new cutting planes. These greatly improve the effectiveness of the underlying basic MIP model, enabling the automated design of practically relevant patch antennas for a wide variety of applications.

papers.title: Hilbert-Kunz multiplicities of powers of ideals and normalized Hilbert coefficients
papers.authors: Tran Nam Trung, Hoang Le Truong
papers.abstract: We give negative answers to two questions of Smirnov on Hilbert coefficients of Frobenius powers and Hilbert-Kunz multiplicities of ordinary powers. We construct complete normal Cohen-Macaulay hypersurfaces whose maximal ideals have normalized Hilbert coefficients of every index at least three tending to minus infinity. We also construct isolated normal F-pure non-Cohen-Macaulay singularities whose maximal ideals have convergent normalized coefficients but do not satisfy the proposed eventual polynomial formula. For every Noetherian local ring of positive characteristic and dimension $d\geq2$, we prove convergence of the second normalized Hilbert coefficient and a three-term asymptotic expansion with remainder $o(n^{d-2})$. Thus coefficient convergence always holds in dimension two, and index three is the first possible failure in higher dimensions. Both questions have positive answers for every ideal primary to the maximal ideal in a local ring of finite F-representation type.

papers.title: Algebras with bounded multiplicities of the central cocharacters
papers.authors: Wesley Q. Cota, Luiz H. S. Matos, Breno O. Souza
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an associative PI-algebra over a field of characteristic zero. The central polynomials of $A$ give rise to a sequence $\{\chi_n^z(A)\}_{n\geq 1}$ of $S_n$-characters, called its central cocharacters. A natural problem is to understand which algebraic properties of $A$ are imposed by bounds on the multiplicities occurring in the decompositions of these cocharacters into irreducible characters. We prove that these multiplicities are bounded by one if and only if there exist scalars $(\alpha,\beta)\neq(0,0)$ such that $\alpha[x_1,x_2]x_1+\beta x_1[x_1,x_2]$ takes values in the center of $A$. This provides a central analogue of the Ananin-Kemer theorem for ordinary cocharacters. We also characterize the algebras whose central cocharacter multiplicities are uniformly bounded.

papers.title: Harmonic-Einstein maps and critical metrics for eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian
papers.abstract: We prove that Clarke critical metrics for the ratio of the first two eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian on a closed manifold with positive Yamabe constant correspond to harmonic--Einstein maps into a sphere. We discuss some rigidity consequences, as well as an extension to the higher-order GJMS operators.

papers.title: Mixed finite element methods for a heat-assisted model of sedimentation
papers.abstract: A model for the consolidation-sedimentation process incorporating thermal effects is analysed. The model is motivated by novel applications to heat-assisted sedimentation of mineral suspensions. A system of convection-diffusion equations for the concentration and temperature are coupled to flow equations for the volume-average velocity and pressure. The model is supplemented with Dirichlet and mixed boundary conditions. A quasi-stationary approach of the system is analysed by means of a mixed variational formulation, where additional variables such as the pseudostress tensor and variables for the gradient of the temperature and concentration are introduced. The existence and uniqueness of the system is shown making use of the Babu{\v s}ka-Brezzi theory and Banach's fixed-point theorem, under hypotheses of smallness of the data and additional regularity on the solutions. A discrete formulation based on finite element spaces is proposed and analysed, and the existence of solutions is achieved thanks to Brouwer's fixed-point theorem. Additionally, C\'ea and a priori estimates are derived for the mixed formulation. Finally, numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the performance of the model and to confirm the theoretical rates of convergence.

papers.title: Strong gradient absorption and initial decay prevent blow-up
papers.abstract:
Consider positive classical solutions of the Cauchy problem for $u_t-\Delta u=u^p-\mu|\nabla u|^q$, with sufficiently smooth initial data $u_0$, in the strong absorption regime, namely $q\ge p>1$ and $\mu>0$. It has remained a long standing open problem whether finite time blow-up can occur if $u_0$ decays at space infinity. We here solve this problem, showing that the answer in negative.
  To this end, we establish a novel, universal Bernstein-type gradient estimate, of independent interest, valid only in the range $q\ge p$. Moreover, the decay assumption on $u_0$ turns out to be essentially optimal. Indeed we show that the solution blows up in finite time whenever $u_0$ has a positive limit at infinity, and we determine the blow-up behavior of $u$ at space infinity under an additional assumption.

papers.title: The Octonionic Rational Wave Numbers: Non-Associative Sequence Algebras, Moufang Loops, and Exceptional $G_2$ Symmetries
papers.abstract: We generalize discrete rational wave numbers (arXiv:2609.23233) to the octonionic rational wave numbers $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ over Cayley's octonions $\mathbb{O}$. Rather than assuming higher imaginary units, all rational wave number spaces $\mathbb{C}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ are derived constructively from two scalar primitives: the coordinate advance $E_Z$ and phase calibration $E_{\bar{1}}$. Their closure under pointwise multiplication, inversion, and rational roots generates an infinite divisible Moufang loop on the sequence ring $\mathcal{S}_\mathbb{O} := \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$, terminating strictly at $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ via sedenionic zero-divisor excision. By Artin's Theorem, pairwise compositions remain strictly associative, whereas three-wave interactions generate an intrinsic non-associative curvature quantified by the associator $[u, v, w] = (uv)w - u(vw)$. We define a real-valued sequence inner product that bypasses the Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner obstruction, establishing the orthonormality of the seven Fano coordinate primitives. We establish three principal theorems: (1) The Invariant Hexagonal Mesh Theorem, proving that cumulative integration exhibits a scale-invariant bifurcation at $n=6$ governed by the root system of $G_2 = \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{O})$ and its $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ stabilizer subgroup; (2) The Algebraic Phase Jitter Theorem, showing that Catalan parenthesization trees across non-Fano triads produce an irreducible zero-point phase fluctuation, yielding an algebraic origin for vacuum jitter; and (3) The Rational Loop Closure Theorem, proving that rational frequencies select closed finite Moufang sub-loops, while irrational frequencies yield topologically dense, non-closing trajectories. This provides an autonomous, discrete algebraic foundation for non-associative geometry and fundamental physical symmetries.

papers.title: Kinetic Mean-Field Planning via Schr\"odinger Bridges: Existence, Penalization, and Consistency Bounds
papers.authors: Erhan Bayraktar, Zhiyan Ding, Hiroaki Horikawa
papers.abstract: We study a mean-field planning problem for a swarm of interacting, non-cooperative agents whose dynamics are stochastic and kinetic. The noise acts on the velocity only, and the interaction (of Cucker-Smale type for instance) enters through the drift. For a fixed flow, the problem reduces to a Schr\"odinger bridge problem, and we first prove the existence of an equilibrium by a Schauder fixed-point argument. Then we replace the hard terminal constraint by a penalty function and show that equilibria of the penalized problems converge, along subsequences, to an equilibrium of the original problem. Since equilibria are not unique in general, we instead quantify the consistency error, which measures how far an equilibrium of the penalized problem is from being an equilibrium of the original one. The rate is of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the relative-entropy penalty. The proof relies on the quantitative stability of entropic optimal transport and on a pointwise linear growth bound on the score of the degenerate reference dynamics, which is of independent interest.

papers.title: Lieb-Robinson bounds via the Combes-Thomas estimate
papers.authors: Tali Braester, Haochen Luo, George Peykanu, Sergii Solomakha
papers.abstract: This paper studies quantum spin systems: networks of spins coupled by local interactions. The Lieb-Robinson bound predicts that in these systems, information propagates at an essentially finite speed. We produce a new proof of this result. Our approach relies on a spectral bound on entries of resolvents of band matrices, the Combes-Thomas estimate, rather than on the standard path-counting argument.

papers.title: Boot-AVT: Asymptotically Anytime-Valid Testing with Degenerate U-Statistics via Bootstrap
papers.authors: Jixuan Liu, Long Feng, Liuhua Peng, Zhaojun Wang
papers.abstract: Many nonparametric tests are based on $U$-statistics that are degenerate under the null hypothesis. We develop Boot-AVT, a bootstrap procedure for asymptotically anytime-valid testing with these statistics. Using Brownian scaling and time inversion for the limiting Gaussian chaos process, we show that logarithmically penalized maxima over observed and future sample sizes have a common limiting null distribution. A quadratic multiplier bootstrap estimates the corresponding critical values. We also develop Boot-AVT-Multi for joint testing with multiple kernels. For both procedures, we establish uniform consistency of the bootstrap critical values, explicit bounds on size distortion, and asymptotic size $\alpha$ over an unbounded monitoring horizon as the monitoring start tends to infinity. Under fixed alternatives, we derive finite-horizon power bounds and establish power one with finite expected stopping times. Simulation studies evaluate finite-sample size and power in goodness-of-fit, two-sample and independence testing, and real-data analyses compare stopping times.

papers.title: Functional limit theorems for self-interacting random walks
papers.authors: Elena Kosygina, Laure Mar\^ech\'e, Thomas Mountford, Jonathon Peterson
papers.abstract: We consider a wide class of nearest neighbor self-interacting random walks on $\mathbb{Z}$ and show that, under mild conditions, their scaling limits at the process level can be uniquely identified and constructed directly from the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem for their local times, i.e., the joint convergence of rescaled local time ``curves'' of the walks stopped at certain stopping times together with the merge and absorption times of these ``curves'' to a concatenation of coalescing reflected-absorbed diffusions and their merge and absorption times. We apply our results to polynomially self-repelling walks introduced and studied in the mid-90s by B. T\'oth, and to ``true'' self-avoiding walks with bond repulsion. The first application solves a problem that has been open since T\'oth's work: it gives a construction and first properties of a new family of processes, polynomially self-repelling motions, as scaling limits of polynomially self-repelling walks. These processes were simultaneously and independently constructed from flows of correlated powers of Bessel processes by Y. Yu. The second application strengthens an earlier result on convergence of rescaled ``true'' self-avoiding walks to the ``true'' self-repelling motion of B. T\'oth and W. Werner, and streamlines its proof. Our results can be thought of as an ``inversion'' of the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem to get a functional limit theorem for self-interacting random walks.

papers.title: The domination number of the $k$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$
papers.authors: Nathaniel Chinman, Antonio Cortijo, Beatrice Pedroni, Ian Seong, Lucy Stenger
papers.abstract: This paper is about token graphs and domination number. Let $G=(X,E)$ denote an undirected graph that is connected, with no loops or multiple edges, vertex set $X$, and edge set $E$. Pick a positive integer $k\leq \vert X\vert$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, denoted by $F_k(G)$, is defined as follows. The vertex set $\mathcal{X}$ consists of all $k$-subsets of $X$. Two vertices $x,y\in \mathcal{X}$ are adjacent whenever the symmetric difference of $x$ and $y$ consists of two vertices that form an edge in $E$. In this paper, we compute the exact value for the domination number of $F_2(K_{m,n})$ where $K_{m,n}$ is the complete bipartite graph with parameters $m,n$. We present some bounds for the domination number of $F_k(K_{m,n})$ when $k\geq 3$.

papers.title: On the Road Again: How the $N$-Lane TASEP and Local Reservoirs Drive Jamming in Axonal Transport
papers.abstract: Intracellular transport by molecular motors along microtubules is essential for cellular function, particularly in neuronal axons where track disruption drives neurodegenerative disease. We develop an \(N\)-track totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) model where motors reversibly detach into local off-track states. Using mean-field, continuum, and fast-switching approximations, we derive an effective nonlinear transport equation for total motor density. This reduced model retains the classical TASEP phase structure but reveals that increasing \(N\) shifts the boundaries between low-density, high-density, and maximal-current regimes. Crucially, under source-driven boundary conditions reflecting constant cargo production, the entrance density undergoes a saddle-node bifurcation when the production rate exceeds the network's transport capacity, \(N/4\). This triggers persistent cargo accumulation that propagates throughout the domain. Our results establish a physical mechanism by which gradual microtubule degradation drives a transition from efficient transport to jammed pathological states.

papers.title: On Euler's abelian relation of the web induced by the forgetful maps on the moduli space $\boldsymbol{\mathcal M_{0,n+3}}$: the case when $n$ is even
papers.abstract:
In a previous paper ${\bf [P1]}$, for every $n\geq 2$, we studied the curvilinear web $\boldsymbol{\mathcal W}_{0,n+3}$ on the moduli space $\boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+3}$, defined by the $n+3$ forgetful maps $ \boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+3}\rightarrow \boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+2}$, with particular emphasis on its abelian relations. In particular, when $n$ is even, we conjectured an explicit formula for its Euler abelian relation. This relation is constructed \`a la Gelfand-MacPherson from an invariant differential form representing the appropriate power of the Euler class of the tautological bundle of the Grassmannian manifold $G_2^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathbf R^{n+3})$ of oriented $2$-planes in $\mathbf R^{n+3}$.
  In this note, we obtain an explicit antisymmetrized formula for Euler's abelian relation for every even $n\geq 2$, and prove that it coincides, up to the explicit factor $-(n+1)(n+2)/2$, with the formula conjectured in ${\bf [P1]}$, which is therefore established for all even $n$.

papers.title: Polynomial Invariants of Pseudo-Anosov Maps (Addendum)
papers.abstract: We show that homology, puncture, and symplectic polynomials of a pseudo-Anosov map arXiv:1001.5094 are invariants of the mapping class, as well as of the conjugacy class.

papers.title: Same Gaps, Different Sets: A Survey on Complimentary sets and their Dimensions
papers.authors: Nicol\'as Angelini, Carlos Cabrelli, Ursula Molter
papers.abstract:
Let a=\{a_n\} be a non-increasing sequence of positive real numbers adding up to $1$. Cutting out of the unit interval disjoint open gaps of lengths $a_1,a_2,\dots$, one for each term, leaves a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero, and since the gaps can be placed in infinitely many ways, there are infinitely many such sets. We call them the \emph{complementary sets} of $a$ and write $\mathfrak{C}_a$ for the family of all of them. Every set in $\mathfrak{C}_a$ is compact and totally disconnected, and all of them share the same gap lengths; what distinguishes one from another is only the arrangement of the gaps. Among them, the perfect sets are exactly the Cantor sets with those gaps, and they form a distinguished subclass.
  The central question of this survey is what such a rearrangement can change and what it cannot. The answer depends sharply on the notion of size: the box dimensions are constant on $\mathfrak{C}_a$, while the Hausdorff dimension attains every value in a closed interval whose endpoints are realised by two distinguished members, the Cantor set $C_a$ built by placing the gaps in a Cantor-like pattern, and the countable decreasing rearrangement $D_a$. We survey how this dichotomy persists, and how the roles of $C_a$ and $D_a$ are exchanged, across the intermediate dimensions of Falconer, Fraser and Kempton, the Assouad-type and $\Phi$-dimensions, and the Hausdorff and packing $h$-measures associated with a general dimension function; we also describe the almost sure behaviour of a randomly rearranged complementary set, where a sharp threshold in the depth of the scales examined separates two incompatible regimes. A final part restricts attention to the Cantor subclass and turns to the dynamical description of the sets C_a.

papers.title: Asymptotics of Masur-Veech volume of strata of quadratic differentials with many simple poles
papers.abstract: We provide large $n$ asymptotics of the Masur-Veech volumes for strata of quadratic differentials of the form $\mathcal{Q}_g(n,d_1,\dots,d_k,-1^{n+D-4g+4})$, where all positive integers $d_i$ are fixed and $D=d_1+\dots+d_k$. Our formulae are particularly explicit in genus $1$. For the two series of non-varying strata $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,-1^n)$ and $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,1,-1^{n+1})$ we give simple closed formulae for the volumes for any $n$.

papers.title: Universality of approximate message passing under a fourth-moment tail condition
papers.abstract: We prove state evolution for approximate message passing (AMP) with rectangular random matrices whose entries are independent, centered, and variance-normalized. The row and column dimensions grow with a ratio that converges to a positive finite limit. The entry laws may differ across coordinates and dimensions, and we assume uniform integrability of the fourth powers of the rescaled entries. For entries sampled independently from a fixed law, a finite fourth moment suffices, with no requirement for higher moments. The nonlinearities are continuously differentiable and globally Lipschitz, with bounded continuous first state derivatives. The signal and noise have independent and identically distributed coordinates with finite moments of all orders, and are independent of each other and of the matrix. At every fixed number of iterations, empirical averages of pseudo-Lipschitz functions of order two converge in probability to the limits specified by Gaussian state evolution. These averages include empirical second moments and products of trajectory coordinates. The proof combines an aggregate bound on third derivatives with randomized Lindeberg replacement and operator-norm truncation, without matching third moments or invoking a non-Gaussian universality theorem. We also show that independence of complementary projected components for every deterministic rank-one constraint pair characterizes Gaussian entries. This identifies the limitation of extending Gaussian conditioning identities to independent non-Gaussian matrices. Finally, a variance-profile example shows that average variance normalization alone does not ensure the homogeneous state evolution limits.

papers.title: On the automorphisms of Pick bodies
papers.abstract: We determine the biholomorphic automorphisms of the Pick body associated with finitely many distinct points in a Carath\'eodory hyperbolic domain. Every automorphism is the composition of a common disc automorphism applied to all coordinates and a coordinate permutation preserving the Pick body. The proof uses the quotient Banach algebra of interpolation data, its generalized von Neumann inequality, and the fact that its symmetric part consists precisely of the constant vectors. For nodes in a polydisc, we introduce minimal effective coordinate tuples and identify the admissible permutations with the automorphisms of a lower-dimensional polydisc that preserve the projected node set. This yields a direct-product description of the automorphism group, with one factor equal to the automorphism group of the disc and the other finite. We also give the resulting descriptions for nodes in the disc and the bidisc.

papers.title: From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Many problems in signal processing, machine learning, and neuroimaging provide several jointly observed measurements of one process, each mixing a component common to all of them with a component private to itself, and require the common component to be recovered without supervision. This problem has been studied in several communities, largely independently. Statisticians proposed canonical correlation analysis (CCA), introduced by Hotelling in 1936. Information theorists proposed two notions of common information, due to G\'acs and K\"orner and to Wyner. Engineers developed subspace methods for sensor arrays and multiuser communications to design multiview receivers. This tutorial presents the main results and tools each community developed for this problem in a single exposition, and explains the connections that emerge where they meet, distinguishing exact equivalences from special cases and analogies. We develop the information-theoretic foundation from first principles. We then introduce CCA and its extension to several views, followed by the engineering thread from blind multiuser detection to CCA as a blind receiver. Next, we turn to nonlinear CCA, covering kernel, deep, and probabilistic formulations, the conditions under which the common factor is identifiable, and connections to self-supervised learning. We conclude with a discussion of further extensions and open directions. The exposition is self-contained, so that readers from each of these communities can follow the parts developed by the others.

papers.title: Calibrations close to $\mathrm{G}_2$-twistor space
papers.abstract: We study natural structures of the kind of $\mathrm{G}_2$ existing on the unit tangent sphere bundle $SM \rightarrow M$ of any oriented Riemannian 4-manifold $M$. Based on the Harvey-Morgan classification of degree 3 calibrations on $\mathbb{R}^7$, we identity those which can be found on $SM$. We also study the Laplacian of the Sasaki metric on 3-forms.

papers.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
papers.abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).

papers.title: Diffusion Sensitivity Geometry and Strong Duality for Optimal Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs
papers.abstract: Existing approaches to differential privacy in diffusion models rely on loose sensitivity bounds and isotropic Gaussian noise, leading to unnecessary estimation error. We develop a framework for the optimal privacy-utility tradeoff of ideal diffusion denoisers, replacing conservative bounds with exact sensitivity characterizations and provably optimal noise calibration. First, we show that worst-case sensitivity over datasets of arbitrary size can be characterized exactly using only two records. For a data domain of size $m$, this reduces the analysis to at most $m(m-1)$ constraints, regardless of dataset size. Our characterization can be arbitrarily tighter than conventional diameter-based sensitivity bounds, revealing potentially unbounded improvements in noise calibration. Second, we obtain exact privacy guarantees for R\'enyi, approximate, and Gaussian differential privacy, as well as mutual-information privacy for binary records, avoiding the looseness of previous generic privacy conversions. Finally, we show that the minimum achievable weighted mean-squared error can be computed through a semidefinite program and prove strong duality, providing certificates of global optimality.

papers.title: Dirichlet eigenvalue asymptotics on conformally compact Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract:
We study the first Dirichlet eigenvalues of large geodesic balls and fixed-width boundary layers on conformally compact Einstein manifolds of dimension $n+1.$ For large balls, we determine the exponential rate of convergence when the spectral bottom is less than $\frac{n^2}{4},$ i.e. the bottom of the continuous spectrum. When it equals the bottom of the continuous spectrum, the second coefficient has two possible values, according to whether the continued resolvent is regular or has a pole there. We also give examples with negative Yamabe conformal infinity realizing both threshold alternatives and construct metrics with a Ricci lower bound that have other second coefficients.
  Under nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity, we also find the exact second coefficient for the nonlinear $p$-Laplacian on large balls.
  For layers defined by a geodesic boundary defining function, we compute the first correction and show that its sign characterizes nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity.

papers.title: Optimal R\'enyi and Logarithmic Additive Functional Entropy Estimation
papers.abstract:
We characterize the minimax sample complexity of estimating R\'enyi entropy from independent samples on an alphabet of size at most $k$, when the known order $\alpha>1$ may vary with $k$. For every fixed additive accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and success probability $2/3$, we prove matching bounds with constants independent of $k$ and $\alpha$. For $1<\alpha<\log k$, the rate is $\Theta_\varepsilon(\alpha k^{1-1/\alpha}X_\alpha(k,\varepsilon))$, where a monotone scalar inequality defines $X_\alpha$ at noninteger orders. The bounds remain uniform as the order approaches one or an integer, or grows with the alphabet. Integer orders below $\log k$ have rate $\Theta_\varepsilon(\alpha k^{1-1/\alpha})$; orders at least $\log k$ and min-entropy have rate $\Theta_\varepsilon(k\log k)$.
  We extend the analysis to logarithms of positive additive functionals. For every fixed continuous $f$ satisfying $f(0)=0$, $f(x)>0$ for $x>0$, and $f(x)\sim ax^r$ at zero, with $a>0$ and $r>1$, estimating $-\beta^{-1}\log\sum_i f(p_i)$ at fixed accuracy, for fixed $\beta>0$, has sample complexity $\Theta(k^{1-1/r})$ for integer $r$ and $\Theta(k/\log k)$ otherwise. A replication reduction preserves the sampling experiment and transfers the rates for powers. Smooth flat functions show that regularity alone does not determine the complexity.
  The upper bound combines polynomial approximation, Gamma count statistics, and an independent pilot, with a global affine correction near order one. The lower bound uses interpolation to construct positive mean-one priors and controls their distinguishability and entropy separation after normalization. Exact count-variance identities and weighted approximation duality connect the two arguments.

papers.title: Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion
papers.abstract: We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.

papers.title: On Finite Groups with Element Order Set of Width 3
papers.authors: Eric Min, Chloe So, Yong Yang, Eddy Zhang, Mengtian Zhang, Cody Zhou
papers.abstract: We study finite groups in which every element order is divisible by at most three distinct primes. We determine the possible nonabelian composition factors, prove that a nonabelian simple group with this property has at most $15$ prime divisors in its order, and deduce that $\rho(G)\leq192$ for every finite group $G$ with $\alpha(G)\leq3$.

papers.title: A Jump-Modified Wasserstein Gradient Flow for Maximum Mean Discrepancy with Energy Kernels
papers.authors: Ansh Desai, Jason Liu, Srujan Roplekar, Matthew Rosenzweig
papers.abstract: We study a jump-modified Wasserstein gradient flow of the squared maximum mean discrepancy generated by the energy kernels $K(z)=-|z|^q$, $0<q<2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$ as well as the one-dimensional range $1\le q<2$. Under subcritical density and finite-moment assumptions, we prove global well-posedness. The added jumps transfer mass toward smaller values of the first variation and dissipate the same MMD energy as the transport term. Under our hypotheses on the target and jump rates, every Borel probability measure with finite MMD energy and zero jump dissipation is equal to the target. Combining this rigidity with compactness and a second-moment identity yields convergence to the target from finite-second-moment data, without additional uniform-in-time density or moment assumptions. We also construct a global collision-free particle process whose energy is nonincreasing along each path. A quantitative mean-field estimate applies to general initial empirical approximations, including deterministic configurations; propagation of chaos for exchangeable data and long-time target approximation follow as consequences.

papers.title: Affine $G$-multibiquandle modules for colored links I: representability of coloring functors and color-profile polynomials
papers.abstract:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $G$ be an abelian group, and fix $u\in R[G]^\times$. For each component-labeled oriented link diagram $(D,\sigma)$, we construct a finitely presented $R[G]$-module $M_u(D,\sigma;R[G])$ with a universal affine coloring $U_{D,\sigma}$. Every affine coloring with values in an $R[G]$-module factors uniquely through $U_{D,\sigma}$ by a module homomorphism. Thus the module represents the affine coloring functor. Each specified colored Reidemeister move induces a unique module isomorphism compatible with coloring transport, and the module isomorphism class is a colored-link invariant. The representing modules and universal colorings commute with arbitrary scalar extension, without a flatness assumption. For classical links, simultaneous rescaling of the component labels removes the common deformation unit.
  For any multibiquandle, associated-biquandle colorings decompose into fibers indexed by component labelings. For finite targets and palettes, we define a color-profile polynomial recording the joint distribution of fiber sizes and numbers of palette labels used, and prove its invariance under oriented link isotopy. In the affine case, the representing modules determine these fibers, and their specialized dimensions determine the coloring counts over finite fields. The color-profile polynomial is not determined, in general, by the full unweighted distribution of coloring-fiber sizes. It therefore retains information beyond the associated-biquandle coloring count.

papers.title: A logarithmic regularity criterion for the axisymmetric Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: For axisymmetric solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb R^3$, the circulation $\Gamma=ru^\theta$ obeys a maximum principle, and the resulting a priori bound on $\Gamma$ is scale-invariant. Nonetheless, the global regularity problem remains completely open. The sharpest known regularity criteria in terms of the circulation are slightly subcritical, namely $|\Gamma|\lesssim(\log r^{-1})^{-k}$ near the symmetry axis; Lei and Zhang proved regularity for $k=2$, and Wei later lowered the exponent to $k=3/2$. In this note, we strengthen the criterion further to $k=5/4$. The argument follows the usual route of energy estimates for the quantities $\omega^r/r$ and $\omega^\theta/r$, but now with a sharper bound on the vortex stretching term in the equation for $\omega^r/r$, in which the loss is proportional only to the square root of the number of scales between the inner vortex core and the far field.

papers.title: On the Number of Iterations in a Kruskal-Type Process
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Kruskal counting procedure, this paper investigates a combinatorial elimination process defined on a deck consisting of $m$ copies of each value $1,2,\ldots,n$. Starting from an arbitrary arrangement of the $mn$ cards, the process repeatedly removes a number of consecutive cards equal to the value of the first remaining card. This generates a sequence of elimination steps whose length determines $T$, representing the total number of iterations required to exhaust the deck. The main objective of this paper is to analyze an upper bound $\sigma(m,n)$ for $T$, valid for every initial configuration of the deck, and to show that this bound is attained by a specific configuration.

papers.title: Isotropy sets of periodic geodesic flows on three dimensional manifolds
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Wadsley states that if all geodesics on a Riemannian manifold M are periodic, then they have a common period, and the geodesic flow induces an S^1-action on the unit tangent bundle. Moreover, a conjecture of Berger asserts that this action is free whenever M is simply connected. In this paper, we investigate the Berger conjecture in dimension three by studying the isotropy set of the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow. Using Morse theory for the energy functional on the free loop space of M, we establish two results in this direction. First, we show that all isotropy groups of the geodesic flow have odd order. Second, we prove that the geodesic flow either acts freely on the unit tangent bundle $T^1M$ or has at least two singular orbit types. This paper serves as preparation for the subsequent paper The Berger conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds, in which the conjecture is proved in dimension three.

papers.title: Zeros of quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We consider Dirichlet $L$-functions $L(s, \chi)$ where $\chi$ is a quadratic character to modulus $q$. We show that for $\chi$ even (resp. odd) $L(\sigma, \chi)\neq 0$ for all $\sigma >0$ provided that $q\leq 10^{9}$ (resp. $q\leq 10^{10})$. In particular, this result rules out Siegel--Landau zeros for such $L$-functions. Combined, these results improve on previous work by nearly four orders of magnitude. We also list some applications of this work.

papers.title: Encoding Trees: A Method for Producing a Variable-Length Prefix Code From Sets of Arbitrary Size
papers.abstract: In this work we formalize a new class of binary trees called encoding trees. We extend this structure in two ways, through labelling to create the class of labelled encoding trees, and pruning to create the class of pruned encoding trees. We discuss how these two extensions can be combined to create the the class of pruned labelled encoding trees. Using the supplementary results that we prove about these classes of trees, we construct a code that uses pruned labelled encoding trees to convert a string of symbols from a sequence of non-empty sets to a binary string. We prove that this code is a variable-length prefix code that can process any valid string of symbols from the given sequence of non-empty sets. Furthermore, we construct a code from the class of pruned labelled encoding trees that goes in the opposite direction, from binary strings to a string of symbols from a sequence of non-empty sets of arbitrary symbols. We prove that this code is also a variable-length prefix code that can process any binary string of any length, provided that the sequence of non-empty sets is sufficiently long. We provide an equation that establishes the minimum sequence length to encode any binary string of a given length, based on that length.

papers.title: Neural Vector Field Transformations: Learning the Flow of Autonomous Systems by Conjugation to Explicitly Integrable Reference Flows
papers.abstract: We represent the flow map of an autonomous ODE $\dot x=f(x)$ as a conjugate $\Phi_t=F_\theta^{-1}\circ\Psi_t\circ F_\theta$ of an explicitly integrable reference flow $\Psi_t$ by an invertible neural network $F_\theta$, the neural vector field transformation. The representation is an exact flow for every parameter value and inherits the phase portrait of the reference. A $C^1$ conjugacy preserves the eigenvalues of equilibria, the periods and Floquet multipliers of periodic orbits and the frequency-amplitude relation of centers, so these invariants must be learnable parameters of $\Psi$. We give parametrized reference flows with explicit integral curves, show that an action-angle reference is Hamiltonian only if its learnable frequency map is a gradient, and show that an orientation-preserving $F_\theta$ cannot reverse the rotation sense of the reference, so it must be fixed before training. The main contribution is a training recipe: a push-forward equation residual made relative to $|f|$ and sampled log-uniformly in $|x|$ around an equilibrium, with the anchors $F_\theta(0)=0$, $DF_\theta(0)=I$; a symplectic transformation with the gradient-form frequency map; and invariants initialized from the field or data. With it the full spectrum of a three- and a six-dimensional nonlinear sink is recovered (eigenvalue deviation $8.3\times10^{-3}$ and relative error 2.3%, three seeds each), and the action-angle variables of a four-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system with frequency maps and actions correct to a median of 0.09% and 0.22%, and an exactly symplectic flow. On a dispersive system a time-input network is eight times more accurate inside its horizon, and the data-only identification of the Van der Pol oscillator yields a conjugacy on the data region with the Floquet exponent 17% off; an oracle run with the true invariants frozen attributes this to the expressivity of $F_\theta$.

papers.title: Stability for the adjoint Finner inequality and improved lower bounds on the $k$-plane transform
papers.abstract: We establish stability properties of near-extremisers for the Loomis--Whitney inequality and its adjoint, presenting our results in the general framework of Finner. In particular, we show that a function nearly achieves equality in the adjoint Finner inequality if and only if it is near to being an indicator function of a cartesian product. As an application, we obtain new lower bounds for the classical $k$-plane transform on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, modestly improving those obtained recently by Tao and the first author. We also present an alternative approach to such improvements based on stability in the setting of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality and the theory of fusion frames. We conclude with an interpretation of our $k$-plane transform estimates as adjoint forms of the continuous Brascamp--Lieb inequalities.

papers.title: Every tournament of dichromatic number $10 k^2$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood has dichromatic number more than $k$
papers.abstract: The dichromatic number of a tournament is the minimum number of colors needed to color the vertices so that no directed cycle is monochromatic.
