Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour (2025) asked whether every tournament with dichromatic number $2k$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number at least $k$. We answer their question negatively by finding an example with dichromatic number $\Omega(k^2)$. Furthermore, this quadratic bound is tight up to a constant factor; we show that for every integer $k \geq 1$, every tournament of dichromatic number $\Omega(k^2)$ contains a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number more than $k$. This improves the previous best bound $\mathcal{O}(k^2\log k)$ due to Colinot and Newman (2026). To show this, we prove that every tournament of fractional dichromatic number $c$ has a dominating set of size at most $5c-1$. The proof uses Brouwer's fixed point theorem.

papers.title: Non-trivial intersecting families for direct products
papers.authors: Jian Wang, Biao Wu, Huajun Zhang
papers.abstract: A family of sets is intersecting if any two of its sets intersect, and non-trivial intersecting if there is not any element which appears in every set of the family. The study of intersection problems (or Erd\H{o}s-Ko-Rado problems) on families of sets is one of the most important topics in extremal combinatorics. A natural extension of the Erd\H{o}s-Ko-Rado problem in direct products setting was introduced by Frankl, and developed by Alon and Katona et al. In 2018, Kwan, Sudakov and Vieira [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. A 156 (2018), 44--60] determine the maximum size of a non-trivial intersecting direct product family under the assumption that the sizes of all parts are sufficiently large relative to the set sizes in all parts. Meanwhile, they raised the question of whether this result holds for the size of each part which depends only on its corresponding set size, and the question of characterizing the extremal families. In the present paper, we answere these two questions. Furthermore, the bounds on the size of each part in our result are best possible.1

papers.title: Proofs of Li, Wang and Guo's conjectures on (signless) Laplacian spectral radius
papers.authors: Hongzhang Chen, Jianxi Li, Xiaoyun Lv
papers.abstract: Let $\mu(G)$ and $q(G)$ be the Laplacian and signless Laplacian spectral radii of a graph $G$. Li, Wang and Guo (2026) conjectured that, if $H$ with $|V(H)|\geq 1$ is an induced subgraph of a graph $G$, then $\mu(G)\le\max\limits_{v\in V(H)}\mu(H_v^t)$ and $q(G)\le\max\limits_{v\in V(H)}q(H_v^t)$, where $t=e(G)-e(H)$ and $H_v^t$ is the graph obtained from $H$ by adding $t$ pendant edges to $v\in V(H)$. We prove this conjecture by establishing a spectral comparison theorem for a broader family of positive semidefinite graph matrices which includes the Laplacian and signless Laplacian matrices. We also characterize all equality cases for the prescribed subgraph $H$ with $e(H)\geq 1$ and $t\geq 1$.

papers.title: Ramified convolution and monodromy bases for symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras
papers.abstract: We realize the positive enveloping algebra of a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra by convolution on a ramified preprojective species over $\mathbb{C}((t))$. The coefficients are alternating traces of tame monodromy on representation flag varieties. We prove the relative Serre relations modulo classes induced from proper finite extensions. Monodromy evaluations at compatible generic points of the central reductions yield an integral basis respecting the top and socle crystals. The basis is unchanged by scaling the symmetrizer, induces bases of integrable representation lattices, and agrees with Lusztig's semicanonical basis when the Cartan matrix is symmetric. We prove the acyclic convolution conjecture of Gei\ss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer for all symmetrizable Cartan matrices and all positive integral symmetrizers. Finally, we give a counterexample to the Support Conjecture of Gei\ss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer and compute a ramified lift for which monodromy restores the Serre relation.

papers.title: Free energy and fluctuations of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models and generalized Hopfield models
papers.abstract: We consider the free energy of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models in the high temperature regime, with one spin normalized and the other either normalized or i.i.d. We derive a unified formula for the limiting free energy in both settings. We also prove that the fluctuations of the free energy converge to a Gaussian distribution under mild assumptions. The proof is based on a bipartite multigraph expansion, which also gives free energy results for generalized Hopfield models and log likelihood ratio of spiked rectangular models.

papers.title: General Criterion for a Poset to Admit a Partition Into $\omega$-Chains
papers.abstract: Given a poset $P$ with no maximal element the question naturally arises of when $P$ can be partitioned into $\omega$-chains. In this paper we give general criterion for when this can be done. We show that in the case when a poset with no maximal element is countable or a well-founded forest, then it can always be partitioned into $\omega$-chains. We then introduce the lifting property for posets with no maximal element and show that a poset can be partitioned into $\omega$-chains if and only if it has the lifting property.

papers.title: Time-periodic solutions of an SIS epidemic model
papers.authors: Fang Li, Pengfei Song, Kexin Zhang, Maolin Zhou
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of strictly positive, nonstationary time-periodic solutions for the spatially heterogeneous SIS epidemic model with standard incidence. On a bounded interval with Neumann boundary conditions, we construct smooth, time-independent transmission and recovery rates satisfying \(\beta(x)>\gamma(x)>0\), together with diffusion coefficients \(d_I>d_S>0\), such that periodic solutions coexist with the unique endemic equilibrium for every prescribed positive total population. Thus, pointwise dominance of transmission over recovery does not ensure convergence to equilibrium. Our approach combines an inverse construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium with a coefficient path that preserves both the equilibrium and the pointwise inequalities. A change in the number of unstable eigenvalues along this path yields small-amplitude periodic solutions through a center-manifold reduction and a generalized Hopf bifurcation argument. The proof uses an AI-assisted construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium under the pointwise condition $\beta>\gamma>0$.

papers.title: Pontryagin-Thom, $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere, and principal quadratic divisors
papers.abstract: Segal computed $\pi_0$ of the equivariant sphere spectrum as the Burnside ring by a Pontryagin-Thom construction, transversality, and marks. We carry out the same argument in the motivic setting over a field $k$: the Burnside ring is replaced by the Grothendieck ring $A^u(\Gamma_k)$ of finite \'etale $k$-schemes decorated with a unit, the marks by the Dress map $d(L,u)=\mathrm{tr}_{L/k}\langle u\rangle$ into $\mathrm{GW}(k)$, and a Pontryagin-Thom map $A^u(\Gamma_k)\to\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)$ is shown to be surjective with kernel $\ker(d)$. This gives $\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)\cong\mathrm{GW}(k)$ for infinite perfect fields of characteristic $\ne 2$ without Morel's computation. We then identify $\ker(d)$, by a reciprocity law on $\mathbb{P}^1$, as the group of principal quadratic divisors of rational functions, so that $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere is the unit-decorated Burnside ring of $\Gamma_k$ modulo principal quadratic divisors. The transversality step is proved by an elementary "re-topping" argument.

papers.title: Construction of Galois modules describing ideal class groups and applications to Iwasawa theory
papers.abstract: For a finite Galois extension of number fields, the ideal class groups of intermediate fields do not behave well under taking Galois coinvariants in general. In this paper, we construct a Galois module whose Galois coinvariants explicitly describe the ideal class groups of the intermediate fields. As an application, we demonstrate how this construction naturally yields some results in classical Iwasawa theory.

papers.title: Inviscid Limit Problem for Radially Symmetric Stationary States of Viscous and Heat-Conductive Ideal Gas
papers.abstract: We study the zero-viscosity limit of radially symmetric stationary solutions for the inflow and outflow problems for a viscous and heat-conductive polytropic ideal gas in the exterior of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \geq 3$), under prescribed boundary and far-field conditions. The far-field velocity is assumed to be zero, and the solutions are considered in a sufficiently small neighborhood of the far-field state. In the zero-viscosity limit, the viscous terms disappear from the momentum equation, while the heat-conduction term remains in the energy equation. For the outflow problem, we prove that the viscous stationary solution converges uniformly to the corresponding stationary solution of the heat-conductive inviscid system, with convergence rate $O(\mu)$. For the inflow problem, a boundary layer appears near the inner boundary. We show that the viscous stationary solution is uniformly approximated by the superposition of the limiting stationary solution and a boundary-layer profile. Here, the boundary layer appears only for the density and velocity, whereas no boundary-layer appears for the temperature. Moreover, for any $\alpha \in (0,1)$, the approximation error is of order $O(\mu^\alpha)$.

papers.title: Widom asymptotics for spatial compressions of Schr\"odinger spectral projections
papers.abstract: We establish a Widom trace formula for spatial compressions of exact spectral projections of semiclassical Schr\"odinger operators. The potential is smooth near a compact classically allowed region, and the observation domain lies strictly inside that region. For every continuous spectral function with positive power decay at both endpoints, we obtain a trace formula at scale $h^{1-n}\log h^{-1}$ whose coefficient separates into a boundary integral and a universal spectral functional. This yields the exact von Neumann and R\'enyi entanglement asymptotics for every fixed positive order, and proves their universal ratios to the particle-number variance. The proof combines commutator estimates in every fixed positive Schatten class with a local trace formula obtained from a boundary-adapted normal form and a Hardy model. In dimensions $n\ge2$, a positive partition and the known variance asymptotic control the grazing contribution; in one dimension all boundary Fermi points are transverse. A harmonic-oscillator counterexample shows that continuity and weighted integrability alone are insufficient for the trace formula.

papers.title: Refined Cram\'er-type moderate deviations by Stein's method under dependence
papers.authors: Hui-Lin Liu, Song-Hao Liu, Dawei Lu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish refined Cram\'er-type moderate deviations for dependent random variables at any fixed order $m\geq3$. Combining higher-order Stein identities with exponential tilting, we obtain cumulant-corrected tail approximations with explicit error bounds for boundedly supported kernels. Our main application gives a fourth-order expansion under bounded local dependence, reaching an $O(n^{3/10})$ deviation range under standard normalization with fixed dependence parameters. It improves on previous work in both deviation range and applicability, and also covers bounded $m$-dependent sequences without an independent-base representation. Further applications to the generalized combinatorial central limit theorem and the Curie-Weiss model also extend some earlier results under permutation and mean-field dependence.

papers.title: Isolated Singularities of k-Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We classify isolated singularities of nonpositive, $k$-admissible classical solutions to $k$-Hessian equations without radial symmetry assumptions. For $1\le k<n/2$, we consider $F_k[u]=(-u)^p$ with $1<p\le nk/(n-2k)$. Below the Serrin exponent, we obtain fundamental-solution asymptotics and characterize removability by the vanishing of the leading coefficient. At the Serrin exponent, we determine the exact logarithmic correction and its universal coefficient for every nonremovable singularity. In the critical dimension $k=n/2$, we establish logarithmic asymptotics and a removability criterion for $F_k[u]=f(x,u,\nabla u)$ with continuous sources satisfying $0\le f(x,s,\xi)\le C|\xi|^\ell e^{-\alpha s}$, where $\alpha>0$ and $0\le\ell<n$. The proofs combine Hessian-measure compactness, Wolff-potential estimates, a global B\^ocher theorem, and a bounded-variation analysis of spherical extrema.

papers.title: Pappus configurations in the Hall plane
papers.authors: Stefano Lia, John Sheekey, Geertrui Van de Voorde
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate Pappus configurations in the finite affine Hall plane. In particular, we show that for any two lines $\ell_1,\ell_2$ and for any triple of points on $\ell_1$ there is a triple of points on $\ell_2$ that are contained in a Pappus configuration, thus improving on the results of [F. Lazebnik and L. Leshock. On Pappus configurations in Hall planes. Des. Codes Cryptogr. 90 (2022), 1203--1219.].

papers.title: Rigidity of Pseudoconvex Neighborhoods and Ohsawa--Takegoshi Extension
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a holomorphic section of a holomorphic submersion with one-dimensional fibers over a connected compact complex manifold. Assuming that its normal bundle is unitary flat, we prove that $Y$ admits a fundamental system of locally pseudoconvex neighborhoods if and only if it admits a holomorphic tubular neighborhood. The proof uses the sharp Ohsawa--Takegoshi extension theorem. As an application, we rule out such neighborhood systems in Ueda's example of class $(\gamma)$.

papers.title: Optimal Dividends and Proactive Capital Injection over a Finite Horizon
papers.authors: Ran Xu, Zuo Quan Xu, Xueying Zhang
papers.abstract: We study a finite-horizon dividend and capital-injection problem for a Brownian surplus process with time-varying financing costs. Under a classical passive-injection policy, capital is supplied only at the solvency boundary. Anticipated increases in financing costs may instead make it optimal to inject capital while reserves remain strictly positive. We characterize this proactive financing mechanism through an auxiliary Dynkin game for the marginal value of liquidity. The game identifies an endogenous lower financing boundary and an upper dividend boundary, and yields restrictions on intervention timing and comparative statics with respect to the financing-cost path. Under a regular intervention-band condition, we recover the control value by spatial integration of the game value and verify that the optimal policy is two-sided reflection between the two boundaries. We establish this condition for a canonical class with decreasing marginal dividend rewards, increasing marginal financing costs, and a compatible piecewise affine terminal marginal value. Strictly decreasing financing costs eliminate positive-reserve financing contact and reduce the marginal game to a one-player stopping problem. Numerical examples illustrate the optimal policies and the effects of anticipated financing conditions on shareholder value and intervention thresholds.

papers.title: Mixed sums of infinite multiple zeta-star values with restricted indices
papers.abstract: We study arithmetic sums of infinite multiple zeta-star values subject to upper or lower bounds on their indices. Let $\eta(\mathcal D_q)$ be the image, under the zeta-star correspondence, of the admissible infinite index sequences with all indices at most $q$, and let $\overline{\eta(\mathcal T_p)}$ be the closure of the image of the sequences with all indices at least $p$. We prove that $\eta(\mathcal D_q)+\overline{\eta(\mathcal T_p)}$ is an interval exactly when $p\leq q$; in that case it is $[\zeta^\star(\{q\}^{\infty})+1,\infty)$. We also show that sums of two upper-bounded sets are half-lines, even with different bounds, whereas sums of two lower-bounded sets are never intervals. The proofs combine a uniform product estimate with natural gap constructions. Lateral thickness handles the diagonal case $p=q\geq3$, while a non-strict local bridge--gap criterion treats $p=q=2$ directly. Compact truncations and explicit omitted intervals yield the remaining assertions.

papers.title: Conditional Reflected Backward Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new type of reflected backward stochastic differential equations (reflected BSDEs), referred to as conditional reflected BSDEs, in which the conditional expectation of the Y-component of the solution with respect to a given sub-{\sigma}-algebra appears in both the generator and the obstacle. Under a Lipschitz condition on the loss function with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution for both the case of Lipschitz generator and the case of quadratic generator, bounded terminal value and bounded loss function. When the generator has quadratic growth and the terminal value and loss function are unbounded, we establish the uniqueness with the help of {\theta}-method. Finally, a penalization approximation scheme holds under an additional monotonicity structure imposed on the generator and the loss function, without any restriction on the Lipschitz constants of the loss function.

papers.title: Normal approximation, moderate and large deviations for the elephant random walk with stops and random step sizes
papers.abstract: We study the elephant random walk with stops and independent positive random step sizes. Building on fixed-movement estimates, we obtain quantitative normal approximations for an empirically normalized statistic by controlling its random denominator and the independent movement clock. A permutation comparison preserves the diffusive Kolmogorov rate, while variance matching permits third-order Zolotarev estimates. We also derive self-normalized Cram\'er-type moderate deviations. For regularly varying step-size tails, we obtain uniform precise large deviations and establish the necessity of the diffusive and critical threshold orders. Further applications of the clock representation yield large deviation principles for Weibull-type and light-tailed step sizes, and a precise light-tailed expansion in the balanced case.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of certain quasi-linear elliptic inequalities II
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of isolated singularities for quasilinear elliptic equations of $p$-Laplacian type. We focus on the $p$-Laplace equation with the critical Serrin exponent $n(p-1)/(n-p)$ and the $n$-Laplace equation with critical exponential growth. We prove that any positive solution either admits a $C^{1,\alpha}$ extension to the origin or exhibits a precise singular asymptotic behavior. These results provide a complement to our previous study on $p$-Laplacian type inequalities.

papers.title: On a conjecture concerning two-stack sortable permutations
papers.authors: Yongzhou Wen, Sherry H. F. Yan
papers.abstract: The two-stack sortable permutations of length $n$ are known to be equinumerous with permutations of length $n$ avoiding the dashed patterns $3\text{-}1\text{-}4\text{-}2$ and $2\text{-}41\text{-}3$. In this paper, we confirm an intriguing conjecture posed by Claesson, Kitaev, and Steingr\'imsson, which asserts that the quadruple $(\comp,\asc,\ldr,\rmax)$ is equidistributed on these two permutation classes. Here $\comp$ and $\asc$ count the number of components and ascents, respectively, $\ldr$ denotes the length of the initial decreasing run, and $\rmax$ denotes the number of right-to-left maxima. This is accomplished by constructing bijections between two-stack sortable permutations and $\beta(1,0)$-trees.

papers.title: New matrix-weighted norm inequalities and extrapolation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a new type of matrix-weighted theory and show the corresponding Rubio de Francia extrapolation theorems by means of noncommutative maximal inequalities. We introduce a new matrix $A_p$ condition following Volberg's geometric formulation, and characterize it via a noncommutative Hardy--Littlewood maximal inequality. We then establish a noncommutative analogue of Rubio de Francia's abstract extrapolation theorem for trace-finite von Neumann algebras. The argument extends to $L_\infty(\mathbb R)\bar\otimes M_d(\mathbb C)$ through pointwise matrix operations. This yields the desired extrapolation results for individual operators and maximal families, with applications to matrix-weighted boundedness of Calder\'on--Zygmund operators.

papers.title: Integer Flows on Cyclic Covers of Graphs
papers.authors: Rong Luo, Yuying Ma, D. Christopher Stephens, Dong Ye
papers.abstract: Graph covers preserve the local structure of a graph while allowing its global structure to change substantially. In this paper, we study how such changes in cyclic covers affect nowhere-zero flow properties. For a fixed integer $\ell \ge 2$, we show that for every bridgeless graph $G$, there exists an $\ell$-fold cyclic cover of $G$ that admits a nowhere-zero $3$-flow if $\ell$ is even and a nowhere-zero $4$-flow if $\ell$ is odd. These bounds are best possible in general. For odd $\ell$, we further investigate which bridgeless graphs admit an $\ell$-fold cyclic cover with a nowhere-zero $3$-flow.

papers.title: $G$-crossed braided tensor categories of twisted modules
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. We prove Huang's conjecture that the categories of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, for $g\in G$, form a $G$-crossed braided fusion category. This category is faithfully $G$-graded, with tensor products representing the complete twisted intertwining operators of Du-Huang, the canonical pullback $G$-action, and crossed braiding. In particular, the associativity, coherence and rigidity required by the conjecture all hold.

papers.title: Small covers and the Four Color Theorem
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial proof that every simple convex $3$-polytope admits a small cover without using the Four Color Theorem. We also prove that the assertion that every simple plane triangulation admits a mod~$2$ characteristic function with at most five values is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem.

papers.title: On evaluation of polynomial coefficients
papers.abstract:
The evaluation of polynomial coefficients is an old mathematical problem, which is still actively investigated by many authors. The paper strengthens the known results in this direction and provides a complete solution for the case when the space $P_n$ of polynomials is equipped with Hilbert's norm.
  Our approach involves the intrinsic features of univalent functions and of Teichmuller spaces.

papers.title: Partially Observed McKean--Vlasov Control with Vanishing Observation Intensities
papers.abstract: We study partially observed McKean--Vlasov jump-diffusions with controlled counting intensities that may vanish and depend on the unconditional physical state distribution. A deterministic upper bound on the likelihood supports one-sided state--likelihood variations, a smooth-test-function expansion of the physical state marginal, and a necessary maximum principle without inverse intensity or likelihood terms. We also establish a one-sided total-variation derivative of the physical probability on the fixed noise space, including a nonnegative singular component on baseline-null histories. A quadratic example shows, within a specified policy family and under explicit conditions, that positive variance feedback raises the first-order activation fee threshold while negative feedback lowers it.

papers.title: From Linear Exact Repair to Mixed-Alphabet Codes: The Bandwidth-Subpacketization Tradeoff of MDS Array Codes
papers.authors: Zihao Zhang, Guodong Li, Sihuang Hu
papers.abstract:
MDS array codes achieve optimal storage efficiency in distributed storage systems, but their repair bandwidth depends critically on the sub-packetization level. While the theoretically optimal repair bandwidth (i.e., cut-set bound) of a high-rate exact-repair MDS array code is attainable with sufficiently large sub-packetization, the fundamental limits for fixed sub-packetization remain poorly understood. We study this problem for centralized linear exact repair of $h$ failures from $d$ helper nodes over a fixed finite field.
  We show that the rank profile of any linear repair scheme is constrained by two auxiliary mixed-alphabet codes. The first code is formed from the kernels of the helper projections and exists for all repair degrees; the second is formed from their row spaces and applies in the full-helper regime when $d\ge r$. These codes have complementary alphabet profiles, and their size and minimum-distance requirements are forced solely by the MDS property and repair correctness. This gives a unified route from classical coding-theoretic upper bounds to repair-bandwidth lower bounds. As a consequence, we obtain several explicit lower bounds via Singleton, Hamming, Plotkin, and Griesmer arguments, including known bounds as corollaries. We further formulate a Delsarte-type support-enumerator LP for mixed-alphabet codes and give an exact type-compressed implementation. For fixed sub-packetization \(\ell\), this yields a polynomial-time procedure for evaluating the resulting finite-parameter lower bound.

papers.title: ORSMT: Unleashing the Potential of Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Semantic Verification and Repair in LLM-Based Optimization
papers.authors: Rui Zhang, Chenyu Zhou, Jianghao Lin, Yaoxin Wu, Dongdong Ge, Wen Song
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly automate optimization modeling from natural language problems, producing written mathematics, solver code and a returned report. Verifying one optimization problem across these artifacts requires semantic comparison: unequal models can attain the same objective, equivalent models can use different auxiliary variables, and mutually consistent artifacts can omit the same source requirement. ORSMT provides a typed semantic interface and exact SMT relation queries. It aligns observable decisions, projects auxiliary variables, proves or refutes feasible region and objective relations, localizes refutations to implicated rows or domains and links source texts when available. It then reconstructs one artifact from another, and each adopted candidate passes the required relation checks. Across 3,034 problems and six generator sizes, ORSMT improves the model-code match rate in all 72 benchmark and generator combinations before selection. Protected selection raises the aggregate rate from 43.2% to 88.2% and the share that are both correct and matched from 25.2% to 40.2%. On the 1,905 refuted outputs, certified voting under the shared fallback makes 50.9% of outputs correct and matched, compared with 44.8% for ReLoop and 49.4% for Opt-Verifier. A separate one-round source revision followed by exact reconstruction restores a model-code match for 84.4% of the refuted pairs.

papers.title: A Link-Based Algorithm for Stochastic User Equilibrium with Bounded Choice and Local Detour Threshold
papers.abstract: This study develops a novel solution method for stochastic user equilibrium (SUE) under the bounded choice model with local detour threshold (BCM-LDT SUE; Rasmussen et al., 2024), which restricts the choice set in line with observed route choice behavior. The model assigns zero probability to paths whose total cost exceeds a bound or whose local detour exceeds a threshold; thus, the path choice set varies with link costs. The proposed algorithm updates link flows while implicitly enumerating the path choice set via a depth-first search (DFS) pruned with the BCM-LDT bounds. This distinguishes it from the original algorithm, which updates path flows, and enables quasi-Newton-type acceleration. Since paths are never stored, the method can handle choice sets totaling on the order of $10^7$ paths. On a personal computer, it reached equilibrium in a few to about fifteen minutes, not only for the Anaheim network under the original settings but also for larger networks such as Winnipeg and Barcelona.

papers.title: Normal approximation and self-normalized moderate deviations for the minimal random walk with random step sizes
papers.abstract: We study the minimal random walk with independent positive random step sizes. By separating the movement count from the centered step-size noise, we obtain normal approximations and self-normalized Cram\'er-type moderate deviations under finite-moment assumptions. For the noise, conditioning on the movement count yields Kolmogorov, Wasserstein and Zolotarev bounds. A polynomial moderate-deviation range holds when a recalled stop can lead to movement. At the boundary where this probability is zero, we obtain a logarithmic range and construct a bounded nonsymmetric example excluding a general polynomial range. For the full position, a weighted martingale representation gives limit laws in the different regimes, nonuniform normal approximations and moment-distance bounds without logarithmic losses. Variance concentration also yields self-normalized moderate deviations in the diffusive and critical regimes.

papers.title: A Shadow Sequence Technique for Last-Iterate Convergence Analysis of the Random Reshuffling Method: Relaxed Stepsize Conditions and Beyond
papers.authors: Hai Liu, Tiande Guo, Congying Han
papers.abstract: We prove two last-iterate convergence bounds of the random reshuffling (RR) method in the smooth general convex finite-sum optimization. In the proved results, the stepsize sequence $\{\eta_{k}\}_{k}$ of RR is an arbitrary positive non-increasing sequence with $\eta_{1}\lesssim 1/(\operatorname{polylog}(n)L)$, where $n$ is the number of components of the finite-sum objective and $L$ is the smoothness parameter. Specifically, a last-iterate convergence rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\Vert x_{1}^{1}-x_{*}\Vert^2}{n\sum_{k=1}^{K}\eta_{k}}+\sigma_{*}^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\eta_{k}^{2}}{\sum_{l=k}^{K}\eta_{l}}\right)$ of RR is proved, where $x_{*}$ is a solution of the optimization problem and $\sigma_{*}^{2}$ is the variance at the solution $x_{*}$. This rate is novel to the last-iterate of RR. Also, a last-iterate convergence rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\Vert x_{1}^{1}-x_{*}\Vert^2}{n\sum_{k=1}^{K}\eta_{k}}+n\sigma_{*}^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{\eta_{k}^{3}}{\sum_{l=k}^{K}\eta_{l}} \right)$ of RR is proved. A similar rate exists in the literature, but only under a restrictive stepsize condition $\eta\lesssim 1/(n L)$ and does not allow varying stepsizes. At the heart of our proof for the latter rate is an auxiliary sequence named the shadow sequence, which has the same epoch endpoints with the iterate sequence generated by RR. The shadow sequence can be regarded as an iterate sequence generated by performing an inexact RR on an auxiliary interpolated problem or performing a novel variant of random reshuffled SVRG on the original problem. The shadow sequence technique sheds light on deeper understanding of RR and may be useful in the analysis of other shuffling methods.

papers.title: Partial regularity of heat flow of fractional harmonic maps to spheres
papers.authors: Hengrong Du, Tao Huang, Armin Schikorra, Changyou Wang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notation of stationary heat flow of $s$-harmonic maps from $\R^m$ into the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{\ell-1}\hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^\ell$, for $0<s<1$, framed through the parabolic version of Caffarelli-Silvestre's extension. We prove that any stationary heat flow of $s$-harmonic maps is smooth away from a closed set of vanishing $(m+2-2s)$-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. This extends to the fractional settings the partial regularity theorem on the heat flow of harmonic maps into spheres by Chen-Li-Lin and Feldman.

papers.title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness
papers.abstract: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) has established itself as a widely used method for training deep neural networks. Despite its popularity, existing convergence guarantees for SAM-type methods require smoothness, a restrictive assumption. Generalized smoothness conditions have recently been proposed in the analysis of gradient methods but remain underexplored for SAM. To analyze the effect of SAM's perturbation under generalized smoothness, we use relative gradient distortion to quantify how the sharpness-aware direction departs from the original gradient. Under $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness, we show that this distortion can become unbounded near stationarity for SAM and at large gradients for its unnormalized variant (USAM), with examples where SAM cycles and USAM diverges. We then establish a necessary condition for uniform distortion control among perturbations along the gradient whose nonnegative multipliers depend only on its norm. Motivated by this condition, we propose Curvature-Scaled SAM (CS-SAM), which scales both the perturbation and the descent step by suitable curvature upper bounds, and prove that it uniformly bounds the distortion. Under both $(L_0,L_1)$- and $(H_0,H_1)$-smoothness, we establish deterministic $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ rates for the best squared gradient norm on nonconvex objectives, last-iterate $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ rates for the function gap on convex objectives with a minimizer, and linear convergence under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition. With zero perturbation, our guarantees recover the rates for gradient descent with $(L_0,L_1)$- or $(H_0,H_1)$-based step-sizes. Minibatch experiments on computer vision tasks demonstrate competitive performance for both variants, with the $(H_0,H_1)$ variant achieving the highest mean best-test accuracy in all four settings against tuned SAM and USAM with constant and cosine annealing schedules.

papers.title: The Local Dyadic Conjecture
papers.authors: Mahtab Alghasi, Bertrand Guenin, Levent Tun\c{c}el
papers.abstract: A rational with denominator a power of two is said to be dyadic. A long standing conjecture of Paul Seymour predicts that for an ideal clutter, the dual of the set covering problem always admits an optimal solution where all variables take dyadic values. We present a local version of this conjecture, and motivate it by proving an important special case.

papers.title: On the existence of independent inner functions
papers.authors: Xiangdi Fu, Kunyu Guo, Dilong Li, Yanqi Qiu
papers.abstract: The existence of independent inner functions is established: there exist inner functions $\varphi$ and $\psi$, both vanishing at the origin, such that $$ \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} \varphi^m(e^{i\theta}) \overline{\psi^n(e^{i\theta})}\,d\theta = 0, \qquad m,n \geq 1. $$ In fact, both $\varphi$ and $\psi$ can be chosen to be Blaschke products. The proof proceeds by an iterative construction, which suggests a general approach to produce inner functions with a desired joint distribution.

papers.title: Small deviations for integrators in terms of It\^{o}--Wiener expansions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate small deviations for a class of Gaussian processes, known as integrators. In general, such processes are non-Markovian and may even fail to be semimartingales. First, we investigate small deviations for the multi-dimensional Wiener process, focusing on the asymptotic behavior of the Fourier--Wiener transform of the associated hitting event. We analyze the Fourier--Wiener transform and the separate summands in its It\^{o}--Wiener expansion. Then, we establish the asymptotic limits of the associated multiple integrals with heat kernels. Finally, we obtain the small deviation asymptotic result for the integrator $\eta$ associated with the continuous linear operator.

papers.title: The Logarithmic A-Discriminant
papers.authors: Madeleine Goertz, Bernd Sturmfels, Simon Telen
papers.abstract: We extend the GKZ theory of discriminants to the setting of Euler integrals where both coefficients and exponents are variables. The integrand is the likelihood function of a toric model in algebraic statistics, whose number of critical points is the volume of the Newton polytope. Our logarithmic A-discriminant vanishes when two critical points come together. This discriminant is a hypersurface, parametrized by the logarithmic Horn uniformization. Hurwitz forms of toric varieties yield a degree formula, and a description of leading coefficients. We emphasize applications and computations.

papers.title: A New Modification of the Milstein Method and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.authors: Dmitriy F. Kuznetsov, Mikhail D. Kuznetsov
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modification of the Milstein method for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients.

papers.title: Temporal-Logical Stochastic Processes
papers.abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for Temporal-Logical Stochastic Processes (TLSP), in which temporal-logic specifications induce time-indexed stochastic observables capturing the robustness of temporal satisfaction. Building upon existing probabilistic interpretations of temporal-logic robustness, we systematically investigate the stochastic-process structure of these observables. We establish their measurability, shifted-filtration adaptedness, and sample-path regularity under suitable assumptions, and characterize the action of temporal operators on stochastic processes. We derive pathwise perturbation bounds and quantify the sensitivity of temporal satisfaction probabilities through the probability mass concentrated near the logical boundary. A topology on the observable-process space and a semantic pseudometric on temporal formulas are introduced to establish convergence of temporal-logical observables under perturbations of formula parameters and temporal intervals. We further characterize conditions ensuring weak convergence of observable-process distributions and convergence of temporal satisfaction probabilities. Finally, we establish a process-level large-deviation principle for temporal-logical observables, providing a variational characterization of rare temporal events through minimum-action trajectories. The resulting framework connects temporal-logic semantics with stochastic-process topology, stability, convergence, and rare-event asymptotics, providing a mathematical foundation for the analysis of temporally constrained stochastic systems.

papers.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
papers.authors: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck
papers.abstract:
We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field.
  Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture.
  We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

papers.title: A hybridization-derived interior penalty Nitsche method for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion
papers.abstract: We develop an interior penalty Nitsche finite element formulation for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion problems, which is derived from an interior-penalty stabilized Lagrange multiplier method. A distinctive feature of the derived method is that it simultaneously combines two popular stabilization strategies: (i) a boundary penalty mechanism similar to Nitsche's methods and (ii) an interior penalty mechanism as for Continuous Interior Penalty (CIP) methods. Furthermore, the normal component of the numerical flux is single-valued across the mesh skeleton and available in closed form. We establish the equivalence between the hybridized Lagrange multiplier formulation and its condensed Interior Penalty Nitsche (IPN) form, and we deliver the stability and convergence analysis of the latter. For sufficiently regular solutions, we establish energy-norm error estimates for the three symmetry variants. Under a piecewise elliptic regularity assumption on the adjoint problem, the $L^2$ estimate is optimal for the symmetric variant and exhibits a half-order loss for the incomplete and nonsymmetric variants; its constant may depend on the diffusion coefficients through the adjoint regularity constant. This single-valued numerical normal flux, available in closed form, provides a starting point for locally conservative $H(\mathrm{div})$-conforming flux reconstruction, left for future work. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Third and Fourth Moment Phenomena for Monochromatic Edges and Applications to Graph-Based Two-Sample Tests
papers.authors: Siva Athreya, Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya, Yogesh Dahiya, Karambir Das, Spandan Ghoshal, Sourish Maniyar, Elizabeth Sara Roy
papers.abstract: Given a graph sequence $\{G_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, denote by $T_n$ the number of monochromatic edges when the vertices of $G_n$ are independently colored red or blue with probabilities $p$ and $1-p$, respectively. We characterize the asymptotic normality of $T_n$, after centering and scaling to unit variance, in terms of subgraph (motif) counts and standardized moments. One of the highlights of our results is a {\it third moment phenomenon}: for every fixed $p\in(0,1)\backslash\{\frac12\}$, asymptotic normality holds if and only if the standardized third moment converges to zero. The more familiar {\it fourth moment condition}, which requires the standardized fourth moment to converge to $3$, gives an equivalent characterization except at the two exceptional probabilities $p=\frac{1\pm1/\sqrt3}{2}$. At these values, the standardized fourth moment converges to $3$ for every graph sequence with a diverging number of edges, even when Gaussian convergence fails. In contrast, in the balanced case $p=\frac12$, the fourth moment condition characterizes asymptotic normality, while the third moment condition is insufficient. These results identify three distinct regimes for moment characterizations of Gaussian convergence, determined by the coloring probability. We further show that the third moment condition remains sufficient in the sparse regime, where $p=p_n \to 0$. As an application, we derive the limiting null distribution of two-sample statistics based on undirected $K$-nearest-neighbor graphs in the Poissonized setting, identifying sharp growth conditions on $K$ for asymptotic normality.

papers.title: Bistable Dynamics and Complete Classifications of A Seasonal Competition Model Between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus
papers.authors: Lei Niu, Yi Wang, Xizhuang Xie, Bo Zheng
papers.abstract: The bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics are established for a competition model between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus subject to favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts, originally proposed by Zheng et al. (2025). More precisely, by employing Floquet theory, we prove that the unique positive periodic solution must be unstable. Consequently, bistable dynamics naturally emerge, which provides a rigorous theoretical validation of the numerical simulation results reported in the aforementioned work. Building on this, we further derive a full classification of the model's global dynamics. In addition, we carry out a comprehensive analysis of how seasonal switching mechanisms govern the competitive outcomes between these two mosquito species, thereby offering insights into their ecological coexistence and potential displacement.

papers.title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
papers.authors: Brayden Letwin, Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss
papers.abstract: Let $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det \Gamma \ge 1$ for all sublattices $\Gamma \subseteq \Lambda^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that $f$ is $\alpha$-strongly log-concave, where $\alpha = 2\pi/e$, and $X + \Lambda$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$. Moreover, we show that the existence of such a density $f$ characterizes the assumption on $\Gamma$ up to a constant. There are a few consequences of the above. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ \mu(\Lambda, K) = \max_{x \in \mathbb{R}^n} \min_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \|x-\lambda\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}{\pi}} \cdot \mathbb{E}_G\, \|G\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,I)$. This implies an $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. Second, we establish as a consequence an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem with an explicit constant.

papers.title: Day Convolution and Homotopy Groups on the Pointed Homotopy Category of CW Complexes
papers.abstract: We freely enrich the pointed homotopy category of CW complexes over abelian groups and equip the resulting functor category with the enriched Day convolution induced by the smash product. After identifying the convolution unit and recording the coherence maps, we compute the convolution of the homotopy-group functors. For integers $n,m\geq 2$ we construct a natural isomorphism $\pi_n\star\pi_m\cong\pi_{n+m}$ induced by the external smash product; equivalently, the external smash product is the universal natural pairing of homotopy groups. Under this identification, the symmetry interchanging the two factors acts on $\pi_{n+m}$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{nm}$.

papers.title: A sharp weighted commutator inequality for rank-one matrices
papers.abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be positive definite Hermitian, where $n\ge 2$, and define $\|X\|_A^2=\mathrm{tr}(AX^*X)$ for all $X\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$. We determine the smallest constant $C_A$ for which $$ \|XY-YX\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le C_A\|X\|_A^2\|Y\|_A^2 $$ holds for all rank-one $X,Y\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, where $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. The constant depends only on the two smallest eigenvalues of $A$ and is determined by a strictly monotone scalar equation. This answers the sharp-constant question for rank-one matrices formulated by Fang and Cheng. We also characterize all equality pairs.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotics for a free boundary touching a degenerate boundary: the perpetual Heston put
papers.authors: Takwon Kim, Junkee Jeon, Jehan Oh
papers.abstract: We study the exercise boundary of the perpetual American put in the Heston model near zero variance. There the pricing operator degenerates, and the exercise boundary, a free boundary in the stock--variance half-plane, touches the boundary of the half-plane. No Feller condition is imposed. The boundary is analytic at positive variance and extends as a regular $C^1$ curve tangent to the zero-variance axis. Its approach to the axis follows one of three laws, according to whether the Feller ratio $2\kappa\theta/\sigma^2$ is larger than, equal to, or smaller than one: a logarithmic correction to linear order, an exponential correction in the square root of the logarithm, or a fractional power. In the first two cases the leading coefficients are explicit and the tangent is not H\"older continuous at the axis. In the third case the exponent is selected by a possibly nonsymmetric stable operator on the axis, and the amplitude is finite and positive.

papers.title: Higher-order convex orders under free multiplicative convolution
papers.abstract: We prove that free multiplicative convolution with a probability measure on $[0,\infty)$ preserves the $k$-convex order for every integer $k\ge2$, assuming finite $(k-1)$st absolute moments for the two measures being compared and for the convolving measure. The compared measures may have arbitrary support in $\mathbb{R}$.

papers.title: Group Distributionally Robust Optimization over Decentralized Networks
papers.authors: Haomin Bai, Junyan Sun, Quan Cheng, Yuanyu Wan, Lijun Zhang
papers.abstract: We study group distributionally robust optimization (GDRO) over decentralized networks, where workers collaborate to learn robust models by minimizing the maximum local risk. Existing methods optimize only dual-regularized surrogates and establish guarantees for a globally averaged model that is not available to workers. In this paper, we directly optimize the original GDRO objective and establish guarantees for local models in semi-decentralized (SemiDec) and fully decentralized (Dec) settings. A key difficulty is that applying the primal-dual decomposition from centralized GDRO yields worker-dependent losses whose evaluation requires unavailable cross-worker information. To address this challenge, we develop a novel error decomposition that recasts decentralized GDRO as (i) a decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) problem and a prediction-with-expert-advice problem in SemiDec, and as (ii) two coupled D-OCO problems in Dec, with discrepancy terms capturing inconsistencies among local decisions. By isolating consensus errors in analysis, we develop modular frameworks that support different consensus routines. We then establish the \emph{first} per-worker convergence guarantees for optimizing the original GDRO objective over decentralized networks. Instantiations with accelerated gossip and Choco-gossip achieve an $O(\sqrt{(\log m)/T})$ convergence rate over $T$ update rounds, while experiments demonstrate improved worst-worker performance over baselines.

papers.title: Ramification and Finiteness of Equivariant Minimal Surfaces
papers.authors: Indranil Biswas, Satyajit Guin, Pradip Kumar
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. For $1\ \leq \ b\ \leq\ 2g-3$, we show that representations admitting an equivariant minimal map of total ramification at least $b$, for some marked complex structure, form a countable union of compact null sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $16g-16-2b$. For larger $b$, this locus is empty. Consequently, on a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure in $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$, every nonconstant equivariant minimal map is an immersion, for every marked complex structure. On the convex cocompact locus, a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure consists of representations admitting a finite nonempty set of marked equivariant minimal immersions.

papers.title: Scattering in spacetime cones for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.authors: Andrew Hassell, Qiuye Jia, Xiaoxu Wu
papers.abstract:
We consider the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$, with a class of `mixed' nonlinearities that admit soliton solutions. We are interested in the long-time behaviour of solutions with finite, but possibly large, mass and/or energy. By a spacetime cone, we mean an open set in $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}_{x,t}$ that is invariant under dilation $(x, t) \mapsto (\alpha x, \alpha t)$ for all $\alpha > 0$.
  Our main result is as follows: let $u(x, t)$ be the solution with initial condition in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Let $\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}$ be the mass and energy of $u$, and let $\eta = \eta(\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}) > 0$ be sufficiently small. Let $C_\epsilon$ be the complement of $N \geq 1$ of sufficiently thin spacetime cones $\{ (x, t) \mid |x-v_jt| \leq \epsilon t \}$, where $v_1, \dots, v_N$ are fixed velocities and $\epsilon$ is sufficiently small. If the $L^\infty$ norm of $u$ in $C_\epsilon$ is $\leq \eta$, we prove that $u$ scatters in $C_{2\epsilon} \subset C_\epsilon$.

papers.title: Mean curvature nonpositivity and rational connectedness
papers.abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Gauduchon manifold and let $E$ be a holomorphic vector bundle on $X$. We establish equivalent conditions for the existence of a Hermitian metric on $E$ with nonpositive mean curvature. For a non-uniruled compact K\"ahler manifold $X$ satisfying $\mu_{\omega_0,\max}(T_X)=0$ for some Gauduchon metric $\omega_0$, we show that the corresponding maximal destabilizing subsheaf of $T_X$ splits off holomorphically and is polystable of slope zero with respect to every Gauduchon metric. Its complement, if nonzero, is HN-negative with respect to every such metric. In particular, a compact K\"ahler manifold is not uniruled if and only if , for every Gauduchon metric $\omega$, its tangent bundle admits a Hermitian metric with nonpositive $\omega$-mean curvature. We also obtain an uniruledness criterion that includes the case where the maximal slope of $T_X$ is zero, and a Mumford-type characterization of rational connectedness. Under HN-nonnegativity of $T_X$ for one Gauduchon metric, rational connectedness, the vanishing of all holomorphic covariant tensors, and the condition $\kappa^+(X)=-\infty$ are equivalent.

papers.title: Nielsen coincidence theory for $(n,m)$-valued pairs
papers.abstract: We define a Nielsen coincidence number for pairs of maps $(f,g)$ where $f$ is $n$-valued and $g$ is $m$-valued. The classical definition of the Nielsen number does not work in this setting, but we propose a theory where coincidence classes are allowed to overlap. We invoke a notion of multiplicity of a coincidence point, which indicates to how many classes it can belong, and we show that our Nielsen number is a homotopy-invariant lower bound for the number of coincidence points with multiplicity. We show a computational result in terms of single-valued lift factors, and using this, a Wecken property for self-maps of the circle.

papers.title: A proof of Ward's conjecture on Griesmer codes
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be an $[n,k,d]_q$ Griesmer code, where $q=p^f$ with $p$ prime, and write $e=\nu_p(d)$. Ward conjectured that $C$ is $p^{\max\{0,e-f+1\}}$-divisible. In this paper, we prove this conjecture.

papers.title: Support periods of polynomials and support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes over Galois rings
papers.abstract:
Let \(A=\GR(p^e,r)\) have residue field \(\F_q\), and let \(\lambda\in A^\times\). We relate coefficient compression of monic divisors of \(X^N-\lambda\) to support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes. At a simple-root length, the support period of every nonconstant monic divisor is preserved at each coefficient precision and equals the order of the multiplicative stabilizer of its root set. For a cyclic Frobenius-orbit polynomial, the multiple equal-difference structure determines its support period, core degree, and least relative degree of an unramified extension over which all its basic-irreducible factors are binomials.
  Coordinate projections give every constacyclic code over a finite commutative ring a unique maximal interleaving into copies of one support-primitive code. At simple-root lengths over \(A\), the intrinsic period of a code is the greatest common divisor of the periods of its torsion codes. The decomposition yields distance and duality formulas and the arithmetic Singleton bound for free codes. At every length, a nonzero code over \(A\) has the same minimum Hamming distance as its highest torsion code, which gives a refined bound. At repeated-root lengths, identical torsion filtrations can occur with different intrinsic periods, while a class of nonzero codes obtained by substitution from simple-root generators retains the same core and minimum distance.
  Trace matrices recover the coefficients of basic-irreducible cores using unit pivots, and local Hensel corrections lift compressed factors directly. For \(X^n-1\) with \(p\nmid n\), lifting and output have quasi-linear bit cost in the compressed representation when the arithmetic data and residue factorizations are given.

papers.title: Time-Uniform Dependent Central Limit Theory
papers.abstract: We establish a near-optimal almost sure invariance principle for nonstationary time series under the functional dependence measure (FDM) framework. This result yields a universal time-uniform dependent central limit theorem, which serves as the basis for anytime-valid inference. In particular, we instantiate the theorem through asymptotic confidence sequences (AsympCSs), time-uniform counterparts of asymptotic confidence intervals obtained via central limit theorems, extending those originally proposed in Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) to time series with serial dependence. We further refine their definition because, as we show, it can admit AsympCSs that fail to achieve the desired asymptotic time-uniform coverage for a broad class of data-generating processes, including independent and identically distributed cases. We address this issue by adding a simple eventual-inclusion condition, which in turn permits more flexible variance estimation, particularly useful in time-series settings. For feasible implementation of AsympCSs, we establish strong consistency of HAC variance estimators under the FDM framework, accommodating a wider range of commonly used bandwidth choices than existing results under mixing conditions. As illustrations, we construct AsympCSs for algorithms with Markovian structure and time-series-based causal estimands.

papers.title: On finite-dimensional attractor to 2D incompressible fluid with stress-diffusion
papers.abstract: We consider incompressible visco-elastic rate-type fluid flow, with the Cauchy stress defined in terms of positive-definite symmetric tensor $B$. The tensor $B$ obeys an evolution equation, combining Oldroyd-B and Giesekus model, and, crucially, a diffusion term. Restricting ourselves to the 2D periodic problem, we show existence of a finite-dimensional global attractor. We also estimate its dimension explicitely in terms of the equation parameters.

papers.title: Counting and constructing Latin tableaux
papers.authors: Spencer Daugherty, Michaela Fahnesock, Shawn Huxtable, Michael Larson, Nourah Al Munayes, Storey Peacock
papers.abstract: Latin tableaux generalize Latin squares to Young diagrams and have interesting connections to linear algebra and Rota's basis conjecture. Conjecturally, a partition admits Latin tableaux if and only if it belongs to a special class called wide partitions. We prove that various classes of wide partitions admit Latin tableaux. We extend these classes further by showing that the number of Latin tableaux is weakly increasing over certain operations on wide partitions. Additionally, we establish an explicit formula for the number of Latin tableaux using (0,1)-matrices and matrix permanents.

papers.title: On Continuous Wavelet Transform of Complex Radon Measures on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a necessary and sufficient condition for a measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{\times} \times \mathbb{R}^{d}$ to be the continuous wavelet transform of a complex Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ under suitable regularity conditions on the wavelets. We define a new norm on the collection of such functions and show that it is isometrically isomorphic to the Banach algebra of complex Radon measures under convolution. We show a wavelet inversion formula for measures, in a restricted sense. Under additional hypothesis, we provide a reconstruction formula for the measure of closed rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$ using wavelet transforms. We have included supporting examples to substantiate these assumptions.

papers.title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity.
  Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.

papers.title: Effective stability and sharp logarithmic time scales for Hamiltonian PDEs on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove effective stability and matching logarithmic upper bounds for small solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs on the one-dimensional torus. An analytic coefficient-majorant calculus and an explicit normal-form iteration yield stability times with logarithms of order $L^{1+1/p}/(\log L)^{1/p}$ for Gevrey weights and $L^{1+(q-1)/(pq+1)}$ for logarithmic ultra-differentiable weights, where $L=\log(1/\varepsilon)$ and $p\geq1$ measures the order dependence of the small divisors. Even frequencies are organized into the exact blocks $\{n,-n\}$; elementary frequency gaps and constant weights on these blocks close the energy estimate. We verify the hypotheses for convolution NLS, fractional NLS with every fixed noninteger exponent $\eta>1/2$, and a beam equation with a metric parameter and a variational gradient nonlinearity. Two fixed analytic nonlocal Hamiltonian PDEs admit finite-support solutions whose first prescribed norm amplification occurs on the same logarithmic scales along sequences $\varepsilon_n\to0$. The common lower theorem applies to every sufficiently small datum of each admissible equation. Its combination with these examples establishes sharpness of both regularity-dependent scales under the same analytic and arithmetic hypotheses.

papers.title: On some problems concerning the growth of Betti numbers
papers.abstract: We investigate several problems concerning the growth of Betti numbers over commutative noetherian rings. First, we establish uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds for the ratios of consecutive Betti numbers of finitely generated modules of infinite projective dimension over an arbitrary local ring, giving an affirmative answer to a question of Avramov. We also prove the upper semicontinuity of the curvature of residue fields of localizations over excellent rings. Next, using zeros of Hilbert series, we obtain criteria for exponential growth of Betti and Bass numbers of graded modules. As applications, we establish exponential growth of the Betti numbers of canonical modules for non-Gorenstein positively graded Cohen-Macaulay domains. Furthermore, we show that the first Betti number of the canonical module of a non-Gorenstein generically Gorenstein Cohen-Macaulay local ring is strictly larger than the zeroth. In particular, both questions of Jorgensen and Leuschke have affirmative answers for Cohen-Macaulay quotients of Gorenstein local rings by monomial ideals in regular sequences.

papers.title: Tamed Euler Approximation of Invariant Measures for Weakly Interacting Particle Systems and McKean--Vlasov Equations
papers.authors: Lingyan Cheng, Ruinan Li, Shiyu Liu, Wei Liu
papers.abstract: We analyze explicit tamed Euler approximations for weakly interacting particle systems and McKean--Vlasov diffusions with additive noise and polynomially weighted locally H\"older, possibly superlinear drift.Under dissipativity at infinity and suitable stability assumptions, we establish time-uniform $W_1$ bounds by reflection coupling, separating relaxation, time-discretization, and finite-particle errors.For small step sizes, we prove existence and uniqueness of numerical invariant laws and bound their error relative to the continuous-time particle invariant law uniformly in $N$ in a normalized joint $W_1$ distance. We further bound the error of the one-particle numerical invariant marginal relative to the McKean--Vlasov invariant law by $O(\theta^{\min\{\alpha,\beta/2\}}+N^{-1/2})$, where $\theta$ is the step size, $N$ the particle number, $\alpha\in(0,1/2]$ the taming exponent, and $\beta\in(0,1]$ the H\"older exponent. Analytical examples illustrate the framework for smooth and non-Lipschitz drifts.

papers.title: Upper and lower bounds for heat kernels with very strong degeneracy
papers.abstract: We consider the following degenerate parabolic equation on a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^d$ containing $0$: $\partial_t u - \nabla\cdot(\varphi(t, x) \nabla u)= 0$, where $\varphi$ is a rough weight behaving like $|x|^\theta$ near $0$ for some $\theta \geq 2$, and $u$ satisfies Neumann boundary condition. We prove that this equation admits a heat kernel with upper and lower Gaussian-type bounds.

papers.title: Ideal class groups of certain real quadratic number fields and factorizations of values of certain quadratic polynomials
papers.abstract: We determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $d-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive odd integers $x\leq\sqrt{p}$. We also determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $2p-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive even integers $x\leq\sqrt{2p}$. To this end, we show that these properties of $p$ and $2p$ impose restrictions on the class numbers and fundamental units of the real quadratic fields ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{p})$ and ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{2p})$.

papers.title: An Arnold-Type Stability Analysis of Vortex Filaments
papers.abstract: We establish nonlinear orbital stability of circular arcs with opening angle $\theta\le \pi$ and closed circles under the Localized Induction Equation (LIE), with prescribed endpoint constraints for arcs. Our Arnold-type variational approach combines two conserved quantities, the bending energy and a component of the fluid impulse, into a functional that we prove is comparable to the squared $H^2$-distance from the corresponding orbit for all admissible curves. For circular arcs with angle $\theta>\pi$, we prove nonlinear orbital instability using the inverse generalized Hasimoto transformation.

papers.title: Lipschitz numbers and fine differentiability on metric measure spaces
papers.abstract: On a metric space equipped with a doubling measure supporting a Poincar\'e inequality, we introduce capacity-relaxed infinitesimal Lipschitz numbers and characterize Newtonian functions in $N^{1,p}$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and functions of bounded variation. If $X$ is additionally $Q$-regular, then every BV function is $1$-finely differentiable at $\mu$-almost every point, and its fine differential agrees with its approximate Cheeger differential. We also extend a Sobolev regularity criterion from continuous to $p$-quasicontinuous functions.

papers.title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
papers.abstract: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We prove the second variation formula, identify the energy Hessian with the index form, and characterize its null space. Under additional hypotheses, we establish existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization.

papers.title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design for MIMO-ISAC
papers.authors: Syed Ali Haider Shirazi, Taejoon Kim, David J. Love, Sergiy A. Vorobyov
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.

papers.title: Adaptive Grid Refinement for Optimal Feedback Control
papers.authors: Alen E. Golpashin, Matthew T. Clark, Bruce A. Conway
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an algorithmic approach for adaptive grid refinement for solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) partial differential equation (PDE) to obtain the optimal feedback control. Traditional grid generation methods often face challenges associated with state-space dimensionality, solution regularity, and large variations in the solution. Whereas fixed grid generation methods may fail to capture the intricate details of the optimal solution, our methodology addresses this challenge by dynamically refining the grid used to solve the HJB equation, thereby optimizing computational resource usage while targeting improved solution accuracy. The reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach presented in this study seeks to reduce the node population while constructing a grid with higher node density in regions with large discretization error.

papers.title: Order-Specified Quaternion CP Decomposition: Models, Algorithms, and Applications
papers.authors: Jifei Miao, Niansheng Tang, Michael K. Ng, Juan Han, Kit Ian Kou
papers.abstract: Tensor CP decomposition serves as a fundamental tool for representing multiway data. While quaternion tensors are well suited to modeling color visual data, extending CP decomposition to the quaternion domain is nontrivial due to the noncommutativity of quaternion multiplication. This paper develops an order-specified quaternion CP decomposition (OS-QCP) for third-order tensors, allowing all three factor matrices to be quaternion-valued and explicitly incorporating their multiplication order into the model. We show that different multiplication orders can yield different OS-QCP ranks for the same quaternion tensor, characterize the permutation and quaternion scaling indeterminacies, and establish a sufficient condition for essential uniqueness for any prescribed multiplication order. An explicit example further shows that OS-QCP rank can depend on the multiplication order even when the complex representation of the quaternion tensor admits an essentially unique CP decomposition. An alternating least-squares (ALS) algorithm is derived by expressing quaternion left and right multiplication as real linear operators, reducing each factor update to real least-squares problems. To accommodate order dependence in tensor completion, we further introduce an order-ensemble quaternion CP (OE-QCP) model that incorporates different multiplication orders through nonnegative weights. The model jointly estimates three quaternion factor matrices and the order weights, with each single-order OS-QCP model included as a special case. The resulting completion problem is solved by a parallel row-wise masked ALS algorithm. Experiments on color video inpainting demonstrate the effectiveness and competitive performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Local Lyapunov Exponent-Guided Stochastic Midcourse Correction Design of Low-Energy Earth-Moon Transfers
papers.authors: Zihang Wang, Shuyue Fu, Di Wu, Shengping Gong
papers.abstract: Midcourse correction is essential for reliable cislunar transfer missions. For low-energy Earth-Moon transfers, strongly nonuniform error growth makes conventional correction strategies less effective. This paper proposes a stochastic midcourse correction design for low-energy Earth-Moon transfers based on local Lyapunov exponent (LLE). The local error-amplification characteristics of the nominal trajectory are first analyzed using an instantaneous LLE. The analysis shows that strong sensitivity is concentrated near periapsis, and that the LLE maxima coincide with regions of strong finite-time error growth. These maxima are therefore used to segment the trajectory and define the number of corrections. Based on this segmentation, a reduced parameterization is introduced to describe the correction epochs, while second-order state transition tensors (STTs) are employed for nonlinear correction targeting. The resulting timing variables are then optimized through a sample-average approximation of the chance-constrained stochastic problem. Paired Monte Carlo simulations show that, under the same mission-accuracy requirements, the proposed strategy greatly improves the reliability and robustness of trajectory recovery while requiring less correction cost than the classical Breakwell spacing-ratio strategy.

papers.title: Continuous spectrum-shrinking maps between finite-dimensional power-associative algebras
papers.abstract: For finite-dimensional complex power-associative algebras $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$, each equipped with its unique Hausdorff vector topology, we characterize continuous spectrum-shrinking maps $\phi:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{B}$, i.e. maps satisfying $\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{B}}(\phi(x)) \subseteq\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{A}}(x)$ for all $x\in\mathcal{A}$. The spectrum of an element is the zero set of its minimal polynomial, computed in the unitization for nonunital algebras. No such map exists when $\mathcal{A}$ is unital and $\mathcal{B}$ is nonunital. Otherwise, we symmetrize both products by setting $x\circ y:=\tfrac{1}{2}(xy+yx)$ and factor out the nilradicals to obtain semisimple Jordan quotients. We prove that a continuous map $\phi$ is spectrum-shrinking precisely when, for every $x\in\mathcal{A}$, Jacobson's generic minimal polynomials of the simple quotient coordinates of $\phi(x)$ are products of fixed nonnegative integer powers of those of $x$, with an additional fixed monomial factor allowed when $\mathcal{A}$ is nonunital. Comparing degrees gives linear Diophantine equations characterizing existence, and every nonnegative integer solution is realized by a polynomial spectrum-shrinking map. Spectrum preservation, meaning equality of spectra, is equivalent to additional positivity conditions. We also determine when every continuous spectrum-shrinking map preserves spectra and show that every continuous map $f:\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{C}$ with $f(x)\in\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{A}}(x)$ for all $x\in\mathcal{A}$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linear and satisfies $f(x\circ y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathcal{A}$.

papers.title: The L\'{e}vy wave packet and fractional uncertainty relations
papers.authors: Zi-Xuan Li, Xiao-Dong Li, Towe Wang
papers.abstract: This work revisits the debate on fractional uncertainty relations that arose a decade ago and tries to settle it. After a careful study of the position-momentum uncertainty product of the L\'{e}vy wave packet, a novel lower bound is proposed for uncertainty relations in fractional quantum mechanics. This bound is nearly linear in the L\'{e}vy index and is satisfied by exact, calculable solutions available in the literature.

papers.title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for $L^p$-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study the critical Moser--Trudinger supremum \[ S(\lambda,p) =
\sup_{\substack{ u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} (|\nabla u|^2+u^2)\,dx\le 1 }} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \left(e^{4\pi u^2}-1-\lambda |u|^p\right)\,dx, \qquad p\ge 2. \] Building on the classification away from the thresholds by Chen, Jiang, Lu and Zhu (2026), we resolve the endpoint cases: both thresholds for $p=2$ and the finite threshold for $2<p\le4$ are attained. We also prove compactness of centred radial extremals and one-sided value expansions governed by the selected endpoint $L^p$ mass. For $p>4$, we quantify how extremals spread out as $\lambda\to\infty$ by establishing the two-term expansion \[
  S(\lambda,p)=4\pi+\mathcal C_p\lambda^{-2/(p-4)}
  +D_p\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}+o\bigl(\lambda^{-4/(p-4)}\bigr), \] Here $\mathcal C_p$ is the maximum of a limiting variational problem at unit $L^2$ mass. An explicit correction involving the sixth moment and the full $H^1$ normalization determines $D_p$ and selects the limiting maximizers. Rescaled centred radial extremals converge strongly to these profiles in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ along subsequences. For every fixed $\lambda>\lambda_*(4)$, we further establish \[
  \lim_{p\downarrow4}(p-4)\log\bigl(S(\lambda,p)-4\pi\bigr)
