  =2\log\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}}{\lambda}<0, \] where $\lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local critical penalty determined by the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant. The gradient energy has the same logarithmic rate, and the centred radial profiles, normalized in mass and gradient energy, converge along subsequences to sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg optimizers. An exact transfer identity extends these endpoint and asymptotic results to every constant planar norm.

papers.title: Frobenius forms and semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras
papers.abstract: We determine the Nakayama automorphism of the canonical homogeneous Frobenius form on cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras. We give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on the dominant weight and the rank for semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras of types $A_e^{(1)}$, $C_e^{(1)}$, $A_{2e}^{(2)}$, $D_{e+1}^{(2)}$, $A_\infty$, $B_\infty$, and $C_\infty$. As an application, we prove that a cyclotomic Hecke--Clifford superalgebra is semisimple if and only if the corresponding Poincar\'e polynomial is nonzero.

papers.title: A spinor-adapted geometric approach to nonlinear Dirac systems on the Schwarzschild black hole background
papers.abstract:
Building on our previous work, we extend the spinor-adapted geometric method for nonlinear Dirac systems from small perturbations of Minkowski spacetime to the Schwarzschild background. As a linear foundation, we establish integrated local energy decay estimates and an \(r^p\)-weighted energy hierarchy for spinor fields, adapting the physical-space approach of Dafermos and Rodnianski to the Dirac setting.
  The main focus of the paper is nonlinear. We consider a semilinear tensorial wave--Dirac model motivated by the wave-gauge reduction of the Einstein--Dirac system and prove global small-data stability. A principal difficulty is the apparent loss of derivatives arising from the coupling between the first-order Dirac equation and the second-order tensorial wave equation. We overcome this difficulty through a spinor-adapted energy hierarchy that exploits the complementary roles of the Dirac-current energy and the spinorial wave energy. In particular, the nonlinear estimates are closed without requiring the top-order Dirac-current estimate.
  The nonlinear analysis demonstrates that the spinorial structures remain essential on the black-hole background. The combination of Dirac-current energy, spinorial wave energy, Kosmann Lie derivatives, and the Clifford-algebraic null structure enables us to close the nonlinear estimates without imposing an independent null condition on the tensorial wave equation. Thus, the nonlinear closure relies fundamentally on structures intrinsic to the Dirac equation.
  A second main result is the global small-data stability of the Maxwell--Dirac system in the Lorenz gauge on the Schwarzschild background, under a vanishing-charge assumption. This extends the nonlinear stability theory to a genuine gauge-coupled Dirac system and demonstrates the applicability of the spinor-adapted physical-space approach beyond the tensorial wave--Dirac model.

papers.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q>19683$, we settle the Cheng--Murray deep-hole problem for full-length Reed--Solomon codes in every dimension $2\le k\le q-2$, with the characteristic-two cases stated explicitly. For odd $q$, the deep holes are precisely the words of degree $k$. For even $q$ and $k\ge3$, the same conclusion holds except for an additional family when $k=q-3$. In even characteristic and dimension two, every deep hole has a unique expression $a h(X)+bX+c$, where $a\ne0$ and $h$ is a normalized $o$-polynomial. The proof combines quadratic quotient algebras, graph-theoretic weighted independent-set inequalities, and planar arc completion. We also obtain normal rational curve rigidity in the corresponding nonexceptional dimensions, the projective Reed--Solomon covering radii, and distinct-coordinate solvability and remainder criteria.

papers.title: Exploiting Pinching Antenna Systems in NOMA Covert Communication Networks
papers.authors: Xinwei Yue, Hao Li, Jingjing Zhao, Xianfu Lei, Yuanwei Liu
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) provide flexible transmitter-side radiation reconfiguration for high-frequency wireless communications. This paper applies PASS to non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) covert communication networks, where activated pinching antennas (PAs) transmit superimposed signals to a pair of users stochastically distributed within a rectangle. Two passive wardens respectively monitor the downlink transmissions intended for two users. More specifically, we derive the closed-form detection error probability (DEP) expressions for two wardens under bounded noise uncertainty. Then we analytically determine the optimal detection thresholds and minimum DEPs in the worst-case covert detection scenarios. The covert transmission rates of two users are further characterized by taking into consideration ideal successive interference cancellation and non-ideal successive interference cancellation at near user and intra-NOMA interference at far user. Numerical results are presented to confirm that: 1) PASS-NOMA is capable of providing higher covert rates relative to conventional orthogonal multiple access OMA schemes; 2) As the number of activated PAs begun to increase, the near user has ability to obtain a larger covert rate gain than far user; and 3) The DEP of PASS-NOMA networks is larger than that of both PASS-OMA and traditional antenna (TA) based NOMA in specific output power regions.

papers.title: Classification of analytic conformal product structures
papers.abstract: We classify real-analytic conformal product structures on compact simply connected manifolds in all dimensions $n\ge 2$. We prove that in dimension $2$ and $3$ no such structure exists, while in every dimension $n\ge 4$ the two parallel distributions arise from a global product splitting.

papers.title: Computing Theta Characteristics and their Galois action on general curves of moderate genus
papers.abstract: In this article, we present an algorithm that, given a smooth curve $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, returns an explicit arithmetic representation of both odd and even Theta Characteristics split by parity. It allows us to retrieve their Galois action and \'etale algebra. The output includes the Theta Hyperplanes of the Theta Characteristics when they are finite, their associated proof functions as well as the dictionary of their quadratic forms. The algorithm works in a rather large generality as it handles any one-equation (potentially singular) model of smooth curves. The most binding requirement remains the necessity for an explicit degree 1 rational divisor on the curve or more likely a rational point. We implemented the algorithm and give examples up to genus $5$.

papers.title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
papers.authors: Gehao Wang, Hao Dong, Yufeng Nie, Junzhi Cui
papers.abstract: Significant spatial heterogeneity and nonlocal history-dependent attenuation jointly govern wave propagation in composite materials, making full-scale direct numerical simulation (DNS) computationally prohibitive. This study proposed a high-order multi-scale (HOMS) method for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems with highly oscillatory and discontinuous material coefficients. Using a multi-scale asymptotic expansion approach, the macroscopic homogenized equation, and first- and second-order correction terms are derived to construct the high-accuracy HOMS solution. Moreover, a local pointwise error analysis identifies the leading residual eliminated by this HOMS solution and validates its local physical balance preservation. Then, a global energy-norm error estimate establishes the $O(\varepsilon)$-order convergence rate for the HOMS solution. Subsequently, an efficient spatiotemporal multi-scale algorithm integrating the finite element and finite difference methods is designed, which employs a novel fully discrete $L2\text{-}1_{\sigma}$-Newmark scheme, and corresponding unconditional shifted-energy stability and explicit convergence rates are also obtained for the macroscopic homogenized displacement and velocity, respectively. Both two- and three-dimensional examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, reduced cost, and robustness of the proposed HOMS method. This work provides an effective multi-scale tool for nonlocal-in-time wave simulation in engineering applications.

papers.title: Local well-posedness, blow-up phenomenon and ill-posedness for a model system of the radiating gas
papers.authors: Jian Chen, Zhaonan Luo, Yuchen Yang, Zhaoyang Yin
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Cauchy problem for a model system of radiating gas in multi-dimensional space. Firstly, we prove that the model is locally well-posed in Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $s>1+\frac{d}{p}$ (resp., $s=1+\frac{d}{p}$, $r=1$), including the endpoint space $B^1_{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Secondly, we show that the data-to-solution map is not uniformly continuous on bounded subsets of these Besov spaces. Moreover, we construct a blow-up scenario and derive two sufficient blow-up conditions, which improve the previous blow-up condition obtained in \cite{MR3016436}. Finally, we prove that the Cauchy problem is ill-posed in the critical space $B^{1+\frac{d}{p}}_{p,r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $r>1$ in the sense of norm inflation.

papers.title: Approximate Matrix Multiplication through Joint Leverage Score Sampling
papers.authors: Neophytos Charalambides, Mert Pilanci, Alfred O. Hero III
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate approximate matrix multiplication through random sampling. Specifically, we propose using a non-uniform sampling distribution constructed from the leverage scores of the two matrices, and characterize the associated approximation error in terms of the matrix spectral norm; which is well-known to better characterize the downstream error when the matrix product operator is applied to an input vector. We provide the probability error bounds for the proposed algorithm are also given, and discuss connections to data-oblivious approximate matrix multiplication, and graph sparsification algorithms.

papers.title: General function bases moment models for suspended sediment with vertical profile of concentration
papers.authors: Celia Caballero-C\'ardenas, Jos\'e Garres-D\'iaz, Irene G\'omez-Bueno, Tom\'as Morales de Luna
papers.abstract: We introduce a general hydrostatic shallow moment framework for suspended sediment transport with vertically varying horizontal velocity and concentration profiles. The formulation is constructed over arbitrary vertical functional bases that are numerically orthogonalised via the Gram-Schmidt algorithm. This approach allows the approximation spaces for the vertical profile to be adapted to the specific structure of each physical variable, where also the velocity and sediment concentration can be projected onto different functional spaces. To overcome the limitations due to the inherent oscillatory nature of global Legendre polynomials, we explore a specific continuous piecewise linear $\mathbb{P}_1$ finite-element basis. Furthermore, non-uniform vertical partitions are considered, enabling an enhanced representation of the vertical profiles in specific regions. Numerical experiments involving boundary layers and suspended sediment transport demonstrate that the proposed framework is accurate to reproduce the expected vertical profiles. The improvement is particularly significant for sediment concentration profiles with sharp vertical variations, where polynomial reconstructions exhibit pronounced oscillations leading to physically meaningless profiles, whereas the $\mathbb{P}_1$ bases produce a qualitatively accurate representation of the vertical profiles observed in the sedimentation processes.

papers.title: An entropy proof of the commonality of apices of trees
papers.abstract: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-colouring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random colouring with an equal proportion of each colour. Grzesik, Lee, Lidick\'y and Volec conjectured that every $k$-apex of any connected Sidorenko graph is common. Recently, Kr{\'a}l', Krnc and Lamaison proved that the $k$-apex of any tree is common for $k\leq 5$. In this paper, we extend their result by showing that for every positive integer $k$, the $k$-apex of any tree or any forest with average degree at least one is common. Our proof involves an application of the entropy method.

papers.title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers within the set of squares
papers.abstract: We prove that the set of numbers of type $n = 2m^2$ below $X$ which cannot be written as a sum of two primes has cardinality at most $X^{19/24 + o(1)}$.

papers.title: Enhanced Langlands Parameters of Regular Principal Series
papers.authors: Haoming Li, Xiaohang Yang, Jizhi Zhang, Yelei Zhao
papers.abstract: We describe the enhanced Langlands parameters of the irreducible constituents of a regular principal series of a quasi-split reductive group over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. Starting from the chamber parametrization by Rodier and Luo, we determine the monodromy of each constituent and show that its enhancement is trivial. In particular, we obtain the corresponding parameter of the unique irreducible subrepresentation.

papers.title: Point Cloud Transmission With Patch-Based Rate Adaptation
papers.authors: Shipeng Liu, Garima Bazard, Khac-Hoang Ngo, Per-Erik Forss\'en
papers.abstract: We propose a joint source-channel coding (JSCC) framework for efficient wireless point cloud transmission. In the proposed scheme, the point cloud is first divided into local patches and transformed into compact latent representations, which are then mapped to symbols for transmission over a noisy channel. Our model incorporates an entropy model that exploits inter-patch spatial dependencies to estimate patch-level coding costs and allocate different numbers of symbols accordingly. Unlike existing patch-based point cloud JSCC methods that use the same transmission rate between patches, we adapt the channel usage of each patch latent representation. To exploit inter-patch dependencies without patch-by-patch autoregressive processing, we select a group of anchor patches whose features provide contextual information for entropy estimation of non-anchor ones. The framework is trained using a reconstruction loss and an entropy-based rate surrogate. Experiments on ModelNet40 demonstrate overall rate-distortion improvements over existing baselines across channel conditions.

papers.title: Revisiting the infinite Galois correspondence via group representations
papers.abstract: Inspired by Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem, we interpret the Galois correspondence as a special case of a simple general principle in harmonic analysis on profinite groups. This also gives a representation-theoretic characterisation of profinite groups.

papers.title: Symmetry Inheritance and Exact Mirror Symmetry Reduction for Electric Field Vector Wave Problems with PEC Boundaries
papers.abstract: A symmetry-inheritance and exact domain-reduction framework is developed for the second-order vector wave equation of the electric field in bounded domains with a perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary and general spatially varying anisotropic media. Orthogonal group actions on polar vectors, axial vectors, and second-order constitutive tensors are used to derive the transformed curl--curl equation and PEC trace directly from the original boundary-value problem. Under unique solvability, the common symmetry group of the problem data is inherited by the electric field. When the symmetry group of the electromagnetic medium admits a mirror symmetry, an arbitrary impressed current can be decomposed by the associated reflection projectors into mirror-even and mirror-odd components. The corresponding full-domain fields inherit the respective parities, and their exact restriction to one half-domain yields a perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) condition for the even field and a PEC condition for the odd field. The original problem is therefore represented exactly by two independent reduced-domain problems. A symmetry-compatible first-family N\'ed\'elec discretization preserves this decomposition at the discrete level. Analytical and numerical results verify the symmetry-inheritance theory, the exact PEC/PMC reduced-domain formulations, and the discrete reconstruction for constant and spatially varying anisotropic conductive media under both symmetric and asymmetric excitations.

papers.title: Local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for unitary groups: Trace formula approach for epsilon dichotomy
papers.authors: Cheng Chen, Xiaowei Li, Bushi Ren
papers.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide a proof independent of the theta-lifting for the epsilon-dichotomy of the local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture of real unitary groups for tempered L-parameters. The approach is based on the local trace formula and endoscopic character identities following Waldspurger and Chen-Luo.

papers.title: Frequency Structure of AMM Liquidity Pools: A Multiresolution Analysis of Regime Transitions
papers.abstract: This study examines the temporal structure of liquidity pools in constant-product automated market makers. Using a sample of eighteen pools observed at a five-minute frequency over two years, it aims to identify the temporal scales at which interactions within the system occur and how these interactions reorganize in response to changes in the volatility regime. Methodologically, the study proposes a strictly causal Haar multiresolution analysis in which each variable is estimated using only the information available at the time of measurement. Within this decomposition, three dimensions are examined: the scale composition of the return-to-risk relationship, the frequency-band coupling between pool activity and price volatility, and the detection of regime transitions using a fluctuation-to-trend indicator. The results reveal a clear structural segmentation: pool variability is concentrated at fast scales, whereas the relationships among its series, signal persistence, and information on subsequent performance reside at slow scales. Aggregate measures do not distinguish this separation because they combine both components before they can be compared.

papers.title: Scalar--Mean Rigidity for Hyperbolic Balls in Dimensions $2\le n\le 5$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the non-spin hyperbolic scalar--mean rigidity theorem in dimensions $2\leq n\leq5$, resolving the corresponding low-dimensional case of a problem of Gromov. The proof combines the Jang deformation with capillary $\mu$-bubble dimension reduction. We also establish weighted scalar--mean rigidity for Euclidean ball--torus products in total dimension at most seven and show that its hyperbolic analogue fails.

papers.title: $q$-middle Laplace transform and its applications
papers.abstract:
We introduce a $q$-analog of the one-variable middle Laplace transform defined by the first author. We establish its invertibility and preservation of irreducibility, and derive a decomposition of $q$-middle convolution in terms of this transform.
  As applications, we obtain integral representations of solutions to the confluent $q$-hypergeometric equation and its variant, and construct a transformation of the $2\times 2$ Lax linear equation associated with the $q$-Painlev\'{e} equation of type $A_4^{(1)}$.

papers.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for optimal control of coupled forward-backward stochastic control systems driven by G-Brownian motion
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a coupled forward-backward stochastic control system driven by G-Brownian motion. Based on some detailed estimates for control system, we obtain the variational inequality for cost functional, which is a necessary condition for optimality. Furthermore, we prove that this necessary condition is also a sufficient condition under the usual convexity assumptions.

papers.title: The minimal period solution of Hamiltonian systems with even potentials
papers.abstract: We consider the autonomous system $\ddot{q}+\nabla V(q)=0$ in an arbitrary finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The potential is assumed to be even, nonnegative and of class $C^2$, to satisfy $V(x)=o(|x|^2)$ at the origin, and the Ambrosetti--Rabinowitz superquadratic inequality outside a ball. We prove that, for every prescribed $T>0$, the system has a nonconstant solution with $T$ being its minimal positive period.

papers.title: The first $\ell^2$-Betti number, cost and rank gradient of few-relator random groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a random group in the few-relator model with $n\ge 2$ generators and $m\ge 1$ relators. We prove that asymptotically almost surely the first $\ell^2$-Betti number, the cost minus one, and the absolute rank gradient of $G$ are all equal to $\max\{n-m-1,0\}$. In particular, the equality $\beta_1^{(2)}(G)=0$ when $m\ge n-1$ answers positively a conjecture of Kielak, Kropholler and Wilkes [J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2022].

papers.title: Finite-to-One Maps into Band-Limited Function Spaces and Cubical Shifts with a Hurewicz Bound
papers.abstract: Let $(X,T)$ be a dynamical system with the marker property and finite mean dimension $m$. We prove that, for every integer $D>m$, there exists an equivariant continuous map $f:X\to([0,1]^D)^{\mathbb Z}$ whose fibers contain at most $\lfloor D/(D-m)\rfloor$ points; in particular, $f$ is an embedding when $D>2m$. This is the dynamical analogue of the fiber bound in Hurewicz's classical theorem (1933) for continuous maps into Euclidean cubes. For every real number $a>m$, we also construct an equivariant continuous map from $X$ into the closed unit ball of the real Bernstein space of bounded continuous functions on $\mathbb R$ whose Fourier transforms, understood in the sense of distributions, are supported in $[-a/2,a/2]$, with each fiber containing at most $\lfloor a/(a-m)\rfloor$ points. The proof adapts the signal-analysis method of Gutman--Qiao--Tsukamoto (2019) to the finite-to-one setting and simplifies its analytic and geometric ingredients for $\mathbb Z$-actions.

papers.title: Maximal velocity estimates for Hardy operators
papers.abstract: We prove maximal velocity estimates for the fractional Laplacian with an added subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator, and possibly external potentials. As an application, we give another proof of the nonexistence of the wave operator intertwining Hardy operators with and without long-range perturbations with Coulomb decay.

papers.title: $L^p$-Liouville properties and realizations of Schr\"odinger operators on incomplete Riemannian manifolds
papers.authors: Andrea Bisterzo, Salvatore Lincastri, Giona Veronelli
papers.abstract:
The aim of the paper is to highlight and standardize in a self-contained framework the connections between some properties associated with the Laplace-Beltrami operator on possibly incomplete Riemannian manifolds. We present both new and well-known characterizations of the positivity-preserving property, essential self-adjointness, and Liouville-type results for $L^2$-functions, using the latter to establish a clear hierarchy among these properties.
  Furthermore, we prove the stability of the essential self-adjointness of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on incomplete Riemannian manifolds under the removal of closed (possibly non-compact) subsets from a complete manifold, subject to suitable conditions on their (generalized) Hausdorff measure.
  With appropriate modifications, this framework is adapted throughout the paper to the general $L^p$-case for $p\in (1,+\infty)$.

papers.title: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
papers.abstract: We develop the first tensor-product sparse-grid finite element discretizations of Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. We construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials for Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to full grids.

papers.title: Avoiding two cycles in Avoider--Enforcer games
papers.abstract: We study the strict and monotone $(1:b)$ Avoider--Enforcer games on the edges of the complete graph $K_n$. We prove that, for integers $n\ge2$ and $b\ge6n$, Avoider can keep his graph a forest after every move, except possibly the last. Thus, his final graph contains at most one cycle. This answers Question~10 of Clemens, Ehrenm\"uller, Person, and Tran, which asks whether a bias linear in $n$ is sufficient.

papers.title: Cyclic group tensors and the volume ratio of projective tensor products
papers.abstract: We revisit the problem of estimating the norm of the natural embedding from the Euclidean space $\ell_2^{n^3}$ into the projective tensor product $\ell_p^n\otimes_\pi\ell_q^n\otimes_\pi\ell_r^n$ in the range $1\le p\le q\le 2\le r\le\infty$, studied by Giladi, Prochno, Sch\"utt, Tomczak-Jaegermann and Werner [J. Funct. Anal. 273 (2017), 471-495]. Using convolution on finite cyclic groups, we establish new lower bounds that improve their estimates and determine the exact asymptotic order of the embedding norm whenever $1/p+1/q+1/r\ge 2$. We then apply an estimate of Boedihardjo for the injective norm of random tensors to a randomly signed cyclic convolution tensor and use multilinear interpolation to determine the optimal exponent throughout the entire parameter range, up to logarithmic factors. As consequences, we obtain corresponding improvements and asymptotically sharp estimates, up to logarithmic factors, for the volume ratio of these projective tensor products.

papers.title: Kobayashi's problem for power semigroups of inverse semigroups
papers.abstract:
For a semigroup $S$ (written multiplicatively), let $\mathcal P(S)$ denote the semigroup of all non-empty subsets of $S$ under setwise multiplication. The finitary power semigroup $\mathcal P_\text{fin}(S)$ is the subsemigroup of $\mathcal P(S)$ consisting of all non-empty finite subsets of $S$.
  Kobayashi's problem asks for which classes $\mathcal O$ of semigroups every isomorphism $\mathcal P(H) \to \mathcal P(K)$ with $H, K \in \mathcal O$ maps singletons bijectively onto singletons and hence induces an isomorphism $H \to K$. We give an affirmative answer for inverse semigroups, extending previous results for groups, semilattices, and, more generally, Clifford semigroups. We also establish the corresponding rigidity theorem for finitary power semigroups. To this end, we develop a new framework that provides a common approach to both settings.

papers.title: Minimax Rates for imperfect Physics-Informed Regression
papers.abstract: Physics-informed machine learning incorporates physical knowledge into data-driven models, often through a partial differential equation (PDE) that the target is assumed to satisfy. However, how much this knowledge improves statistical performance remains unclear, especially when the physical model is imperfect. Since satisfying a PDE implies being differentiable, a natural benchmark for physics-informed regression is the best achievable performance when smoothness is the only prior information about the target function. We show that there is a characteristic threshold for the modeling error above which the physical prior cannot improve the convergence rate. The form of this threshold is common to every linear PDE and certain nonlinear PDEs. Below it, the gain depends on the equation type. For classes of elliptic and hyperbolic PDEs with constant coefficients, we establish convergence rates that improve continuously as the modeling error decreases, and prove their minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors. With exact physics, the rates correspond to learning in dimension d-1 rather than d, reflecting the freedom left by unknown boundary or initial data. We also give conditions for computing the estimator with near-linear complexity and show how to tune its hyperparameters without knowing the modeling error.

papers.title: A recovery based linear finite element method for the Monge--Amp\`{e}re equation
papers.authors: Tianyang Chu, Hailong Guo, Zhimin Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study finite element approximations of a fourth-order perturbed semilinear partial differential equation that arises naturally in the computation of viscosity solutions to the fully nonlinear Monge--Amp\`{e}re equation. We develop a novel recovery-based $C^0$ linear finite element method for discretizing this model problem. The key analytical tool is a Miranda--Talenti-type estimate for the recovery operator, which guides the formulation of the discrete scheme and guarantees its well-posedness. We rigorously establish convergence in the $H^2$ norm by employing a fixed-point argument. Furthermore, optimal $H^1$-error estimates are derived using a duality argument. Numerical experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed method and validate the theoretical convergence results.

papers.title: Cartan Subalgebras of Dimension Drop Interval Algebras and Their Inductive Limits
papers.abstract: We describe the conjugacy of non-degenerate Cartan subalgebras of the dimension drop interval algebras $M_m(\widetilde{\mathbb I}_p)$ in terms of double cosets of permutation groups, and describe their spectra by finite bi-partite multigraphs. All Cartan subalgebras are non-degenerate precisely when the two parameters are coprime. We also give splitting interval examples with prescribed finite numbers of Cartan conjugacy classes. Passing to inductive limits, we construct a unital simple AD algebra $\mathcal{A}$ of real rank zero and stable rank one, with $K_0(\mathcal{A})\cong\mathbb Z[1/3]$ and $K_1(\mathcal{A})\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. It contains infinitely many mutually isomorphic but pairwise nonconjugate $\mathrm{C}^*$-diagonals. Their spectra are all homeomorphic to the dense amalgam of circles, while orbit multiplicities in the Weyl groupoids distinguish their embeddings. The same AD algebra also contains infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic Cartan subalgebras.

papers.title: Broadcasting in Centimeter-Wave Gigantic MIMO Systems: Beam Shaping is All You Need
papers.authors: Boyu Ning, Yike Xie, Jaebum Park, Songjie Yang, Weidong Mei, Emil Bj\"ornson, Robert W. Heath Jr
papers.abstract: Beamforming is a key enabling technology for centimeter-wave Gigantic MIMO (G-MIMO) systems, using antenna arrays to generate wide beams for cell-wide broadcasting or narrow beams for data transmission. This paper presents a novel \emph{beam shaping technology} for designing environment-aware broadcast beams (i.e., beams for common control information delivery, as in 5G SSB). As a case study, we shape a \emph{prostrate beam} in the vertical plane to approximate uniform electromagnetic power distribution across the ground, thereby enhancing broadcast coverage quality. We first propose a geometric broadcasting model that, through coordinate transformation, relates base station height, beam spread, maximum service distance, and downtilt angle. Building on this model and the signal propagation model, we formulate the beam shaping problem as a non-convex optimization problem that aims to maximize ground-level coverage. To solve it, we develop a generalized optimization framework. We reformulate the problem into a matrix representation, equivalently transforming it into a target pursuit optimization (TPO) problem. Using variable substitution, the objective is convexified into a quadratically constrained quadratic program, and the non-convex rank constraint is handled via successive convex approximation, decomposing the problem into iteratively solved subproblems. We provide complexity and convergence analyses for the proposed algorithm. Numerical simulations confirm that the optimization effectively shapes the intended beam pattern and that the proposed prostrate beam yields significant performance gains, including substantially extended coverage distance, over conventional wide-beam benchmarks.

papers.title: Sequential Entropic Optimal Transport for Bayesian Inverse Problems via Multilevel Monte Carlo
papers.authors: Jason Beh, Pierre Del Moral, Ajay Jasra
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of Bayesian estimation associated to inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). In most cases of practical interest, one must use numerical solvers to implement computational methods based on Monte Carlo methods. This inevitably leads to an adaptation of multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) methods to reduce computational efforts to achieve a pre-specified mean square error (MSE). MLMC is based on sampling coupled versions of Bayesian posteriors associated to increasingly precise numerical solves of the PDE. In this article we present a novel method to implement MLMC based upon sequential entropic optimal transport couplings learned with light Schr\"odinger bridges, and correct the transport with Metropolis--Hastings steps that preserve the pairing. We bound the mean square error associated to a version of our new estimation method and show, for an elliptic inverse problem, that to achieve a MSE of $\mathcal{O}(\delta^2)$ ($\delta >0$) one can have an optimal cost of $\mathcal{O}(\delta^{-2})$. The results feature explicit bounds on the effect of the fitted transport and of the Metropolis--Hastings correction. From a numerical perspective, on elliptic, Darcy-flow and Navier-Stokes problems, the method reduces the variance of the most precise solver by a factor of five to ten and is faster than multilevel sequential Monte Carlo [arXiv:1503.07259] at tight accuracies.

papers.title: Algorithm duality from resolvent Moreau identities
papers.authors: Andrew Calcan, Alberto De Marchi, Scott B. Lindstrom
papers.abstract: Duality is classically defined as a relationship between objective functions, one that breaks down beyond convexity. We show that a more fundamental duality persists between the resolvent operators used to solve associated problems. We establish a framework from which we obtain complete characterizations of the duality-like correspondences between proximal fixed-point iterations and their alternating minimization scheme counterparts. Namely, we show the known primal-dual relationships between forward--backward splitting and Tseng's alternating minimization algorithm, and between the Douglas-Rachford method and alternating direction method of multipliers, to hold generically and irrespective of problem assumptions. The approach considered herein avoids the machinery of convex analysis entirely, providing a definitive formulation of algorithmic dualities in maximal generality while greatly simplifying their proofs. In particular, assumptions such as monotonicity, weak monotonicity, Lipschitz continuity, and injectivity of linear operators are all shown to be unnecessary. In addition, we utilize our framework to reveal and analyze a novel primal-dual relationship between backward-backward splitting and a special instance of the alternating minimization algorithm. This illustrates how our duality framework provides a principled basis for primal-dual algorithm design and analysis in nonmonotone settings. Finally, our experiments show that our backward--backward splitting--based approach reliably outperforms the FISTA and SR3 algorithms for the LASSO problem.

papers.title: Subsequential Version of Breiman's Conjecture
papers.abstract:
We study randomly weighted sums \[ T_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n X_iY_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i}, \] where $(X_i)$ and $(Y_i)$ are independent sequences of i.i.d. random variables, with nonnegative weights $Y_i$, motivated by Breiman's conjecture.
  We introduce the class $ISSV$ of $I$-subsequentially slowly varying tails and establish a subsequential analogue of Darling's maximum--sum theorem. This provides a subsequential generalization of Breiman's slowly varying theorem and, as a corollary, resolves the slowly varying case of his conjecture.
  We also establish a subsequential analogue of Breiman's nonzero-index theorem, characterizing the existence of nondegenerate subsequential limits, distinct in distribution from $X_1,$ by the failure of slow variation of the integrated tail, for weight $Y_1$ with tail distributions outside the class $ISSV$.
  Finally, we formulate the subsequential separation principle, prove it under a finite-second-moment assumption, and show that its general validity would imply the nonzero-index case of Breiman's conjecture.

papers.title: Harnack-type inequalities for nonlocal parabolic equations in the upper fast-diffusion range
papers.authors: Mariia Savchenko, Igor Skrypnik, Yevgeniia Yevgenieva
papers.abstract: We study non-negative weak solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear nonlocal parabolic equations of the form $$ (u^q)_t+\mathcal Lu=0, $$ where $\mathcal L$ is a nonlocal $p$-Laplace-type operator with a symmetric measurable kernel. We consider the fast-diffusion range $1<p<q+1$ and establish Harnack-type estimates in the upper fast-diffusion regime $\widetilde p_c<p<q+1$, where $\widetilde p_c$ is a critical exponent determined by the interplay between the temporal nonlinearity and the nonlocal diffusion. In particular, the estimates apply to the nonlocal parabolic $p$-Laplace equation and the nonlocal porous medium equation.

papers.title: Dynamical low-rank approximations for the optimal control of matrix ODEs
papers.abstract: We consider the open-loop optimal control of a dynamical system whose state is described by a time-dependent matrix $X(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$. Gradient-based optimization methods may incur substantial computational and memory costs, particularly for large-scale systems and fine temporal discretizations. To alleviate this computational burden, we develop a mathematical framework to use Dynamical Low Rank Approximations (DLRA) in optimal control problems. We study two distinct paradigms: the first one, called Optimize-then-Project (OtP), first derives the optimality system and then approximates both the state and adjoint equations using DLRA. The second one, called Project-then-Optimize (PtO), first replaces the state equation with its DLR approximation, and then derives the optimality conditions for the resulting optimization problem. The two approaches differ fundamentally concerning the role of the adjoint variable. In OtP, the adjoint variable evolves on the manifold of fixed rank matrices, whereas in PtO, the adjoint variable belongs to the tangent space to the fixed-rank manifold at the evolving state variable. This latter formulation leads to a covariant ODE describing the dynamics of the adjoint variable as the underlying tangent space evolves in time. For both approaches we establish rigorous error estimates for the approximated gradients, identifying how their accuracy depends on the low-rank approximations of initial and terminal conditions, the components of the state and adjoint vector fields normal to the relevant tangent spaces, the stability properties of the dynamics, and the manifold curvature. PtO further requires tailored time discretization strategies for the adjoint covariant ODE, which we show to be robust against small singular values of the state variable. To illustrate the framework, we apply these methods to the optimal control of a random parabolic PDE.

papers.title: Data-driven calibration of a two-dimensional traffic flow model: Dimension reduction and optimization strategies
papers.abstract: We study the data-driven calibration of a two-dimensional first-order macroscopic traffic flow model, in which the movement along and across the road is described by a three-parameter flux model. The calibration is based on three real-world datasets, ranging from microscopic drone trajectories on German highways to aggregated urban sensor measurements. We recall the well-posedness of the underlying scalar conservation law and derive structural properties of the flux model. In particular, one parameter enters linearly and can be eliminated analytically, which reduces the non-linear least-squares problem from three to two dimensions. We solve the full and reduced calibration problem with two local optimization methods, Nelder-Mead and L-BFGS-B, and three global population-based methods Differential Evolution, Consensus-Based Optimization, and its deterministic variant Quasi-Monte Carlo consensus based optimization. In addition to accuracy and computational cost, we examine how sensitive the objective is to the parameters and how robust the algorithms are with respect to randomness and initialization. The reduced formulation is considerably cheaper and less sensitive to the choice of optimizer. The local methods are the most efficient when suitably initialized, whereas the global methods are more robust.

papers.title: Continuity of Furstenberg entropy on Bowen Poisson bundles
papers.abstract: We provide a sufficient criterion for continuity of the Furstenberg entropy of Bowen Poisson bundles, jointly in the random walk measure and the underlying invariant random subgroup. The criterion applies in particular for tree-like Poisson bundles of a free group and for intersectional invariant random subgroups on lamplighter groups. It also provides continuity of the boundary entropy spectrum of powers of prime measured groups.

papers.title: The Conjugacy Problem for Recursively Presented Virtually Soluble Groups of Finite Pr\"ufer Rank
papers.authors: M. Brescia, E. Ingrosso, M. Trombetti
papers.abstract: We solve a long-standing conjugacy problem for finitely presented soluble groups of finite Pr\"ufer rank, recorded as Problem~9.52 in the Kourovka Notebook, in the stronger setting of recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble groups. Robinson proved that, in every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble minimax group, conjugacy to any fixed element is decidable, while explicitly lefting open whether the procedure could be made uniform in the target element. We establish this uniformity. More specifically, we prove that every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble group of finite Pr\"ufer rank has decidable Conjugacy Problem.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous random graphs: how heavy tails reshape connectivity
papers.authors: Luisa Andreis, Luca Avena, Rajat Subhra Hazra, Elena Matteini
papers.abstract: We study inhomogeneous random graphs on $n$ vertices with independent Pareto weights of parameter $\alpha>0$ and connection probabilities $\min(\varepsilon_n W_iW_j, 1)$. Our main focus is the infinite-mean regime $0<\alpha<1$. Under the scaling $n\varepsilon_n^\alpha=\lambda$, with $\lambda>0$ fixed, the global architecture of the graph is entirely governed by the Poisson point process $\Pi$ of rescaled extreme weights. In particular, the size of the largest component, divided by $n$, converges to a non-degenerate random variable expressed as an explicit functional of $\Pi$. Through the point process $\Pi$, we also characterize the exact limiting connectivity probability, uncovering a non-sharp connectivity threshold. The second largest component and the diameter of the largest component are bounded with high probability. The distance between two uniformly chosen vertices in the largest component is at most three with high probability. We also prove convergence of the point process of rescaled degrees and identify the limiting distribution of the maximum degree. For completeness, we obtain expected degree asymptotics, typical degree limits and connectivity regimes for all $\alpha>0$. Due to the failure of classical branching process approximations in the infinite-mean regime, our approach relies fundamentally on analyzing the extreme weight environment $\Pi$.

papers.title: A short proof of a range-relative FPTAS for polynomial integer optimization over bounded polyhedra
papers.abstract: We give a short proof of a fully polynomial-time range-relative approximation scheme for polynomial optimization over the integer points of a bounded rational polyhedron in fixed dimension. The proof combines the reflecting-set decomposition of Cook, Hartmann, Kannan, and McDiarmid with Markov's polynomial derivative inequality and uses one integer linear feasibility query per refined cell. The running time is polynomial in the input encoding size, numerical degree, and reciprocal accuracy.

papers.title: Matrix $\Phi$-Entropic Measures of Dependence
papers.abstract: We introduce matrix $\Phi$-ribbons, extending the scalar $\Phi$-ribbons to the matrix case. For $\Phi$ in the subadditivity class, we establish data processing and tensorization properties of matrix $\Phi$-ribbons. We establish scalar and matrix $\Phi$-entropy inequalities and use them to show that both $\Phi$-ribbons characterize the corresponding $\Phi$-strong data processing inequality (SDPI) constants. We obtain exact evaluations of the SDPI constants for several sources. We provide examples showing that the matrix $\Phi$-SDPI constant can exceed the scalar counterpart. Finally, we derive inner bounds for $\Phi$-ribbons from prescribed independence structures and prove that these bounds are optimal when $\Phi(t)=t\log t$.

papers.title: Sharp local scalar-curvature rigidity of spherical caps
papers.abstract:
Let $B(\delta)\subset\mathbb S^n$ be a geodesic ball with the round metric $\bar{g}$ of sectional curvature one, where $n\geq3$ and $0<\delta<\pi/2$. We prove local scalar-curvature rigidity under preservation of the induced boundary metric and a one-sided lower bound for the boundary mean curvature. More precisely, every sufficiently small $C^{2,\alpha}$ perturbation $g$ of $\bar{g}$ satisfying $R(g)\geq n(n-1)$ and $H(g)\geq(n-1)\cot\delta$ is round up to a diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise.
  Inspired by the scalar--vector--tensor decomposition used in the study of Yamabe compactness, we establish positivity of the Brendle--Marques quadratic form in the divergence-free gauge for variations preserving the induced boundary metric and satisfying the joint linearized constraints $D R_{\bar{g}}(h)=D H_{\bar{g}}(h)=0$. The hemisphere counterexamples of Brendle--Marques--Neves show that the radius range is sharp.

papers.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof that R(5,10;5,8)=21 for the Generalized Threshold Ramsey Number
papers.abstract: We prove that the generalized threshold Ramsey number R(5,10;5,8) equals 21. This number corresponds to the set Ramsey number r_5(10,8) introduced by Harborth. The proof is computer-assisted. We first enumerate all (4,6;5,8)-good and (5,10;4,4)-good graphs. Then we apply the lucky-vertex inequality derived from the McKay--Radziszowski edge identity to filter candidate pairs for a gluing search, and encode the remaining cases as SAT instances. The search yields exactly 17 non-isomorphic (5,10;5,8;20)-good graphs. Finally, we exclude all one-vertex extensions of these 17 graphs, which proves that no (5,10;5,8;21)-good graph exists.Additionally, we update the tabulation of small set Ramsey numbers r_5(m,n) for 1 <= m,n <= 10.

papers.title: Examples of absolutely minimal polyhedral chains in maximum norm spaces
papers.abstract: We construct explicit area-minimizing polyhedral disks in $\R^n$ with the maximum norm for $n=2,3,4$. Their boundaries are polygonal images of the geodesic circle of length $2\pi$, obtained from $n$ distance functions. Piecewise constant calibrations show that these disks minimize mass among Ambrosio--Kirchheim metric currents with the same boundary. The example for $n=4$ gives the lower bound $11\pi^2/20\approx5.42828$ for Gromov's filling area conjecture. For $n>4$, finite linear programs provide further lower bounds.

papers.title: Scalar curvature integrals on geodesic balls
papers.abstract:
We study scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and rotational symmetry, we prove the sharp bound \[
  \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g
  \le 2n(n-1)\omega_n
  \bigl(1-v^{1/(n-1)}\bigr)r^{n-2}, \] when $p$ is the rotational origin. Here $\omega_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball and $v=V_{M^n}$ is the asymptotic volume ratio. In dimension three, with the center at a pole, we obtain a sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le16\pi r, \] without any positive volume growth assumption. We also obtain a bound for every asymptotic volume ratio which is sharp for $0\le v\le1/4$.
  Under nonnegative sectional curvature and $v>0$, we prove the explicit bound at arbitrary centers \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le12\pi(1-v)v^{-3}r. \] If $0\le1-v\le1/100$, we further obtain \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le\bigl[8\pi(1-v)+200\pi(1-v)^2\bigr]r. \] The leading coefficient $8\pi$ is sharp, and a remainder of quadratic order in $1-v$ is necessary.

papers.title: Residue Sums Modulo Products of Two Distinct Odd Primes
papers.authors: Haobo Ma, Mircea Merca, Wenlin Zhang
papers.abstract: Let $S_m(a)$ denote the sum of the least positive residues in one multiplicative period of $a$ modulo $m$, of length $k$. We study the equality $S_m(a)=mk/2$ for $m=pq$, where $p,q$ are distinct odd primes and $k$ is even. Complementary pairing settles subgroups containing $-1$; the remaining cases depend on their embedding in the two local unit groups. At index four, we exclude mixed cyclic subgroups with biquadratic annihilator and classify every eligible imprimitive quartic kernel using two odd integer moments at its prime conductor. For each fixed conductor, the proportion of admissible second primes giving equality is $1/4$ or $1/2$; full coset balance has proportion $1/4$. For primitive quartic characters, classical triangular character-sum identities yield explicit short-sum criteria, and the relative class-number formula gives an obstruction to a centered coset. At index six, we give structural counts and construct an infinite family modulo $19q$ in which nonzero sextic and quadratic moments cancel. These applications use a standard odd-character expansion, which also recovers the known index-two balance classification and determines the sign of its deviation. A reproducible census for $pq\le10000$ counts $75\,090$ eligible cyclic subgroups and identifies $101$ mixed index-four subgroups whose own sum is centered although some coset sums are not.

papers.title: Extending Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodules and noncommutative covers
papers.abstract:
Doi and Takeuchi, and independently Blattner, Cohen and Montgomery, have exhibited a correspondence between cleft extensions of an algebra $U$ by a Hopf algebra $H$ and $H$-measurings on $U$ equipped with a compatible normalized 2-cocycle. Each cleft extension is isomorphic as an algebra, a left $U$-module and a right $H$-comodule to the crossed product algebra constructed from the measuring and the cocycle. Cleft $H$-extensions are a special case of $H$-Hopf-Galois extensions, describing noncommutative principal $H$-bundles with affine total and affine base space. Corings are used to describe noncommutative space covers, allowing a description of possibly nonaffine noncommutative spaces. We propose to describe the total space of a noncommutative $H$-principal bundle by an internal $E$-coring in $H$-comodules where $E$ is an $H$-comodule algebra which is itself $H$-Hopf-Galois. This article focuses on the cleft case.
  As corings involve bimodules and morphisms of bimodules we extend the Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodule $H$-comodules between cleft extensions on one side and bimodules of $H$-coinvariants equipped with bimodule $H$-measurings compatible with 2-cocycles on the other side. In fact, the correspondences for algebras and for bimodules are parts of a biequivalence of suitable bicategories defined in this article. As a corollary one obtains a correspondence between cleft $H$-extensions of corings and corings equipped with a nonabelian \v{C}ech 1-cocycle covalued in $H$.

papers.title: Linear Stability of Double-Double Orbits in the Equal-Mass Four-Body Problem via Index Theory
papers.abstract: In this paper, using the Maslov-type index theory in symplectic geometry, we study the linear stability of the double-double orbits in the planar equal-mass four body problem. By analyzing its symmetry properties and variational characterization, we clarify the relationship between linear stability and its variational nature on various loop spaces and show that for any rotation angle $\theta=\frac{\pi}{n}$, the retrograde double-double orbits are linearly stable with integer $n\in[3,30]$ and the prograde double-double orbits are linearly stable with integer $n\in[4,30]$. We also give the distributions of the eigenvalues on the unit circle of the monodromy matrices associated with the orbits. The basic idea is as follows: the variational characterization of the orbits provides information about its Morse index; based on its relation to the Maslov-type index, our stability criteria come into play.

papers.title: Global existence for the semilinear regular Euler-Poisson-Darboux-Tricomi equation, II
papers.abstract:
In our previous work [25], we established the global existence of solutions to the semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux-Tricomi equation with power nonlinearity \(|u|^p\) in the case where the damping term dominates the mass term. In contrast, this paper studies the reverse case, namely, the existence of global solutions to the equation when the mass term dominates the damping term.
  We prove that small-data solutions exist globally if \[ p>\max\{p_0((m+1)n,\mu), \widetilde{p}_1(n,m,\mu)\} \] for \(\delta\doteq(\mu-1)^2-4\nu^2\leq0\), where \(\delta\) measures the relative dominance between the damping and mass terms, \(p_0(n,\mu)\) is the \textit{Strauss-related} exponent defined by (1.12), and \(\widetilde{p}_1(n,m,\mu)\) is defined by (2.5).

papers.title: Sharp Brezis--Merle Inequalities for Polyharmonic Dirichlet Problems: Extremal Measures and Critical Asymptotics
papers.authors: Jo\~ao Marcos do \'O, Federica Sani, Victor Rafael Silva
papers.abstract: We establish the Brezis--Merle inequality for very weak solutions of polyharmonic Dirichlet problems with integrable data on smooth bounded domains in conformal dimensions. The inequality is sharp both with respect to the admissible range of the exponent and to the quantity appearing on the right-hand side, which is characterized as the maximum of an associated one-pole Green functional. The supremum defining this quantity is not attained by any integrable datum, but remains unchanged when the admissible class is extended to Radon probability measures; in this enlarged class, the extremals are Dirac masses, and their concentration points are characterized in terms of the associated Green function. On the unit ball, we prove uniqueness of the extremal measure and obtain an explicit optimal bound extending the sharp result for the Laplacian. Finally, we determine the critical asymptotics of the sharp constant on the right-hand side and show that the possible limiting concentration points are selected by the maximum points of the polyharmonic Robin function.

papers.title: Homological branching laws for $p$-adic and mod $p$ representations of ${\rm GL}_2$ over a $p$-adic field
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $p\geq 5$. In this paper, we establish homological branching laws for mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ restricted to split and nonsplit maximal tori, treating principal and special series and, when $F=\mathbb Q_p$, supersingular representations. We determine the derived Hom-complexes in both orders for nonexceptional characters. At exceptional characters, we calculate their Euler--Poincar\'e characteristics under a $p$-torsion-freeness hypothesis. We also establish corresponding results for a class of unitary Banach space representations.

papers.title: Perturbing the Conway sequence
papers.abstract: We study the alternating perturbation of Conway's nested recurrence, $C(n)=C(C(n-1))+C(n-C(n-1))+(-1)^n$ for $n\geq 3$, with $C(1)=C(2)=1$. We prove that the sequence is well defined and satisfies $C(n)=\psi^{-3}n+O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, where $\psi>1$ is the real root of $\psi^3=\psi^2+1$.

papers.title: On the Gauss sphere problem
papers.abstract: In this article we improve Heath-Brown's estimate for the error term in the three-dimensional sphere problem, proving \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}=\frac{4\pi}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{55/42+\varepsilon}). \] Incoporating the recent OpenAI quasi-GRH into our argument further improves this to \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}= \frac{4\pi}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{\frac{2274811}{1743872}+\varepsilon}). \]

papers.title: Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications
papers.authors: Yan Gong, Zheng Chu, Wei Koong Chai, Hari Mohan Pandey, Jingrui Hou, Miao Zhang, Yuanjian Li, Pei Xiao
papers.abstract: Semantic communication jointly optimizes inference accuracy, channel use, and computation, yet the underlying communication program is typically specified before training. This paper presents ComRSI (Communications-Oriented Recursive Self-Improvement), a framework for recursively evolving that program through large-language-model-assisted code edits. A fixed agent modifies the encoder, channel adapters, decoder, loss, and training policy; a protected evaluator screens candidates under prescribed budgets and resource constraints. Accepted code and textual feedback inform subsequent proposals, while candidate weights are trained from scratch. In the original ten-generation CIFAR-100 lineage, eight accepted revisions produce an attention-pooled code achieving 74.3% test accuracy over an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel at 32 complex symbols per image, compared with 67.2% at 256 symbols for the initial design. The program also improves fading-channel accuracy and transfers to Tiny-ImageNet after retraining. A repeat study with ten searches per method compares ComRSI against non-recursive agents with and without textual history. Mean final search scores balancing accuracy, transmission rate, and computational cost are 0.7587, 0.7376, and 0.7089, respectively; the mean numbers of accepted revisions per search are 6.0, 5.0, and 2.1. The advantage over the memoryless agent is supported by a two-sided rank test, whereas the difference from the history-equipped agent remains statistically inconclusive at this sample size. Archived proposals show that pooling can yield a large improvement, while retained history supports subsequent refinement. These results support recursive program optimization within the evaluated setting and expose its remaining rate-robustness and compute-placement trade-offs.

papers.title: Geometrization of continuum mechanics and nonequilibrium thermodynamics: Heat conduction
papers.abstract: We propose a geometric formulation of non-equilibrium heat conduction. It combines the variational (Hamiltonian) structure of symmetric hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (SHTC) equations with the exterior calculus of differential forms. The central object is the thermal impulse one-form on the four-dimensional matter-time manifold. Its time component is the temperature, and for reversible (ballistic) heat transport it is the exact differential of a scalar potential (i.e. it is holonomic). Non-equilibrium effects are described by a second one-form, the small-scale thermal impulse, which is not required to be exact. Its time component is a fluctuating temperature, and its exterior derivative, the four-thermal vorticity, satisfies a Bianchi-type kinematic identity. The variational principle together with this identity yields a non-equilibrium two-temperature model. Its field equations have the same structure as Maxwell's equations in a medium, with the thermal impulse field, the thermal vorticity field and a thermal Poynting vector contributing to the heat flux. Dissipation is introduced through relaxation terms that conserve the total energy and produce entropy. A formal asymptotic analysis shows that, in the relaxation limit, the model reduces to a Guyer-Krumhansl-type heat conduction with independent transverse and longitudinal length scales. The transverse nonlocal term comes from the spatial non-holonomy of the small-scale thermal impulse, while the longitudinal term comes from its non-holonomy in time, i.e. from the relaxation of the fluctuating temperature. We also discuss the gauge-theoretic interpretation of the model. Its kinematics is that of an abelian gauge theory, while the local gauge symmetry is explicitly broken by the existence of two temperatures. Finally, we discuss the consequences of the geometric structure for structure-preserving numerical methods.

papers.title: Wave equation with unbounded terms driven by a stochastic measure
papers.abstract: The one-dimensional wave equation with additive noise driven by a stochastic measure is considered. For the stochastic integrator, we assume only the sigma-additivity in probability and that $|y|^\tau$ is integrable on $\mathbb{R}$ for some $\tau>1/2$. The class of stochastic measures includes many important cases of random processes. In the equation, the stochastic measure depends only on the spatial variable. The existence, uniqueness, and H\"{o}lder regularity of the mild solution are proved. In the previous publications, similar results were obtained for the case of bounded terms of the wave equation driven by a stochastic measure. In our paper, one term may be unbounded, satisfying the linear growth condition. Nevertheless, we prove that the solution is bounded in this case.

papers.title: Connected Coloring Games on Corona Products of Graphs
papers.abstract: We study the connected coloring game on corona products of graphs. For connected graphs $G$ and $H$, we prove the sharp upper bound $\chi_{cg}(G\circ H)\leq\max\{\Delta(G),\Delta(H)+1\}+1$ and establish a further bound using the Bob-start ordinary coloring game on the second factor. We show that the difference between the Alice-start and Bob-start connected game chromatic numbers can be arbitrarily large in either direction. We further prove that a connected subgraph may have arbitrarily larger connected game chromatic number than its ambient connected graph, and that $\chi_{cg}(G\circ H)$ cannot be bounded in terms of $\chi_{cg}(G)$ and $\chi_{cg}(H)$ alone, even when both factors have connected game chromatic number $2$. We also obtain corona products for which the difference $\chi_g-\chi_{cg}$ is arbitrarily large and construct infinitely many connected graphs with $\chi_g<\chi_{cg}$. Finally, for corona products of trees, we prove the universal upper bound $5$, characterize those attaining the value $3$, give structural sufficient conditions for the value $4$, and exhibit a broad family attaining the value $5$.

papers.title: Small and Large Quasi-Kernels in General Digraphs
papers.abstract:
In a digraph $D$, a set $Q$ of vertices is a quasi-kernel if $Q$ is an independent set and every vertex in $D$ can be reached from $Q$ via at most two edges. The small quasi-kernel conjecture by Erd\H{o}s and Sz\'ekely predicts that every source-free $n$-vertex digraph contains a quasi-kernel of size at most $n - n/2$. Chv\'atal and Lov\'asz' 1974 work implies a bound of $n - \sqrt{n}+1$. In 2024, Sprio shows the bound $n - \frac{1}{4} \sqrt{n \log_2 n}$. We show that there always is a quasi-kernel of size at most $n - \frac{1}{51}n^{2/3} / \ln^{2/3}(n)$.
  For the related large quasi-kernel conjecture by Spiro, we show that there always is a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|N^+[Q]| \ge 0.2917 \cdot n^{2/3} / \ln^{2/3}(n)$.

papers.title: On the planar Neumann--Poincar\'e inverse spectral problem
papers.abstract: Does the Neumann--Poincar\'e spectrum determine a planar domain up to an extended M\"obius transformation? We construct a pair showing that the answer is no, even for analytic, strictly convex, algebraic boundaries. Their operators are similar. We then prove a positive result for prescribed finite-dimensional families of normalised exterior conformal maps. For every $m\ge1$, the first $m$ positive eigenvalues determine $m$ real Laurent coefficients on a small truncated convex cone, provided the higher coefficients are a prescribed analytic remainder of quadratic order. Recovery is Lipschitz stable, uniformly down to the disk. The proof combines the Grunsky representation with a nondegeneracy argument for weighted Hankel matrices and differentiated perturbation estimates. Explicit two- and three-parameter examples, single-mode families with repeated leading eigenvalues, and M\"obius equivalence classes illustrate the result. Direct proofs for complete polarization data show what spectral weights add to the eigenvalues.

papers.title: Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{\xi\in \mathbb F_q^d:\xi_1^2+\cdots+\xi_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, d\sigma)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $\eta_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $\eta_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.

papers.title: Parameters Robust Parallelizable Iterative Decoupled Algorithms for Thermo-Poroelasticity with Nonlinear Convective Transport
papers.abstract: This paper presents several parallel iterative algorithms for the nonlinear thermo-poroelasticity. We introduce an auxiliary variable to transform the original model into a four-field formulation to overcome Poisson locking. The iterative idea is extended to linearize and decouple the four-field model. Different coupling strategies are employed among these three subproblems, combined with appropriately designed iteration settings, yielding distinct iterative parallel algorithms. Stabilization terms are incorporated into these algorithms to ensure parameter robustness in extreme situations. We derive error estimates and prove the convergence of these parallel iterative decoupled algorithms. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to compare the performance of the different parallel algorithms in extreme parameter settings, thereby validating their efficiency and robustness.

papers.title: Restriction of $p'$-degree characters, fields of values, and relative normal complements
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group for a prime $p$, and let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Centella and Navarro proved that there is a canonical bijection ${\rm Irr}_{p'}(\Phi_{1_G})\to{\rm Irr}_{p'}(\Phi_{1_{\textbf N_G(P)}})$ preserving fields of values, where $\Phi_{1_G}$ denotes the principal projective indecomposable character of $G$. In the spirit of a result of Berkovich on the McKay bijection, we characterize when this projective correspondence can be realized by restriction, proving that it holds if and only if $\mathbf{N}_G(P)$ admits a certain relative normal complement in $G$. More generally, we establish a refined criterion incorporating fields of values, and we extend this characterization to $\pi$-separable groups with nilpotent Hall $\pi$-subgroups.

papers.title: Numerical Shadow Rigidity for 3x3 Matrices
papers.abstract: The numerical shadow of a complex matrix is the measure obtained by pushing forward that Haar measure on the unit sphere in $\mathbb{C}^n$ by the numerical range map. By the choice of measure, unitary equivalence implies same measure, but the reverse is not true for $n\geq 3$. We name a matrix $\textbf{shadow rigid}$ it its unitary equivalence class and shadow equivalence class coincide. It is known that normal matrices are rigid, but the topic has not been explored beyond this in the literature. The main result of the paper is showing that in the $n=3$ case, a matrix is rigid if and only if it is non-generic. We also show that rigidity is preserved under an affine group action and present three normal-like properties of $3\times 3$ non-generic matrices.

papers.title: Optimally Emulating Smooth Functions for Bayesian Analyses
papers.authors: Scott Pratt, Oleh Savchuk, Eren Erdogan, Ekaksh Kataria, Christal Martin, Syed Afrid Jahan, Frederi Viens
papers.abstract: For Bayesian analyses aimed at constraining the parameter space of computationally expensive models by comparison with heterogeneous data sets, model emulators play a pivotal role. Model emulators enable searches through high-dimensional parameter spaces, searches which might otherwise require millions of full model runs. Here, an emulation strategy is presented based on the assumption that the model output can be well described by a polynomial expansion with all terms being independent of one another and with higher order terms being given decreasing weights according to a convergence parameter. It is found that if the expansion's form is constrained to being invariant to rotation and translation of the parameter space that the polynomial form becomes equivalent to that of a Gaussian process emulator using a correlation kernel with a Gaussian form. In the limit that the function is smooth, quantified by a convergence parameter, $\Lambda$, it is found that rather few training points are required to reproduce the full model and provide a good estimate of its uncertainty. An accuracy metric is defined based on an average of the expected uncertainty over the prior before training data are actually gathered. Analytic expressions for the expected accuracy are provided based solely on an expected value of $\Lambda$ and the location of the training points. This enables a tenable optimized placement of training points, which is shown to be significantly superior to random placement or that from Latin hyper-cube sampling. Examples of optimized placement are provided, and the accuracy is studied as a function of various variables, such as the number of model parameters, the number of training points, and the convergence parameter.

papers.title: Discrete homotopy of graphs and $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements
papers.abstract: Discrete homotopy theory is a combinatorial homotopy theory defined for discrete objects. Barcelo--Severs--White conjectured that the homotopy groups of complements of $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements are isomorphic to the discrete homotopy groups of graphs associated with the Coxeter complexes. We show that this correspondence fails in general by giving a counterexample in degree two for the $4$-parabolic subspace arrangement of type $A_5$.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of logarithmic connections associated with difference Painlev\'e equations of type $E^{(1)}_n$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit correspondence between moduli spaces of parabolic logarithmic connections on the projective line with spectral type $(2^2,1^4,1^4)$ and $(3^2, 2^3, 1^6)$, and the spaces of initial conditions for difference Painlev\'e equations with symmetry of type $E^{(1)}_7$ and $E^{(1)}_8$, respectively. Furthermore, we realize the extended affine Weyl group symmetries of the space of initial conditions in terms of connections.

papers.title: S-PASS: Star-Topology Pinching-Antenna Systems with Pipelined Antenna Pre-Positioning
papers.abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) flexibly reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide near each user. Releasing and re-attaching an antenna, however, is a mechanical operation orders of magnitude slower than electronic switching, wasting much transmission time. Existing designs generally assume instant reconfiguration, neglect the mechanical latency, or keep the antenna fixed. This paper proposes S-PASS, a star architecture of waveguides sharing one radio-frequency chain through a switch, and pipelined antenna pre-positioning (PAP), a time-division protocol in which idle waveguides pre-position their antennas for their next users while one transmits. It derives in closed form the scheduling efficiency, the number of waveguides beyond which the latency costs no transmission time, and the latency up to which PAP outperforms fixed placement. Analytical and numerical results show that this latency grows with each added waveguide, and users at the outer ends of the waveguides gain most.

papers.title: Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
papers.authors: Zakaria Fattah, Ilias Ftouhi, Giorgio Saracco
papers.abstract: We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. We also establish an explicit reparametrization law, by which, for nonnegative times, the profile of the regularized body is determined by that of the initial one, and the order of profiles of bodies of equal area is preserved. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.

papers.title: Property (R) with its stability for analytic functional system and under compact perturbations
papers.authors: Sinan Qiu, Lining Jiang, Xiaomin Wei
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{F}_T$ be the analytic functional system generated by a linear bounded operator $T$ on an infinite dimensional complex Hilbert space.
  This paper characterizes the stability of property (R), a variant of Weyl's theorem, for $\mathcal{F}_T$ and under compact perturbations in terms of the spectrum on consistency in Weyl. In particular, the stability of property (R) under compact perturbations is shown to imply the (R)-stability of $\mathcal{F}_T$.

papers.title: On unit groups of purely infinite rings
papers.abstract: We prove that the unit group of any purely infinite, regular, right self-injective ring admits a universal sequence of words (thus has strong distortion), is minimally almost periodic, has finite involution width, is verbally simple and verbally elliptic, and has uncountable uniform strong cofinality. These findings are consequences of more refined structural results, some of which provide concrete cardinal estimates involving the Goodearl--Boyle dimension of the ring. A central ingredient in our results is a comprehensive study of bounded normal generation, in particular with respect to certain classes of involutions. Along the way, we develop some abstract methods and concepts pertaining to geometric group theory.

papers.title: Will AI kill us all---or just make mathematicians obsolete?
papers.abstract: AI's recent advances have fueled predictions of human intellectual obsolescence and fears for the future of mathematics. I argue that, impressive as these achievements are, they do not establish AI's capacity to invent new concepts and theories or sustain autonomous recursive self-improvement. Human intelligence also involves judgment, imagination, and embodied experience that standard measures fail to capture. Mathematics extends beyond proving theorems: its creative core lies in conceptual discovery and understanding. AI can strengthen this enterprise, but realizing its promise requires protecting attribution, open exchange, confidentiality, and mathematical training. I propose an academic AI consortium to provide powerful research tools with enforceable guarantees safeguarding unpublished ideas.

papers.title: Higher rank spectral projector estimates and a Stein--Tomas restriction theorem
papers.authors: Phillip Harris, Jiaqi Hou, Xiaoqi Huang
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact locally symmetric space of noncompact type. We prove sharp upper bounds for the $L^2\to L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for joint eigenfunctions of the full ring of invariant differential operators on $X$. This improves the corresponding result of Marshall, by removing a logarithmic power loss at the critical exponent. Using the same method, we also prove the endpoint case of Mockenhaupt's $(L^2,L^p)$ Fourier restriction theorem.

papers.title: Accelerated primal-dual dynamics and algorithms for strongly convex-concave bilinear saddle point problems
papers.authors: Yun-xi Zhang, Yi-bin Xiao, Xin He
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop accelerated primal-dual dynamics and algorithms for strongly convex-concave saddle point problems with bilinear coupling. Combining strongly convex Nesterov dynamics with scaled heavy-ball dynamics, we propose a second-order primal-dual dynamical system with constant damping and derive an associated algorithm by time discretization and coefficient adjustment. Under suitable conditions on the continuous scaling function $\beta(t)$ and the discrete scaling sequence $\beta_k$, we establish primal-dual gap estimates of $\mathcal O(1/\beta(t))$ in continuous time and $\mathcal O(1/\beta_k)$ in discrete time. The maximal admissible growth rates of these scales recover the exponential and linear convergence rates of strongly convex Nesterov methods in continuous and discrete time, respectively. We also prove convergence of the primal-dual trajectory and sequence, even when the dual solution is nonunique. Saddle residual estimates of $\mathcal O(1/\sqrt{\beta(t)})$ and $\mathcal O(1/\sqrt{\beta_k})$ hold under globally Lipschitz gradients in continuous time and with a possibly nonsmooth dual potential in discrete time. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and the performance of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Model Predictive Control: Systematic Design Tailored to Nonholonomic Systems
papers.authors: Emilia F. P.
