In that way, and without changing the general categorical infrastructure of coherent differentiation, this theory accommodates new notions of ''differentiation'' of which we describe several instances. Among many others, such notions include various forms of finite differences as well as Taylor expansion truncated at any fixed degree, and finite Taylor expansion of a fixed finite degree with a remainder.

papers.title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
papers.authors: Juan Diego Toscano, Sascha Ranft, Zhiwei Gao, Li-Lian Wang, George Em Karniadakis
papers.abstract: Machine-learning surrogates in computational science often require not only accurate predictions but also expectations, variances, conserved integrals, and normalization constants. Conventional neural networks, including Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs), generally evaluate these quantities through Monte Carlo sampling or multidimensional quadrature, making repeated inference costly, particularly in high dimensions. We introduce KANs with Tractable Operators for Uncertainty and Constraints (TOUCKANs), whose finite-degree polynomial outer functions yield a decomposable sum--product representation. Under factorizing input measures, expectations and higher moments then reduce algebraically to deterministic recursions over one-dimensional leaf integrals. Independent and shared inner-block variants form a parameter-efficiency hierarchy, and a universal-approximation proof for its most restricted member extends to the complete class. The same deterministic operators allow conserved integrals and normalization to be imposed throughout training. Across uniform and Gaussian benchmarks through 50 dimensions, deterministic mean and variance errors remained below the median fixed-budget Monte Carlo errors in every case. TOUCKANs also conserved Cahn--Hilliard mass to machine precision and imposed normalization and orthogonality through deterministic moments, enabling joint computation of the lowest four Schr\"odinger eigenpairs in two, three, and five dimensions. TOUCKANs therefore connect KAN approximation with tractable probabilistic circuits, making statistical operators and integral constraints directly available within an expressive neural surrogate.

papers.title: Preventing Model Extraction in Contextual Linear Optimization
papers.authors: Adam N. Elmachtoub, Tianyi Lin, Wenxuan Liu
papers.abstract: Consider a contextual linear optimization problem, where a predict-then-optimize (PTO) system returns optimal decisions without revealing the cost vectors used in its downstream linear program. Our focus is on how to prevent attackers, who can submit context queries, from extracting the underlying prediction model. Although the cost-to-decision map is many-to-one, observations across contexts can reveal the underlying prediction model. For linear models, we provide sufficient conditions where the attacker can learn the model up to positive scaling by only observing the decision. These conditions motivate an adaptive attack that alternates inverse optimization with boundary sampling, i.e., using context queries leading to decision boundaries of the current attacker model. To prevent extraction, we propose a mechanism that perturbs decisions only when the predicted cost vector is near a decision boundary. We establish a regret bound in terms of the perturbation radius. For the attackers that fit the defended responses as optimal decisions under the evaluation distribution, we also prove a lower bound on expected extraction error. Experiments on synthetic instances and real data quantify the security-performance trade-off of the defense mechanism and illustrate that our defense can increase the extraction error.

papers.title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
papers.authors: Xi He, Chao Zhang, Shilin Huang, Bei Zeng
papers.abstract: We establish that transversal diagonal gates on exact qubit codes of distance at least two can be exhaustively classified within a finite search space. Although code-preserving physical gates can have continuous phases, any projective logical action induced by a transversal diagonal gate can always be realized by a physical gate of finite order. Crucially, we prove that this physical order has an upper bound determined solely by the code parameters. This order bound enables the subset-sum-linear-programming (SSLP) framework introduced in arXiv:2504.20847 to exhaustively enumerate all candidate discrete symmetries, after which the Knill-Laflamme equations determine the remaining continuous code parameters. Applying this method to the nontrivial diagonal sector of exact $((6,2,3))$ codes, SSLP yields $66$ candidate symmetry classes, of which exactly $15$ are realizable, supporting full projective diagonal logical cyclic groups of orders $2$, $3$, and $5$. In particular, for order $5$, the code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations, equivalent to the code constructed in arXiv:2504.20847. This code also attains the minimum length $n=6$ among exact $((n, 2, \ge 3))$ codes whose full projective transversal group cannot be conjugated into the projective Clifford group.

papers.title: Relative geometry of nuclear mean fields through differential forms
papers.abstract: Proton and neutron densities can have similar multipole moments while differing locally. We use differential forms to measure and locate such differences between nuclear mean fields. A pair invariant measures the angle between two density gradients, weighted by their magnitudes, and the coarea formula resolves its contribution over level surfaces. A triple invariant factorizes exactly into a weighted pair term and a directional term that measures the variation of a third field along the level-surface intersections. We test these quantities in 98 magnetized Wigner-Seitz solutions, five static Hartree-Fock configurations, an illustrative $^{16}$O + $^{34}$Mg collision, and periodic nuclear pasta (a slab and a connected network). The pair invariant distinguishes cell solutions with comparable proton quadrupole moments and is 253 times larger in $^{34}$Mg than in $^{24}$Mg; refinement to 0.6 fm changes it by at most 1.3% in the four configurations recomputed. The directional factor separates the sampled triaxial configurations from the prolate ones. In the collision, it accounts for the 7.3-fold rise of the triple before the first recorded low-density connection, while the weighted pair term changes by at most 3%. In nuclear pasta, slab and network configurations have similar integrated proton-neutron misalignment but different distributions over density levels; their triple invariants differ by a factor of about 370 on the finer grid, mainly due to the variation of the Coulomb potential along joint density levels. These comparisons require no preferred origin or axis. A resolved nonzero triple excludes a common symmetry axis, but zero does not establish one. The pasta results require further convergence studies.

papers.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: exposition and barriers
papers.authors: Alimzhan Amanov, Maxim van den Berg, Jeroen Zuiddam
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that the exponent $\omega_\mathbb{C}$ of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers satisfies $\omega_\mathbb{C}\leq9/4$. Our version of the proof gives $\omega_\mathbb{F}\leq9/4$ over every field $\mathbb{F}$. We also treat the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$. Here we have $\omega_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)=2$ for $0\leq k\leq1/2$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)\leq1+k+1/(4k)$ for $k\geq1/2$, and, for real numbers $a\geq b\geq c\geq0$, $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)=a+b$ if $c(a+b)\leq ab$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)\leq(a+b+c)/2+(ab/c+ac/b+bc/a)/4$ otherwise. Our exposition is in the language of degeneration inequalities among polynomial multiplication tensors and Strassen's asymptotic spectrum duality. We moreover prove an operational barrier (which can be thought of as coming from an operational asymptotic spectrum) showing that the current analysis of all these upper bounds on $\omega_\mathbb{F}$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$ is optimal and that in fact the current degeneration ingredients cannot improve the bounds.

papers.title: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
papers.authors: Hanmin Li, Yury Demidovich, Peter Richt\'arik
papers.abstract: Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. Independent sets certify compatible edits whose verified gains, measured against the same current solution, add exactly. A coordinator constructs a safe compatible candidate and can also evaluate interacting edits to capture favorable interactions. We prove that an optimal fractional coloring yields a merger that preserves a $1/\chi_f(G)$ fraction of the total verified local improvement, where $\chi_f(G)$ is the graph's fractional chromatic number. This guarantee is tight among mergers that select a subset of the same proposals. Under conditional local-improvement guarantees and a block error-bound condition, repeated collaboration converges geometrically in the objective gap. The rate separates task structure, agent allocation, and computation cost, yielding a linear program for agent assignment and an explicit time-cost trade-off. Code-repair experiments show that verified merging resolves conflicts between individually useful edits that cause naive merging to fail. On larger conflict-free tasks, parallel agents reduce modeled completion time at higher input-token-equivalent cost. On three public road networks, fractional integration retains 922 units of verified graph-cut improvement across 90 paired runs. For route-search agents sharing exclusive access to vehicle routes, fractional scheduling reduces measured wall time by a median of 15% across twelve paired runs, with route-cost changes varying across runs.

papers.title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
papers.abstract: We prove a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for bounded functions of a regenerative process with independent, identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length. The bound uses observed cycle lengths and retains explicit terms for truncation and the cycle ending after the observation horizon. Selecting a tuning parameter from a finite deterministic collection gives a version of Bernstein inequality where all terms are empirical but one, related to the tails of the regeneration times. We then study this term in many regimes: it turns out that it is of second-order in many cases of interest. This is important for applications in machine learning: we prove generalization error bounds for classification with non-i.i.d., regenerative data. These bounds can be used to define learning objectives: by minimizing the first-order term only in the bound, we define agnostic classifiers that still satisfy oracle inequalities. We also show that the bound on the average deviation provided by our results is minimax-optimal in the sample size and in the expected regeneration time. Finally, we combine the Bernstein inequality with a regenerative strong approximation to obtain a Gaussian approximation using an observable block variance estimator.

papers.title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
papers.abstract: We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.

papers.title: Temporal Exploration and Rendezvous via Weisfeiler-Leman Colorings
papers.authors: Frank Kammer, Sandra Kiefer, Johannes Meintrup
papers.abstract:
Temporal graphs are graphs whose edge relation changes in discrete time steps. The Temporal Exploration Problem (TEXP) asks for a temporal walk that visits all vertices. We show that every connected temporal graph with $n$ vertices can be explored in $O(qn\log^3(n))$ time steps, where $q$ is the number of vertex color classes induced by the 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman (2-WL) coloring. For small $q$, our bound substantially improves on the known worst-case bound of $\Theta(n^2)$ in general connected temporal graphs. A corresponding walk can be constructed in deterministic polynomial time. The upper bound is complemented by lower bounds of $\Omega(n\log(n))$ when $q$ is constant and $\Omega(qn)$ when $1 \leq q \leq n$.
  We also apply our techniques to the Temporal Rendezvous Problem (TRP), in which two agents that do not communicate have to meet on a vertex of the temporal graph. Our exploration algorithm yields that, with only polynomial-time computational power, the agents can meet in $O(n\log^3(n))$ time steps, leaving a gap of only $\log^2(n)$ to the known lower bound.
  Dogeas, Erlebach, Kammer, Meintrup, and Moses Jr. [ICALP'24] have shown an $O(rn^{1+\epsilon})$ bound for TEXP, for every fixed $\epsilon > 0$, where $r$ is the number of orbits, and an $O(n^{1+\epsilon})$ bound for TRP. Both results require superpolynomial computation time. Our contribution improves upon these results in several ways. First, the dependence on $n$ in the upper bounds on the number of time steps is decreased from $n^{1+\epsilon}$ to $n\log^3(n)$ for both TEXP and TRP. Second, for TEXP, we bound the number of time steps linearly by the parameter q, which is efficiently computable and upper bounded by $r$. Third, we provide novel deterministic polynomial-time algorithms for both TEXP and TRP.

papers.title: $\delta$-superderivations of simple finite-dimensional Jordan and Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We introduce the concept of a $\delta$-superderivation of a superalgebra. $\delta$-Derivations of Cartan-type Lie superalgebras are treated, as well as $\delta$-superderivations of simple finite-dimensional Lie superalgebras and Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. We give a complete description of $\{1}{2}$-derivations for Cartan-type Lie superalgebras. It is proved that nontrivial $\delta$-(super)derivations are missing on the given classes of superalgebras, and as a consequence, $\delta$-superderivations are shown to be trivial on simple finite-dimensional noncommutative Jordan superalgebras of degree at least 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. Also we consider $\delta$-derivations of unital flexible and semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan algebras over a field of characteristic not 2.

papers.title: $\delta$-derivations of classical Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We consider the $\delta$-derivations of classical Lie superalgebras and prove that these superalgebras admit nonzero $\delta$-derivations only when $\delta = 0,1/2,1$. The structure of $1/2$-derivations for classical Lie superalgebras is completely determined.

papers.title: Convergence of solutions to the $p$-Laplace evolution equation as $p$ goes to 1
papers.abstract: We prove that the set of solutions to the parabolic singular $p$-Laplace equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ for all space dimensions is continuous in the parameter $p\in [1,+\infty)$ and the initial data. The highly singular limit case $p=1$ is included. In particular, we show that the solutions $u_p$ converge strongly in $L^2(\Omega)$, uniformly in time, to the solution $u_1$ of the parabolic $1$-Laplace equation as $p\to 1$.

papers.title: On $\delta$-superderivations of simple superalgebras of Jordan brackets
papers.abstract: A complete description of $\delta$-derivations and $\delta$-superderivations is given for simple unital superalgebras of Jordan brackets over a field of characteristic different from~$2$ \textup{(}and, for the odd $\delta$-superderivations, different from~$3$; see Remark~A for characteristic~$3$\textup{)} and for simple unital finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\neq2$ \textup{(}with the corrections of Remarks~A and~C for $p>2$\textup{)}. As a consequence, a criterion for simple unital superalgebras of Jordan brackets to be special is obtained.

papers.title: Complex zero strip decreasing operators
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the effect of linear differential operators coming from the Laguerre-Polya class that act on functions in the extended Laguerre-Polya class with zeros in a horizontal strip in the complex plane. These operator decrease the size of the strip containing the zeros.

papers.title: Subclass of bi-univalent function associated to Chebyshev polynomial
papers.authors: G. M. Birajdar, N. D. Sangle
papers.abstract: The Chebyshev polynomials are utilized in this study to define the subclass of the bi-univalent function. Also, Chebyshev polynomial bounds and Fekete-Szego inequalities for functions defined in the classes are established.

papers.title: On the modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we establish the modularity of every elliptic curve $E/F$, where $F$ runs over infinitely many imaginary quadratic fields, including $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$ for $d=1,2,3,5$. More precisely, let $F$ be imaginary quadratic and assume that the modular curve $X_0(15)$, which is an elliptic curve of rank $0$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, also has rank $0$ over $F$. Then we prove that all elliptic curves over $F$ are modular. More generally, when $F/\mathbb{Q}$ is an imaginary CM field that does not contain a primitive fifth root of unity, we prove the modularity of elliptic curves $E/F$ under a technical assumption on the image of the representation of $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{F}/F)$ on $E[3]$ or $E[5]$.
  The key new technical ingredient we use is a local-global compatibility theorem for the $p$-adic Galois representations associated to torsion in the cohomology of the relevant locally symmetric spaces. We establish this result in the crystalline case, under some technical assumptions, but allowing arbitrary dimension, arbitrarily large regular Hodge--Tate weights, and allowing $p$ to be small and highly ramified in the imaginary CM field $F$.

papers.title: Supermodular Rank: Set Function Decomposition and Optimization
papers.authors: Rishi Sonthalia, Anna Seigal, Guido Montufar
papers.abstract: We define the supermodular rank of a function on a lattice. This is the smallest number of terms needed to decompose it into a sum of supermodular functions. The supermodular summands are defined with respect to different partial orders. We characterize the maximum possible value of the supermodular rank and describe the functions with fixed supermodular rank. We analogously define the submodular rank. We use submodular decompositions to optimize set functions. Given a bound on the submodular rank of a set function, we formulate an algorithm that splits an optimization problem into submodular subproblems. We show that this method improves the approximation ratio guarantees of several algorithms for monotone set function maximization and ratio of set functions minimization, at a computation overhead that depends on the submodular rank.

papers.title: The maximum distance covariance of bounded random vectors
papers.abstract: A sharp upper bound is obtained for the distance covariance of bounded random vectors in terms of the diameters of their supports alone. The bound is attained for all pairs of support diameter constraints and hence provides the maximum distance covariance subject to constraints of this kind. A normalized measure of dependence is derived by dividing distance covariance by the sharp bound when it is positive. Several properties of the resulting quotient are proved, including domination by distance correlation, invariance under similarities, and subadditivity under sums of independent pairs. The quotient is shown to be nonincreasing under the addition of independent noise, a property not shared by distance correlation. The usual sample distance covariance inherits the sharp bound from the population quantity and the associated normalized statistic is strongly consistent.

papers.title: Spectral mod p Satake isomorphism for GL_n
papers.abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension with residue field $k$. By a work of Emerton--Gee, irreducible components inside the reduced special fiber of the moduli stack of rank $n$ \'etale $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules are labeled by Serre weights of $\mathrm{GL}_n(k)$. Let $\sigma$ be a non-Steinberg Serre weight and $\mathcal{C}_\sigma$ be the corresponding irreducible component. Motivated by the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands program, we construct a natural injective map $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{C}_\sigma) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{H}(\sigma)$ from the ring of global functions on $\mathcal{C}_\sigma$ to the Hecke algebra of $\sigma$ compatible with the mod $p$ Satake isomorphism by Herzig and Henniart--Vign\'eras in a suitable sense. For sufficiently generic $\sigma$, we prove that it is an isomorphism. As an application, we obtain a natural stratification of the irreducible component whose strata are equipped with a parabolic structure. Our main input is a construction of a morphism from an integral Hecke algebra of a generic tame type to the ring of global functions on a tamely potentially crystalline Emerton--Gee stack.

papers.title: Extreme change-point detection
papers.abstract: We examine rules for predicting whether a point in $\mathbb{R}$ generated from a 50-50 mixture of two different probability distributions came from one distribution or the other, given limited (or no) information on the two distributions, and, as clues, one point generated randomly from each of the two distributions. We prove that nearest-neighbor prediction does better than chance when we know the two distributions are Gaussian densities without knowing their parameter values. We conjecture that this result holds for general probability distributions and, furthermore, that the nearest-neighbor rule is optimal in this setting, i.e., no other rule can do better than it if we do not know the distributions or do not know their parameters, or both.

papers.title: Port-Hamiltonian systems with energy and power ports
papers.authors: Kaja Krhac, Bernhard Maschke, Arjan van der Schaft
papers.abstract: We extend the port-Hamiltonian framework defined with respect to a Lagrangian submanifold and a Dirac structure by augmenting the Lagrangian submanifold with the space of external variables. The new pair of conjugated variables is called energy port. We show that in the most general case, the extension describes constrained Hamiltonian systems whose Hamiltonian function depends on inputs.

papers.title: Spherical growth of reciprocal classes in the Hecke Groups
papers.abstract:
Let $\Gamma_p$ denote the Hecke group where $p=2r$, $r>0$. Let $\mathcal{N}_l$ denote the set of conjugacy classes of reciprocal elements of word length $l$ in $\Gamma_p$. We prove that for $l \to \infty$,
  $$|\mathcal{N}_l| = \mathcal{O}\left(\left\lfloor \tfrac{l+1}{2} \right\rfloor^{s-1} \rho^{\left\lfloor \tfrac{l+1}{2} \right\rfloor} \right),
  $$
  where $\mathcal O$ is the `big O', $\rho \in [\sqrt{2}, 2]$ is the unique positive real root of
  $$
  p(x) = x^{r+1} - 2\sum_{j=1}^{r-1} x^{r-j} - 1,
  $$
  and $s$ is the maximal multiplicity among the roots of $p(x)$.
  Our method relies on the free product structure of the Hecke group $\Gamma_p$, a combinatorial counting function, and recurrence relations derived from cyclically reduced representatives. We also derive that the growth rate of the primitive reciprocal classes of word length $l$ is in agreement with that of $\mathcal{N}_l$. This work generalizes previous results for odd $p$ and provides an explicit asymptotic bound for all Hecke groups.

papers.title: Complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for positive $(p,p)$-forms on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: A complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for differential $(p,p)$-forms is introduced on compact K\"ahler manifolds. For any $1 \leq p < n$, we show the existence of smooth solutions unique up to adding constants. For $p=1$, this corresponds to the Calabi-Yau theorem proved by S. T. Yau, and for $p=n-1$, this gives the Monge-Amp\`ere equation for $(n-1)$ plurisubharmonic functions studied by Tosatti-Weinkove. For other $p$ values, this defines a non-linear PDE that falls outside of the general framework of Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck. Further, we define a geometric flow for higher-order forms that extends the K\"ahler-Ricci flow naturally to $(p,p)$-forms. As a consequence of our main theorem, we show that this flow exists in a maximal time interval and can be shown to converge under some assumptions. A modified flow is introduced and the convergence of the associated normalized flow is shown.

papers.title: Partial actions of groups on monoidal categories
papers.authors: Eliezer Batista, Felipe Lopes Castro, Mykola Khrypchenko
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce the notion of a partial action of a group on a strict monoidal category. We propose, in the context of Monoidal categories, new constructions analogous to those existing for partial group actions over an algebra such as the globalization, the subalgebra of partial invariants, and the partial smash product.

papers.title: Normal forms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras and Landau-Lifshitz type of equations
papers.abstract: We present normal forms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras with dihedral symmetry of order 4, which arise naturally in the context of Landau-Lifshitz type of equations. These normal forms provide a transparent description and allow a classification of such Lie algebras over $\mathbb{C}$. Using this perspective, we show that a Lie algebra introduced by Uglov, as well as the hidden symmetry algebra of the Landau-Lifshitz equation introduced by Holod, can each be realised as an elliptic $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$-current algebra. Furthermore, we realise the Wahlquist-Estabrook algebra of the Landau-Lifshitz equation in terms of elliptic automorphic Lie algebras. This construction reveals that, as a complex Lie algebra, it is isomorphic to the direct sum of an $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$-current algebra and the two-dimensional abelian Lie algebra $\mathbb{C}^2$. Finally, we apply the automorphic Lie algebra framework to an $n$-component generalisation of the Landau-Lifshitz equation due to Golubchik and Sokolov in the case $n=3$.

papers.title: On Dependence Measures Based on $f$-Divergence and $\Phi$-Entropy
papers.abstract:
We study dependence measures induced by $\Phi$-divergence (also known as $ f$-divergence in the literature) for finite random variables. We define conditional $\Phi$-mutual information through an exact chain rule and develop its structural properties and variational representations. But in general it lacks conditional symmetry and deterministic self-reduction. To tackle this, we introduce max-$\Phi$-mutual information $\wIPhi$, a variational envelope obtained by optimizing over $\IPhi$ quantities containing auxiliary random variables, which restores both properties and satisfies a subadditive chain rule. Both quantities reduce to Shannon's mutual information when $\Phi(t)=t\log t$. For smooth convex generators with $\Phi(0)<\infty$ and concave $t\mapsto t^2\Phi''(t)$, we establish an optimizer characterization and obtain a closed-form expression for the unconditional quantity in terms of $\Phi$-self-information. For the same class, we show that its private-randomness-assisted version is either an affine function of Shannon's mutual information, with coefficients depending only on $\Phi$, or identically infinite. This dichotomy is determined by the asymptotic growth of $\Phi$ and clarifies the sensitivity of max-$\Phi$-mutual information to local randomness.
  We further derive inner bounds on $\Phi$-ribbons from prescribed independence structures and prove that these bounds are optimal when $\Phi(t)=t\log t$. We also establish a multipartite $\Phi$-generalization of the Zhang--Yeung inequality and derive corresponding ribbon regions. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for reducing the computation of $\Phi$-strong data processing constants for Z-channel sources to a boundary optimization.

papers.title: Existence and Smoothing for a Nondivergence-Form Degenerate Diffusion from Plasma-Wave Theory
papers.authors: William Porteous, Irene M. Gamba, Kun Huang
papers.abstract: We prove existence and positive-time smoothing of weak solutions to the degenerate parabolic Cauchy--Dirichlet problem $\partial_t u = \rho_\lambda(x)u\,\partial_x^2 u + \rho_\lambda(x)g(x)u$ on the half-line, where $\rho_\lambda$ vanishes at the boundary and grows at infinity. This scalar problem arises from a formal reduction of the one-dimensional quasilinear system for plasma waves, which couples an electron distribution to a wave-energy spectrum: we develop a solution theory for the scalar problem that lifts to this system. For the scalar problem, we construct nonnegative weak solutions under weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data and boundedness of the reaction coefficient $\rho_\lambda g$, admitting unbounded and discontinuous data pertinent to the physical model. We establish a one-sided bound on $\partial_t u$ which yields positive-time smoothing: solutions become locally H\"older continuous in both space and time and locally Lipschitz continuous in space. Explicit examples show that this spatial regularity is sharp. Under natural assumptions on the initial data, our scalar solutions lift to weak solutions of the particle--wave system that preserve nonnegativity, conserve particle mass, smooth initial particle measures to locally bounded densities at positive times, and exhibit quantitative decay of the wave spectrum at large wavenumber.

papers.title: Normal approximation for subgraph counts in random intersection graphs: the case of edges
papers.abstract: We investigate the subgraph count in the random intersection graph model $\mathcal G(n,m,p)$. Due to substantial edge dependencies, studying even such fundamental statistics is significantly more challenging than in the classical binomial model $\mathcal G(n,p)$. This article establish new normal approximation bounds in both the Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances for general non-degenerate $U$-statistics. We then illustrate how these results can be potentially applied to the standardized number of subgraphs in the random intersection graph model. Finally, as a basic example, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic normality of the number of edges in $\mathcal G(n,m,p)$.

papers.title: An Inexact Variable Metric Proximal Gradient-subgradient Algorithm for a Class of Fractional Optimization Problems
papers.authors: Lei Yang, Xiangrui Kong, Min Zhang, Yaohua Hu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of fractional optimization problems, in which the numerator of the objective is the sum of a convex function and a differentiable function with a Lipschitz continuous gradient, while the denominator is a nonsmooth convex function. This model captures ratio-type formulations arising in sparse learning and related applications. To address this class of problems, we propose an inexact variable metric proximal gradient-subgradient algorithm (iVPGSA), which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first inexact proximal algorithm specifically designed for such type of fractional problems. By incorporating a variable metric proximal term and allowing for approximate subproblem solutions under a flexible error criterion, the proposed algorithm is highly adaptable to a broader range of problems while achieving favorable computational efficiency. Under suitable assumptions, we establish that any accumulation point of the generated sequence is a critical point of the target problem. Moreover, we develop a Kurdyka-{\L}ojasiewicz (KL)-based analysis framework, relying only on the classical KL property and its associated exponent, to prove the global convergence of the entire sequence and characterize its convergence rate, \textit{without} requiring a strict sufficient descent property. Our results clarify how the classical KL exponent and inexactness jointly influence the convergence rate. Finally, numerical experiments on the $\ell_1/\ell_2$ Lasso problem and the constrained $\ell_1/\ell_2$ sparse optimization problem demonstrate the computational advantages of the iVPGSA over existing representative algorithms.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Plane Curves defined from Chebychev polynomials
papers.abstract: For any $d\geq 4$ we determine the automorphism groups of the algebraic curves \[ \mathcal{C}_d : y^d = \varphi_d(x), \] where $\varphi_d(x)$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of degree $d$, defined over a field $k$ with $p:=\operatorname{char}(k) \nmid 2d$. For $d>4$, it is $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, except when $2d=p^r+1$ or $4d=p^r+1$ for some $r\geq 1$. In these cases it is, respectively, $(\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z})\rtimes S_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times S_3$. Two ingredients used here are a description of all total inflection points on $\cC_d$, and knowledge of the group of fractional linear transformations that preserve the set of zeros of $\varphi_d$.

papers.title: On electrostatic manifolds with boundary
papers.abstract: Static manifolds with boundary were recently introduced in the context of the problem of prescribing both the scalar curvature of a Riemannian manifold and the mean curvature of its boundary. These manifolds are also of interest from the perspective of general relativity. In this article, we introduce electrostatic manifolds with boundary as a natural generalization of static manifolds with boundary in the presence of a nonzero electric field. We also introduce Robin electrostatic quadruples, extending the notion of Robin static triples previously introduced by the second author. We establish several uniqueness theorems for suitable regions of the Reissner-Nordstr\"om manifold. Finally, we characterize the criticality of the first eigenvalue of an associated mixed Robin-Dirichlet Schr\"odinger operator under admissible volume-preserving variations in terms of the equality of the surface gravities along the Dirichlet boundary components.

papers.title: Non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics of two summands
papers.abstract: We prove the non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics on a class of compact manifolds arising as double disk bundles, whose principal orbits split into two inequivalent irreducible summands. The proof uses a phase space barrier argument that yields a new obstruction to the existence of closed cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics, even when the principal orbits admit homogeneous Einstein metrics.

papers.title: $SU(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs functional with Higgs self-interaction on $3$-manifolds
papers.authors: Da Rong Cheng, Daniel Fadel, Luiz Lara
papers.abstract:
Given a constant $\lambda>0$, for any parameter $\varepsilon>0$ we study critical points of the Yang--Mills--Higgs energy \[ \mathcal{Y}_{\varepsilon}(
abla,\Phi) = \int_M \left(\varepsilon^2|F_{
abla}|^2 + |
abla\Phi|^2 +  rac{\lambda}{4\varepsilon^2}(1-|\Phi|^2)^2ight)\mathrm{vol}_g, \] defined for pairs $(
abla,\Phi)$, where $
abla$ is a connection on an $SU(2)$-bundle over an oriented Riemannian $3$-manifold $(M^3, g)$, and $\Phi$ a section of the associated adjoint bundle. When $M$ is closed, we use a $3$-parameter min-max construction to produce, for $\varepsilon\ll_M 1$, non-trivial critical points in the energy regime \[ 1 \lesssim_{\lambda}\varepsilon^{-1}\mathcal{Y}_{\varepsilon}(
abla_{\varepsilon},\Phi_{\varepsilon}) \lesssim_{\lambda, M} 1. \] When $b_1(M)=0$, these critical points are irreducible: $
abla_{\varepsilon}\Phi_{\varepsilon}
eq 0$. Next, assuming $M$ has bounded geometry (not necessarily compact), and given critical points with $\varepsilon^{-1}\mathcal{Y}_{\varepsilon}(
abla_{\varepsilon}, \Phi_{\varepsilon})$ uniformly bounded, we show that as $\varepsilon	o 0$, the energy measures $\varepsilon^{-1}e_{\varepsilon}(
abla_{\varepsilon}, \Phi_{\varepsilon}) \mathrm{vol}_{g}$ converge subsequentially to \[ |h|^2 \mathrm{vol}_g + \sum_{x \in S}\Theta(x)\delta_{x}, \] where $h$ is an $L^2$ harmonic $1$-form, $S$ a finite set and each $\Theta(x)$ equals the energy of a finite collection of $\mathcal{Y}_{1}$-critical points on $\mathbb{R}^3$. Finally, the estimates involved also lead to an energy gap for critical points on $3$-manifolds with bounded geometry. As a byproduct of our results, we deduce the existence of non-trivial $\mathcal{Y}_{1}$-critical points over $\mathbb{R}^3$ for any $\lambda>0$.

papers.title: Average measure theoretic entropy for a family of expanding on average random Blaschke products
papers.abstract: This work gives a computable formula for the average measure theoretic entropy of a family of expanding on average random Blaschke products, generalizing work by Pujals, Roberts and Shub [Expanding maps of the circle revisited: positive Lyapunov exponents in a rich family. $\textit{Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems.}$ $\textbf{26}(6)$ $(2006),$ $1931$-$1937$] to the random setting. In doing so, we describe the random invariant measure and associated measure theoretic entropy for a class of admissible random Blaschke products, allowing for maps which are not necessarily expanding and may even have an attracting fixed point.

papers.title: Variational structure of Fokker-Planck equations with variable mobility
papers.abstract: We study Fokker--Planck equations with symmetric, positive definite mobility matrices capturing diffusion in heterogeneous environments. A weighted Wasserstein metric is introduced for which these equations are gradient flows. This metric is shown to emerge from an optimal control problem in the space of probability densities for a class of variable mobility matrices, with the cost function capturing the work dissipated via friction. Using the Nash-Kuiper isometric embedding theorem for Riemannian manifolds, we demonstrate the existence of optimal transport maps. Additionally, we construct a time-discrete variational scheme, establish key properties for the associated minimizing problem, and prove convergence to weak solutions of the associated Fokker-Planck equation.

papers.title: On the complement of nef divisors on projective manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $X'$ be a complex projective manifold, $\dim X'>1$, $Z$ a connected analytic subset of codimension one which is the support of a nef effective Cartier divisor $D$ on $X'$, $X:=X'\setminus Z$. Let $\kappa(D)$ be the Iitaka dimension of $D$. We prove that $X$ is not Hartogs if and only if $D$ is abundant and $\kappa(D)=1$. In particular, $X$ is not Hartogs if and only if $X$ is a proper fibration over an affine curve.

papers.title: Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the well-posedness and long-time behavior of a general continuum neural field model with Gaussian noise on possibly unbounded domains. In particular, we give conditions for the existence of invariant probability measures by restricting the solution flow to an invariant subspace with a nonlocal metric. Under the assumption of a sufficiently large decay parameter relative to the noise intensity, the norm of the connectivity kernel operator, and the Lipschitz regularity of the activation function, we establish exponential ergodicity and exponential mixing of the associated Markovian Feller semigroup and the uniqueness of the invariant measure.

papers.title: Proof of a conjecture on isolation of graphs with a universal vertex
papers.abstract: A copy of a graph $F$ is called an $F$-copy. For any graph $G$, the $F$-isolation number of $G$, denoted by $\iota(G,F)$, is the size of a smallest subset $D$ of the vertex set of $G$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ in $G$ intersects the vertex sets of the $F$-copies contained by $G$ (equivalently, $G-N[D]$ contains no $F$-copy). Thus, $\iota(G,K_1)$ is the domination number $\gamma(G)$ of $G$, and $\iota(G,K_2)$ is the vertex-edge domination number of $G$. Settling a conjecture of Zhang and Wu, the present first author proved that if $F$ is a $k$-edge graph, $\gamma(F) = 1$ (that is, $F$ has a vertex that is adjacent to all the other vertices of $F$), and $G$ is a connected $m$-edge graph, then $\iota(G,F) \leq \frac{m+1}{k+2} $ unless $G$ is an $F$-copy or $F$ is a $3$-vertex path and $G$ is a $6$-cycle. The graphs that attain the bound were determined for $0 \leq k \leq 1$ by Fenech, Kaemawichanurat and the present first author, and for $k = 2$ by Zhang and Wu. In this paper, we determine them for $k \geq 3$. Our result was also conjectured by Zhang and Wu.

papers.title: Random Batch Methods for Discretized PDEs on Graphs
papers.abstract: Diffusion and transport processes on networks arise in applications such as pipeline systems, traffic and information flow, and energy and thermal networks. In these settings the dynamics are often modeled by partial differential equations (PDEs) on graph domains, and their simulation becomes increasingly expensive as the network size grows. The Random Batch Method (RBM) offers a way to reduce this cost, while preserving the large-scale behavior in expectation. In this paper, we study a discretize+RBM strategy for the heat equation. After a finite element discretization in space, we combine it with RBM by decomposing the resulting discrete operator into a finite sum of submatrices and, on short time intervals, replacing the full discrete operator by a randomly chosen partial sum. This defines a computationally cheaper, unbiased RBM approximation of the semi-discrete dynamics. For the one-dimensional heat equation, we prove mean-square convergence of this RBM approximation to the exact PDE solution under a suitable coupling between the short-interval length and the spatial discretization step, and we extend this analysis to a linear-quadratic optimal control problem. The same framework is then applied to the heat equation on metric graphs, and we validate it numerically, showing that the discretize+RBM scheme attains accuracy comparable to a full-graph solver while reducing computational resources. The method can be interpreted as a randomized domain-decomposition strategy on graphs. We emphasize that, beyond the heat equation, the underlying discretize+RBM construction can in principle be applied to a wider class of linear PDEs.

papers.title: Semisimplicity of conformal blocks
papers.abstract: We prove that braid group representations associated to braided fusion categories and mapping class group representations associated to modular fusion categories are always semisimple. The proof relies on the theory of extensions in non-Abelian Hodge theory and on Ocneanu rigidity. By combining this with previous results on the existence of variations in Hodge structures, we further show that such a braid group or mapping class group representation preserves a non-degenerate Hermitian form and can be defined over some CM number field.

papers.title: Stackelberg stopping games
papers.abstract: We study a Stackelberg variant of the classical discrete-time Dynkin game, in which Player 1 (the leader) commits to a stopping strategy first and Player 2 (the follower) responds optimally. This leader-follower structure induces an optimal control problem for the leader and gives rise to intrinsic time-inconsistency. We first clarify notions of precommitment and equilibrium strategies in the Stackelberg setting, and contrast them with the Nash equilibrium in the standard Dynkin game using a finite-horizon example. We then consider an infinite-horizon framework with a time-homogeneous Markov process on a general Polish state space. We characterize the leader's value function under randomized precommitment strategies and show that randomized exact equilibrium strategies may fail to exist via a counterexample. Motivated by this nonexistence phenomenon, we introduce an entropy-regularized Stackelberg stopping game. The regularization induces a continuous response rule and yields the existence of randomized regular equilibria. We further show that these regular equilibria induce epsilon-equilibria for the original Stackelberg stopping game when the regularization parameter is sufficiently small. In the finite-state setting, we also establish a limiting result as the regularization parameter converges to zero.

papers.title: A Note on Zoll Manifolds with Entire Grauert Tubes
papers.abstract: We compute several algebraic indices of the algebraization of the tangent bundle of a Zoll manifold that admits an entire Grauert tube. As an application, we prove that any Zoll manifold of type $\mathbb{HP}^2$ with an entire Grauert tube is isometric to the canonical $\mathbb{HP}^2$.

papers.title: Parabolic abstract evolution equations in cylindrical domains and uniformly local Sobolev spaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider parabolic equations of the type $$\partial_t u(x,t)=\Delta u(x,t) - Bu(x,t) + F(u(x,t))$$ where $u$ is valued in a transverse Hilbert space $Y$ and $B$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on $Y$, allowing a different diffusion mechanism in the transverse direction. We aim at considering solutions with infinite energy and we study the Cauchy problem in the uniformly local spaces associated with the norm $$\|u\|_{L^2_{\text{ul}}(\mathbb{R},Y)}= \sup_{a\in\mathbb{R}^d} \|u(x)\|_{L^2(B(a,1),Y)}.$$ For the classical parabolic equation, i.e. if $Y=\mathbb{R}$, it is known that the Cauchy problem is ill-posed in the weak version of the uniformly local spaces but well-posed in a stronger version, where additional uniform continuity is required. In this paper, we show that the linear operator $\partial^2_{xx} - B$ is not necessarily a sectorial operator in any version of the uniformly local Lebesgue space, due to the possible non-density of its domain. Then, we use the theory of parabolic abstract evolution equations to set a well-posed Cauchy problem, even in the weak version of the uniformly local space. In particular, we believe that this paper offers a new perspective on the comparison between both versions of the uniformly local spaces and also provides a new natural example of differential operators with non-dense domain.

papers.title: On a class of multiplicative Lindley-type recursions with Markov-modulated dependencies
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of Markov-modulated multiplicative Lindley-type recursions of the form $W_{n+1}=[V_nW_n+Y_n(V_n)]^+$, where the additive term may depend on the multiplicative coefficient and on a common finite-state background Markov chain. The main feature of the model is that the multiplicative coefficient is allowed to take negative values, which destroys the usual monotonicity structure of Lindley-type recursions. We consider two cases. In the first one, $V_n$ may take the values $1$, a constant $a\in(0,1)$, or a negative value, according to specific probabilities, while $Y_n(V_n)=S_n-A_{n+1}$ and the relevant Laplace--Stieltjes transforms are assumed to be rational. In the second one, $V_n\in\{1,-1\}$, and the additive term has a more general form depending on $V_n$. For both models, we derive vector-valued functional equations for the stationary transform. For the first model, we obtain a recursive transform representation, while for the second model we derive a finite-dimensional characterization based on root-cancellation conditions. We also provide a recursive procedure for computing stationary moments and discuss the light-tailed asymptotic behaviour. An extension based on the Farlie--Gumbel--Morgenstern copula is also presented. Numerical experiments show how the transform representation can be used to compute stationary moments, tail probabilities and quantiles, and validate the results against Monte Carlo simulation.

papers.title: Noncommutative principal bundles and central extensions
papers.abstract: Motivated by the classical theory of spin structures, we develop a theory for lifting free C$^*$-dynamical systems, a.k.a. noncommutative principal bundles, along central extensions. This theory extends the bundle-theoretic notion of spin structures and yields a complete existence and classification result for such lifts. Using factor system techniques and Picard formalism, our approach introduces new invariants and obstruction classes, thereby unifying geometric, cohomological, and operator-algebraic perspectives. A range of examples demonstrates the scope of the theory.

papers.title: Weak Relative Calabi-Yau Structures for Legendrian Contact Homology
papers.abstract: Legendrian Contact Homology (LCH) and its augmentations are important invariants of Legendrian submanifolds, and for Legendrian knots in the standard contact 3-space in particular. We increase understanding of the algebraic structure of LCH by generalizing the duality isomorphism and long exact sequence for linearized LCH for Legendrian knots to a weak relative Calabi-Yau structure for $A_\infty$ bimodules over the positive augmentation category.

papers.title: Fast Multipole Method with Complex Coordinates
papers.authors: Tristan Goodwill, Leslie Greengard, Jeremy Hoskins, Manas Rachh, Yuguan Wang
papers.abstract: When solving problems of potential theory in unbounded layered media, recently developed integral equation methods rely on coordinate complexification to permit truncation of the computational domain while retaining high order accuracy. As a result, classical fast multipole methods (FMMs) cannot be used to accelerate the evaluation of layer potentials. In this paper, we present a variant of the FMM which applies when the source and target locations have complex coordinates in two and three dimensions. This complex coordinate FMM is based on the analytic continuation of the various special function identities used in the real-space setting. To achieve the same linear-time complexity as in the classical FMM, we construct a hierarchical tree based solely on the real parts of the complex point locations and derive convergence rates for truncated expansions when the imaginary parts of the locations depend Lipschitz-continuously on the corresponding real parts. We demonstrate the efficiency of our approach through several numerical examples and illustrate its application to solving large-scale linearized water wave problems and Helmholtz transmission problems.

papers.title: Sharpness of the phase transition for constrained-degree percolation
papers.authors: Ivailo Hartarsky, Roger W. C. Silva
papers.abstract: We consider constrained-degree percolation on the hypercubic lattice. Initially, all edges are closed, and each edge independently attempts to open at a uniformly distributed random time; the attempt succeeds if, at that instant, both end-vertices have degrees strictly less than a prescribed parameter. The absence of the FKG inequality and the finite energy property, as well as the infinite range of dependence, make the rigorous analysis of the model particularly challenging. In this work, we show that the one-arm probability exhibits exponential decay in its entire subcritical phase. The proof relies on the Duminil-Copin--Raoufi--Tassion randomized algorithm method and resolves a problem of dos Santos and the second author. At the heart of the argument lies an intricate combinatorial transformation of pivotality in the spirit of Aizenman--Grimmett essential enhancements, but with unbounded range. This technique may be of use in other dynamical settings.

papers.title: Tiny and Unique: The Lubin-Tate Action at Height $p-1$ from the Minimal Curve with Its Symmetries
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be odd and $G' = \mathbb{Z}/p \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/(p-1)^2$ the maximal finite subgroup of the Morava stabilizer group at height $p-1$. Inverse Galois theory produces from $G'$ alone a curve $X$, the unique curve of minimal genus with $\operatorname{Aut}(X) \simeq G'$; its ramification, its field of definition and its equation are consequences of the group, not choices. We prove a $G'$-equivariant equivalence between the deformations of $X$ and Lubin--Tate space, so that the Lubin--Tate action of $G'$ is the action of $\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ on deformations of the curve. The proof is a coordinate-free Kodaira--Spencer argument reducing to a single character count. The action becomes explicit: $G'$ acts through $\mathbb{F}_p \rtimes \mathbb{F}_p^\times$ shifting and scaling $p+1$ points on $\mathbb{P}^1$. From this we compute $H^*(G', \pi_* E_{p-1})$ and its Tate cohomology. One identity, $\pi^{p-1} = -p$, runs through every section.

papers.title: Gelfand-Kirillov dimensions and annihilator varieties of highest weight modules of exceptional Lie algebras
papers.authors: Zhanqiang Bai, Fan Gao, Yutong Wang, Xun Xie
papers.abstract: Let $L(\lambda)$ be an irreducible highest weight module of a complex simple Lie algebra of exceptional type, with highest weight $\lambda-\rho$, where $\rho$ is half the sum of positive roots. Its annihilator variety is the closure of a nilpotent orbit of dimension twice the Gelfand--Kirillov (GK) dimension of $L(\lambda)$. We develop an explicit algorithm that determines both invariants for any infinitesimal character. The GK dimension is reduced to evaluating Lusztig's $\mathbf{a}$-function on the integral Weyl group of $\lambda$. After decomposing the integral root system into irreducible factors, classical factors are treated by the Robinson--Schensted insertion algorithm and the H-algorithm, while exceptional factors are handled by positive index reduction and PyCox. The annihilator orbit is then recovered from the local special datum by Springer theory and Sommers duality. An implementation is available online and takes $\lambda$ as input to compute the GK dimension and annihilator variety of $L(\lambda)$.

papers.title: A remark on the Moduli of parabolic connections
papers.authors: Pradeep Das, Snehajit Misra, Anoop Singh
papers.abstract: We consider the moduli space of stable parabolic connections of full flag type with generic rational weights on a compact Riemann surface $X$ of genus $g \ge 3$, with singularities along the parabolic points. We compute the Chow groups of the fixed determinant moduli space consisting of parabolic connections whose underlying parabolic bundle is stable. We show that the moduli space of stable parabolic connections is not rationally connected, whereas the fixed determinant moduli space is rationally connected and in fact rational. We also prove that the determinant map to the Picard variety is universal among morphisms to abelian varieties. Finally, we show that the algebraic group of rank one holomorphic connections acts trivially on the cohomology of the moduli space of stable parabolic connections.

papers.title: Serre weight conjectures for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$
papers.authors: Daniel Le, Bao V. Le Hung, Heejong Lee
papers.abstract: We prove the weight part of Serre's conjecture for Galois representations valued in $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ that are tamely ramified with explicit genericity at places above $p$ as conjectured by Herzig--Tilouine and Gee--Herzig--Savitt. This improves on arXiv:2304.13879 where an inexplicit genericity hypothesis was required. As an application, we prove a modularity lifting theorem for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ under similar assumptions.

papers.title: A Mapping Theorem for Derived Foliations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct in characteristic zero a derived foliation on derived mapping stacks $\underline{\mathbf{Map}}_S(X,Y)$ under natural representability assumptions, for $S$ a base derived stack, $X$ a proper schematic, flat, and local complete intersection derived stack over $S$, and $Y$ a relative derived Deligne-Mumford stack locally of finite presentation over $S$, when $Y$ is equipped with a derived foliation relative to $S$. In the process, given a derived stack $Z$ locally of finite presentation over a derived stack $X$, we will first show that the $\infty$-category of derived foliations over $Z$ relative to $X$ embeds as a full subcategory of derived stacks over $Z$ equipped with extra structure, and describe its essential image explicitly. We will then show that given a proper schematic, flat, and local complete intersection map of derived stacks $f : X \to Y$, the push-forward or Weil-restriction functor $f_*$ from derived stacks over $X$ to derived stacks over $Y$ preserves the preceding essential images, and thus defines a push-forward, from derived foliations over $Z$ relative to $X$, to derived foliations over $f_* Z$ relative to $Y$, under natural representability assumptions. The aforementioned result on derived mapping stacks is obtained as a special case of this statement. As example applications, given a smooth projective scheme $X$ equipped with a derived foliation, we obtain derived foliations on the derived moduli stacks $\mathbb R \overline{\mathbf M}_{g,n}(X)$ and $\mathbb R \mathbf{Hilb}^{lci}(X)$, which are respectively the derived enhancements of the moduli stack of families of stable curves of genus $g$ with $n$ marked points on $X$, and of the Hilbert scheme of closed subschemes of $X$.

papers.title: On discrete symmetries of the cube of smoothings
papers.abstract: A link diagram with a labeled barycentric subdivision endows the cube of resolutions with an additional combinatorial structure. We study the set of symmetries, preserving this structure. We construct a combinatorial link invariant, based on the symmetries of triangulated smoothings.

papers.title: Hyperbolic $O (N)$ linear sigma model and its mean-field limit
papers.authors: Ruoyuan Liu, Shao Liu, Tadahiro Oh
papers.abstract: We study large $N$ limits of the hyperbolic $O(N)$ linear sigma model ($\text{HLSM}_N$) on the two-dimensional torus $\mathbb T^2$, namely, a system of $N$ interacting stochastic damped nonlinear wave equations (SdNLW) with coupled cubic nonlinearities. After establishing (pathwise) global well-posedness of $\text{HLSM}_N$ and the limiting equation, called the mean-field SdNLW, we first establish global-in-time convergence of $\text{HLSM}_N$ to the mean-field SdNLW with general initial data (under a suitable assumption). In particular, for the local-in-time convergence, we obtain a convergence rate of order $N^{- \frac 12}$ under an additional integrability assumption on initial data. We then show that the invariant Gibbs dynamics for $\text{HLSM}_N$ converges to that for the mean-field SdNLW with a convergence rate of order $N^{- \frac 12}$ on any large time intervals.

papers.title: A Tight-binding Approach for Computing Subwavelength Guided Modes in Crystals with Line Defects
papers.authors: Habib Ammari, Erik Orvehed Hiltunen, Ping Liu, Borui Miao, Yi Zhu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a framework for computing subwavelength guided modes in high-contrast periodic media with line defects, based on a tight-binding approximation. The physical problem is formulated as an eigenvalue problem for the Helmholtz equation with high-contrast parameters. By employing layer potential theory on unbounded domains, we characterize the subwavelength frequencies via the quasi-periodic capacitance matrix. Our main contribution is the proof of exponential decay of the off-diagonal elements of the associated full and quasi-periodic capacitance matrices. These decay properties provide error bounds for the banded approximation of the capacitance matrices, thereby enabling a tight-binding approach for computing the spectral properties of subwavelength resonators with non-compact defects. Numerical experiments illustrate the decay and compare full and banded capacitance matrices for defect and dimerized interface configurations.

papers.title: Completing the enumeration of inversion sequences avoiding triples of relations
papers.abstract: An inversion sequence of length $n$ is an integer sequence $(a_1, \ldots, a_n)$ such that $0 \le a_i < i$ for all $i$. The study of pattern-avoiding inversion sequences was initiated in 2015 by Mansour and Shattuck and in 2016 by Corteel, Martinez, Savage and Weselcouch. Martinez and Savage later defined a new type of pattern, a triple of binary relations, of which there are currently 14 uncounted avoidance classes. We complete the enumeration for all of these classes using generating tree methods "growing on the left" and "growing on the right". For many of these classes we are able to find algebraic generating functions. We also discuss the asymptotic behaviour of the counting sequences.

papers.title: Entropy Rigidity for Maximal Representations
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma\subset \mathsf{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ be a lattice and $\rho:\Gamma\to \mathsf{Sp}(2n,\mathbb{R})$ be a maximal representation. We show that $\rho$ satisfies a measurable $(1,1,2)-$hypertransversality condition. With this we define a measurable Gromov product and the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure associated to the unstable Jacobian introduced by Pozzetti, Sambarino and Wienhard. As a main application, we prove a strong entropy rigidity result for $\rho$.

papers.title: Optimal Stopping for the Uniform Distribution
papers.abstract: Many discrete-time optimal stopping problems are known to have more tractable limit forms based on a planar Poisson process. Using this tool we find a solution to the optimal stopping problem for i.i.d. sequence of $n$ discrete uniform random variables, in the asymptotic regime where $n$ and the range of distribution are of the same order. The optimal stopping rule in the Poisson problem is identified, by means of a time change, with known asymptotic solution to Lindley's problem of minimising the expected rank.

papers.title: Cobordism, spin structures, and profinite completions
papers.abstract: Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth closed connected aspherical manifolds with good (in the sense of Serre) fundamental groups $G$ and $H$. We show that if $\widehat G\cong \widehat H$, then $M$ and $N$ are cobordant and the signatures of $M$ and $N$ agree modulo $8$. Moreover, $M$ is spin (resp. spin$^\mathbb{C}$) if and only if $N$ is spin (resp. spin$^\mathbb{C}$). We consider some analogous results for compact connected aspherical manifolds.

papers.title: An elementary approach to delta and gamma hedging, and the Black--Scholes PDE
papers.abstract: We show how the robustness of gamma hedging can be understood just using the concepts of $p^{th}$ variation along a partition sequence and Taylor's theorem. There is no need to define an integral or proving a version of It\^o's lemma. The same approach allows classical results on delta-hedging to be proved without defining an integral and without the need to define the concept of self-financing in continuous time. We show that the approach can also be applied to barrier options and Asian options. Finally, we extend the framework to path-dependent derivatives. We introduce a Gubinelli-type control along a sequence of partitions, and use it to define a pathwise notion of arbitrage. Finally, we show that in any arbitrage-free pricing model the greeks must satisfy a linear relation. If one additionally assumes time and scaling symmetries, this yields the Black--Scholes PDE.

papers.title: Absolute continuity of the law of the solution to the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation driven by fractional noise
papers.authors: Dimitrios Dimitriou, Dimitris Farazakis, Georgia Karali
papers.abstract: The stochastic partial differential equation analyzed in this work is the Cahn-Hilliard equation perturbed by an additive fractional white noise (fractional in time and white in space). We work in spatial dimensions $d \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ with $d < 4H$, where $H \in (\frac{1}{2}, 1)$ is the Hurst parameter of the noise, and apply Malliavin calculus to investigate the existence of a density for the solution $u$. In particular, we show that $u$ admits a jointly continuous modification and construct a localizing sequence through which we prove that its Malliavin derivative exists locally, and that its law is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$, thereby establishing that a density exists. We obtain the result for the whole range of dimensions and Hurst parameters in which the mild solution is known to exist. The analysis rests on three new estimates. The first bounds the expectation of the $p$-th power ($p \geq 2$) of the $L^{\infty}(D)$-norm of the stochastic integral appearing in the mild formulation. The other two concern the integral involving the operator associated with the kernel that appears in the integral representation of the fractional noise: an upper estimate and, more importantly, a lower estimate on short time intervals, which yields the nondegeneracy of the Malliavin derivative.

papers.title: Normality of monomial ideals in three variables
papers.abstract:
An ideal $I$ in a Noetherian ring is called \textit{normal} if $I^n$ is integrally closed for all $n \geq 1$. Zariski proved that in two-dimensional regular local rings, every integrally closed ideal is normal. However, in dimension three and higher, this is no longer true in general, including monomial ideals in polynomial rings.
  In this paper, we study the normality of integrally closed monomial ideals in the polynomial ring $k[x,y,z]$ over a field $k$. We prove that every such ideal with at most seven minimal monomial generators is normal, thereby giving a sharp bound for normality in this setting. The proof is based on a detailed case-by-case analysis, combined with valuation-theoretic and combinatorial methods via Newton polyhedra.

papers.title: Numerical computations concerning Landau-Siegel zeros
papers.authors: Rick F. Lu, Asif Zaman, Haonan Zhao
papers.abstract: We computationally verify that if $L(s,\chi)$ is a quadratic Dirichlet $L$-function modulo $q \leq 10^{10}$ then $L(\sigma,\chi) \neq 0$ for real $\sigma \ge 1-1/(5\log q)$. The number of verified moduli exceeds benchmarks due to Watkins (2004), Platt (2016), and Languasco (2023) by a factor between 66 and 25,000. Our new algorithm draws from zero-free region arguments.

papers.title: Multivariate and quantitative Erd\H{o}s-Kac laws for Beatty sequences
papers.abstract:
The classical Erd\H{o}s-Kac theorem states that for $n$ chosen uniformly at random from $1, \dots, N$, the random variable $(\omega(n) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to the standard Gaussian as $N$ tends to infinity. Banks and Shparlinski showed that this Gaussian convergence holds for any Beatty sequence $\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor$ in place of $n$. Continuing in this spirit, Crn\v{c}evi\'c, Hern\'andez, Rizk, Sereesuchart and Tao considered the joint distribution of $\omega(n)$ and $\omega(\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor)$, which they showed to be asymptotically independent for irrational values of $\alpha$.
  Generalising both results, we show that for any positive integer $k$, real numbers $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k > 0$ and $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_k$, where $\alpha_i/\alpha_j$ is irrational for $i\neq j$, the joint distribution of $(\omega(\lfloor\alpha_in + \beta_i\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges to the $k$-dimensional standard Gaussian.
  We next discuss quantitative bounds on the rate of convergence which do not depend on the values taken by the relevant parameters. Banks and Shparlinski remarked that such quantitative bounds may be given for a single Beatty sequence $\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor$ under Diophantine type assumptions on $\alpha$. We show that such assumptions are in fact unnecessary. Specifically, for any real numbers $\alpha > 0, \beta$, we show that the Kolmogorov distance between the random variable $(\omega(\lfloor\alpha n + \beta\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ and the standard Gaussian is bounded above by $O(\log\log\log N/\sqrt{\log\log N})$ as $N$ tends to infinity.
  On the other hand, we show that universal quantitative bounds of this kind do not exist for higher-degree generalised polynomials or for the joint convergence for multiple Beatty sequences.

papers.title: High-dimensional linear regression inference via $\ell^2$ weak convergence
papers.abstract: We prove weak convergence in a separable Hilbert space for estimators of high-dimensional regression coefficients, which yields asymptotic normality and enables direct use of standard asymptotic tools such as the continuous mapping theorem. The approach permits diverging sparsity with a growing number of small nonzero coefficients, while requiring that only finitely many have moderate magnitude. As applications, we develop a test for finitely many linear hypotheses and, via a Scheff\'{e}-type approach, simultaneous inference for infinitely many linear hypotheses, yielding both a global test and simultaneous confidence bands for the regression function. The limiting distributions are given by weighted sums of independent chi-squared variables, and plug-in critical values achieve asymptotically correct size.

papers.title: Data-Driven Hull-Fouling Cleaning Schedule Optimization to Reduce Carbon Footprint of Vessels
papers.authors: Samuel J. Ward, Marah-Lisanne Thormann, Julian Wharton, Alain Zemkoho
papers.abstract: In response to climate change, the International Maritime Organization has introduced regulations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping. Compliance with these regulations is increasingly expected from individual shipping companies and can be achieved through more frequent hull and propeller cleanings. Since this maintenance work entails high costs, vessel operators are confronted with the trade-off between lower fleet emissions and better economic performance. As a result, assessing whether fuel efficiency has declined sufficiently to warrant cleaning from an environmental and economic standpoint is a critical task. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel dynamic-programming-based algorithm to optimize vessel cleaning schedules. The main components of the optimization problem are a data-driven function for the fuel consumption costs and an additive term that sums up the costs per vessel cleaning. In numerical experiments, we demonstrate the usefulness of our proposed methodology based on real-world sensor data from nine tramp trading vessels. The results confirm that, over four years, fuel consumption can be reduced by up to 5%, even when accounting for the costs of the additional cleaning events.

papers.title: Stability of the Shape for Circular Vortex Filaments under Non-Symmetric Perturbations
papers.abstract: We establish the nonlinear orbital stability of circular vortex filaments governed by the Localized Induction Equation (LIE) under non-symmetric perturbations, within the framework of [Tani-Nishiyama, 1997]. This result extends the first author's recent work [Aiki, 2025] by removing symmetry assumptions on perturbations. While the circular filaments are known to be Lyapunov unstable due to linear growth of the translational mode, we prove that their shape remains globally stable modulo spatial translations and rotations about the symmetry axis. The crucial ingredient is a geometric stability estimate derived from the conservation of vector fluid impulse, which constrains the low-frequency modulations that are not covered by the relative energy. Finally, we relate the fluid impulse to an isoperimetric inequality, yielding a geometric constraint for closed filaments.

papers.title: Picard bundles and Twisted Picard bundles on the Jacobian of a curve
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ denote an irreducible projective curve with at most nodes as singularities and defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We study the restriction of the twisted Picard bundles on the compactified Jacobian $\overline{J}(Y)$ of $Y$ to the embedded curve in $\overline{J}(Y)$. As an application, we show that for $g =2$ and each integer $r \ge 3$, there is a two-dimensional family of stable ACM bundles on the compactified Jacobian which has the Picard bundle in its limit. We define an embedding $\alpha_Y$ of the (generalised) Jacobian $J(Y)$ in the moduli space $U^s_Y(n,d)$ of stable vector bundles on $Y$ using a twisted restriction $E_Y$ of a Picard bundle to $Y \subset J(Y)$. We show that (under suitable conditions) the restriction of the universal bundle $\mathcal{U}$ to $Y \times J(Y)$ is stable for suitable polarisation. For the embedding of a smooth curve $Y$ given by $E_Y \otimes B, B$ a line bundle of degree $b$, we show that the restriction of the Picard bundle on $U^s_Y(n, d+nb)$ to $J(Y)$ is $\theta$-semistable for $b \ge 2g-1$ and $\theta$-stable for $b \ge 2g$. We also determine the relation between the restriction of the theta divisor on $U^s_Y(n,d+nb)$ to $J(Y)$ and the theta divisor $\theta$ on $\overline{J}(Y)$.

papers.title: A survey of sampling discretization of integral and uniform norms
papers.authors: F. Dai, E. Kosov, V. Temlyakov
papers.abstract:
This paper surveys recent developments in the sampling discretization of integral and uniform norms for functions in general finite-dimensional spaces. These results generalize the classical Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities for trigonometric and algebraic polynomials, which play a crucial role in Fourier analysis, interpolation, and approximation theory. We focus on the problem in the broad context of finite-dimensional subspaces, where norms defined by general probability measures are approximated by their discrete counterparts.
  The primary emphasis is on results closely related to the authors' recent research. A key objective is to highlight the main ideas and techniques that form the foundation of the proofs in this area. This survey serves as a complement to three recently published survey papers on sampling discretization \cite{DPTT, KKLT, LMT}.

papers.title: Domination polynomial of co-maximal graphs of integer modulo ring
papers.abstract: We investigate the domination polynomial of the co-maximal graph $\Gamma(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ related to the ring of integers modulo $n$. Such a polynomial encodes domination sets of all possible sizes, a NP-hard problem for general graph. We give exact formulas for prime powers, integers with two distinct prime divisors, and products of three distinct primes. A prime-support decomposition gives a finite explicit formula for arbitrary $n$, including repeated prime factors. Further results determine the highest coefficients, the precise threshold beyond which every vertex subset dominates, and the number of non-dominating subsets. We discuss unimodality and log-concavity, and derive justified bounds for nonzero domination roots using the Enestr\"om--Kakeya theorem.

papers.title: Warped area-minimizing hypersurface and warped product metric
papers.abstract:
Several metric splitting theorems under spectral Ricci curvature lower bounds have been established in recent years, yet the existing literature mostly yields only isometric direct product decompositions. In some parameter regimes, direct product splitting is even known to fail. In this paper, we study warped (weighted) area-minimizing hypersurfaces and use their variational properties to prove local warped product metric splitting under spectral Ricci curvature conditions.
  Given a smooth compact connected $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ with non vanishing homology $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb Z)$, satisfying our spectral Ricci lower bound, and with dimension $3\le n\le 5$, we consider a nontrivial homological warped area-minimizing hypersurface $\Sigma$ whose existence follows from classical geometric measure theory. By analyzing the first and second variations of the warped area functional together with a foliation argument, we show that $M$ locally decomposes as a warped product $(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times_f \Sigma$, where the warping function is given by $f=u^{-1}$ for the positive weight function $u$ appearing in the spectral Ricci condition.
  Our work complements the existing splitting theory for spectral Ricci curvature: even in parameter ranges where product type splitting cannot hold, we still obtain local warped product rigidity via weighted minimal hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Fast Relax-and-Round Unit Commitment with Economic Horizons
papers.authors: Shaked Regev, Evan J. R. Brody, Charles Foltz, Eve Tsybina, Slaven Peles
papers.abstract: The US energy system is under increasing pressure to serve expanding data centers loads and to accommodate a larger number of generating units with varying technologies and ownership structures. Therefore, developing new unit commitment (UC) methods remains a priority for reliable and affordable grid operations. We expand our novel computational method for UC to include ramping constraints and long-horizon planning, and provide a theoretical bound on its accuracy. We solve problems with thousands of generators at 5-minute market intervals. We show that our method can solve UC problems with over 20,000 generators in approximately 10 seconds on commodity hardware and that an increased planning horizon leads to sizable op- erational cost savings. This is twice as fast as the leading commercial solver, Gurobi. The gap increases when adding more constraints. Our method can be implemented using existing continuous optimization solvers and adapted for different applications. We prove a bound on the error of these solvers and show that it vanishes (in relative terms) as the problem becomes larger. Our novel algorithm could allow an operator to make horizon-aware economic decisions for large systems.

papers.title: The universal property of graded $KK^G$-theory
papers.abstract: To each Kasparov cycle $z$ we attach inclusions $B\xrightarrow{j_z}Y_z\xrightarrow{i_z}X_z$ satisfying $[z]j_zi_z=s_zi_z$. A lift of a second factor along $k_z=j_zi_z$ therefore reduces the product to precomposition by a homomorphism. An additional even symmetry gives a retraction of $k_z$; this includes all cycles between trivially graded algebras and the splitting cycles of graded split extensions. The resulting cycle presentation recovers the ungraded equivariant Kasparov category. For arbitrary gradings, explicit tensor and Dirac relations give fusion by passing to a shifted and doubled cycle. We provide concrete Dirac cycles and a compact verification of the two scalar product identities used in this argument. Finally, an index obstruction shows that the corner of the original cycle need not admit a retraction, even after replacing that cycle by an equivalent representative.

papers.title: Exactness property of Breuil-Kisin functors and Bloch-Kato Selmer groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a $p$-adic field and $T$ a lattice in a semistable representation of $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ with Hodge-Tate weights in $[0, r]$. Assuming $0\leq r<p-1$, we prove that for a semistable extension of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ by $T$, the corresponding sequence of strongly divisible modules is exact. Analogous statements are proved for Breuil-Kisin modules and for prismatic $F$-crystals for all $r\geq 0$.
