In the crystalline case, we deduce that the integral Bloch-Kato Selmer group $H^1_f(K, T)$ is computed by $\mathrm{Ext}^1$ in the category of crystalline strongly divisible modules. Using further exactness results, we define a tensor product of strongly divisible modules, which commutes with the functors to Galois representations. As an application, we show that for abelian varieties $A_1, A_2$ over $K$ with good reduction, the cup product map $\delta_1\cup\delta_2:A_1(K)\otimes A_2(K)\rightarrow H^2(K, T_p(A_1)\otimes T_p(A_2))$ induced by the Kummer sequences of $A_1, A_2$ factors through an $\mathrm{Ext}^2$ group of strongly divisible modules. In the appendix we generalize further the main exactness results to coherent reflexive $F$-gauges.

papers.title: Fokker-Planck analysis and invariant laws for a continuous-time stochastic model inspired by Adam
papers.abstract: We study a degenerate stochastic system inspired by bias-corrected Adam. The system arises as the continuous-time limit of an explicitly modified recursion in which the squared-gradient update is replaced by a prescribed second-moment closure. We construct an entrance solution at the singular initial time and prove convergence of the modified recursion on finite time intervals away from zero. Bias correction enters through time-dependent coefficients which converge to constants as time tends to infinity. For a smooth objective with globally Lipschitz gradient and radial dissipativity at infinity, we prove existence and uniqueness of an invariant probability measure for the autonomous system under either $b<4a$ or $\gamma L_f\le a(\sigma/\sqrt2+\varepsilon)/4$. Here $L_f$ is the Lipschitz constant of the gradient, $a,b$ are the relaxation rates, $\gamma$ is the learning-rate parameter, and $\sigma,\varepsilon$ are the noise and regularization parameters. The proof combines an exponential Lyapunov function with compact-set minorization obtained from explicit control paths and a regular endpoint map. Under an exponential Lyapunov moment condition, we obtain exponential convergence in weighted total variation and in the squared $2$-Wasserstein distance of the complete state. The invariant law has finite moments of every order, and qualitative total variation convergence holds for every initial probability law. The time-inhomogeneous process converges weakly to the same invariant law. We formulate the associated Fokker-Planck equation for probability measures and establish local hypoellipticity and smoothness of the invariant density where $\operatorname{Diag}(\nabla f)D^2f$ is invertible. A quadratic example shows that a uniform exponential convergence estimate requires a prefactor growing exponentially in the initial position along a specified family of states.

papers.title: From BV-BFV Quantization to Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariants
papers.abstract: We propose a program for bridging the gap between the perturbative BV-BFV quantization of Chern-Simons theory and the non-perturbative Reshetikhin-Turaev (RT) invariants of 3-manifolds, passing through factorization homology of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras and the derived algebraic geometry of character stacks. We conjecture that the modular tensor category underlying the RT construction arises as the $\mathbb{E}_2$-category from BV-BFV quantization of Chern-Simons theory on the disk, with the derived character stack $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_\mathbb{C}}(\Sigma)$ of the complexified group and its shifted symplectic structure mediating the proposed identification. A recurring theme is the mismatch between the compact gauge group of Chern-Simons theory and the reductive algebraic group of derived algebraic geometry: we work throughout with $G_\mathbb{C}$ and indicate where a Riemann-Hilbert type comparison is needed to return to the compact theory. We formulate a main conjecture asserting natural equivalence of the BV-BFV and RT constructions as 3-2-1-extended topological quantum field theories, together with several auxiliary conjectures and two questions, develop a proof strategy via deformation quantization of shifted symplectic stacks, and clarify the role of $\mathbb{E}_n$-Koszul duality, which relates the perturbative expansion around a flat connection to the local geometry of the character stack. We relate the perturbative expansions to the sheaf of vanishing cycles on the character stack of a $3$-manifold, propose that a stratification of the character stack by stabilizer type organizes the trans-series decomposition, and propose that the Stokes data of the perturbative expansion should be read as a stability datum in the sense of Kontsevich-Soibelman, with the Chern-Simons functional playing the role of the central charge.

papers.title: Affine Subcode Ensemble Decoding of Linear Block Codes
papers.authors: Jonathan Mandelbaum, Paul Bezner, Holger J\"akel, Stephan ten Brink, Laurent Schmalen
papers.abstract: In the short block length regime, ensemble decoding schemes with their inherently parallel structure can improve error correction performance and reduce latency compared to stand-alone suboptimal decoders such as belief propagation (BP). In this work, we introduce affine subcode ensemble decoding (aSCED), which uses an ensemble of decoders operating on linear block codes and both linear and strictly affine subcodes. This generalizes the recently proposed subcode ensemble decoding (SCED), which is restricted to linear subcodes. We derive BP update rules for affine subcodes and show that aSCED simplifies ensemble design compared to SCED, multiple bases BP, and automorphism ensemble decoding. Monte-Carlo simulations of two low-density parity-check codes and two Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes demonstrate improved error correction performance of aSCED over competing existing ensemble schemes. Notably, for one BCH code, when combining ensemble design with algorithms for constructing high-performance parity-check matrices, aSCED achieves near-maximum likelihood performance using only 64 BP decoding paths.

papers.title: An Inexact Trust-Region Method for Structured Nonsmooth Optimization with Application to Risk-Averse Stochastic Programming
papers.abstract: We develop a trust-region method for efficiently minimizing the sum of a smooth function, a nonsmooth convex function, and the composition of a convex Lipschitz continuous function with a smooth function. Optimization problems with this structure arise in numerous applications including risk-averse stochastic programming and subproblems for nonsmooth penalty nonlinear programming methods. Our algorithm permits the use of inexact value and derivative information, enabling the solution of infinite-dimensional problems governed by, e.g., partial differential equations (PDEs). We prove global convergence of our method and under additional regularity assumptions, demonstrate that the sequence of iterates accumulates at a stationary point of our target problem. We demonstrate our method's efficiency on two PDE-constrained optimization examples, showing that its performance is invariant to the PDE discretization size.

papers.title: A Dehornoy-Type Ordering on Bridge Positions of Links
papers.abstract: By a theorem of Hovland, bridge isotopy classes of $n$-bridge positions of links in $S^3$ correspond bijectively to Hilden double cosets $P_{2n}=H_{2n}\backslash B_{2n}/H_{2n}$. We use this correspondence to introduce Dehornoy-type orderings on bridge positions. After fixing a proper complexity function on $B_{2n}$, we assign to each double coset its Dehornoy-minimal braid among the elements of minimal complexity. Comparing these representatives by the Dehornoy order gives a strict total order $\prec_{D,n}$, and comparing them first by complexity and then by the Dehornoy order gives a strict well-order $\triangleleft_{D,n}$. For a link type $L$ and $n\geq b(L)$, we single out a canonical $n$-bridge position $\operatorname{CanPlat}_D^{(n)}(L)$: it is the $\triangleleft_{D,n}$-least element of the set of $n$-bridge positions of $L$, and the $\prec_{D,n}$-least element among those of minimal complexity, and its canonical braid coincides with the globally Dehornoy-minimal braid of minimal complexity representing $L$. We show by an example that, in general, it need not be least for $\prec_{D,n}$ on the whole set. Finally, we show that the fixed-level bridge finiteness conjecture is equivalent to boundedness of the complexities of the canonical representatives, and to the existence of a $\triangleleft_{D,n}$-greatest $n$-bridge position.

papers.title: Lyapunov Unstable Motion Bifurcating from a Circular Vortex Filament
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of closed vortex filaments in $\R^3$ governed by the Localized Induction Equation. Recently, Aiki and Higaki (2026) established the nonlinear orbital stability of circular vortex filaments under asymmetric perturbations, while identifying Lyapunov instability due to the linear growth of translation modes. Motivated by this result, we prove the existence of a family of closed solutions, which we call axial screw motions, that bifurcate from a circular filament. These solutions remain uniformly close to the orbit of the circle, but drift secularly away from the reference motion because their translation speed along the symmetry axis differs from that of the circular filament. In particular, they provide explicit non-trivial perturbations that satisfy orbital-stability estimates while failing Lyapunov stability, thereby realizing the gap between orbital stability and Lyapunov stability near the circular filament.

papers.title: Vertex misalignment and changepoint localization in network time series
papers.authors: Tianyi Chen, Mohammad Sharifi Kiasari, Avanti Athreya, Sijing Yu, Youngser Park, Carey E Priebe, Vince Lyzinski, Zachary Lubberts
papers.abstract: Inference for time series of networks often relies on accurate vertex correspondence between network realizations at different times. In practice, such vertex alignments can be misspecified or unknown. We study the impact of errorful vertex alignment on changepoint localization for dynamic networks through two illustrative models, with the key distinction being whether changepoint information is contained in marginal or joint distributions of the time-varying latent positions. We compare localization techniques ranging from the simple network statistic of average degree to the modern procedure of Euclidean mirrors. Our results demonstrate that understanding the interplay of marginal and joint information in the observed network time series is key to robust network inference.

papers.title: Central series of cocommutative Hopf braces
papers.authors: Maria Bevilacqua, Marino Gran, Andrea Sciandra
papers.abstract: By extending some classical results known for groups and skew braces, we define and investigate central series of cocommutative Hopf braces. Both left and right central series are defined using a $\star$-product that measures the difference between the two algebra operations, and naturally leads to introducing the notions of socle and of annihilator of a cocommutative Hopf brace. We characterize the central extensions relative to the subcategories of cocommutative Hopf algebras and of commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebras, respectively. Since the category of cocommutative Hopf braces is semi-abelian and it has enough projectives with respect to the class of cleft extensions, one can then establish suitable Hopf formulae for their homology. These are expressed in terms of the corresponding notions of relative commutators of cocommutative Hopf braces. In particular, the one relative to the subcategory of commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebras turns out to be the Huq commutator.

papers.title: Kinetic theory for Transformers and the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon
papers.authors: Mitia Duerinckx, Borjan Geshkovski, Stefano Rossi
papers.abstract: We study causal self-attention dynamics -- a toy model for decoder Transformers -- which we interpret as a non-exchangeable interacting particle system. Adapting cumulant expansions to the triangular causal dependency structure of the model, and appealing to non-hierarchical methods to estimate correlations using Glauber calculus, we prove a quantitative mean-field limit result and a next-order characterization of correlations. For iid uniformly distributed tokens, the limiting correlation equation can be solved in closed form and we obtain a rigorous explanation of the empirically observed \emph{lost-in-the-middle} phenomenon: the token retrieval profile, as a function of the source position in the prompt, is $\mathsf{U}$-shaped, with primacy, recency, and a unique interior minimum under an explicit smallness condition.

papers.title: Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions and Fujii-Seo Determinants in Hilbert spaces
papers.authors: Per {\AA}hag, Rafa{\l} Czy\.z, Antti Per\"al\"a, Jani Virtanen
papers.abstract: A maximal plurisubharmonic function on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space can have an injective, noncompact Levi operator at every point. This raises the question of what replaces the finite-dimensional determinant criterion for maximality. We prove that a twice continuously differentiable plurisubharmonic function is maximal if its Levi operator is compact at every point, without any boundedness assumption on the function. Using the normalized determinants of Fujii and Seo, we also characterize local maximality by the condition that the infimum of the spectrum of the Levi operator is zero. The same condition characterizes maximality when the function is bounded on the closure of every bounded open set whose closure lies in the domain. The compactness result follows from a more general spectral criterion. Its proof combines a bounded transformation with the smooth variational principle of Borwein and Preiss to establish comparison on bounded open sets whose closures need not be compact.

papers.title: On spherical Milnor Classifying Spaces I: differential geometry
papers.abstract:
We compare the original product-subset diffeology on the Milnor join of Magnot--Watts with the locally finite final diffeology on a signed spherical model. The canonical squaring map from the spherical space to the Magnot--Watts join is smooth, whereas the positive square-root section is generally not; we also construct a different smooth injection from the locally finite simplicial model whose inverse is not smooth.
  For Hausdorff Fr\'echet--Lie groups whose smooth real-valued functions separate points, we compute the full algebraic internal tangent space, exhibiting separate first-order branches labelled by elements of the group at every inactive coordinate. The spherical weighted energy descends plotwise and restricts to a Riemannian metric on each support stratum. Smooth normalized strictly positive-definite kernels yield non-canonical ambient tangent metrics; compact Lie groups admit an explicit realization through their heat kernels. We characterize global diffeological forms by descent, construct plotwise Hausdorff Jacobians and varying-degree complementary forms, and show why these data do not define a canonical Hodge star across support changes. Stratumwise Hodge--Dirac operators remain available, but an explicit example obstructs their automatic gluing.
  We prove smooth contractibility of the total spherical space for any diffeological group, as well as equivariant uniqueness of maps to it. For any diffeological group we establish a classifying theorem for $D$-numerable principal bundles, without regularity hypotheses. For Lie groups we construct barycentric connections and their Chern--Weil forms, and distinguish sign local systems from gerbes. The hypotheses and proofs specify which conclusions are global, stratumwise, or conditional.

papers.title: Spherical Milnor Spaces II: Projective Quotients and Higher Topological Structures
papers.abstract: We study projective and semidirect quotients of the spherical Milnor construction and develop a step-by-step lifting obstruction from their explicit spherical local sections. The resulting transition functions produce a twisted Cech 2-cocycle for any specified compatible extension with abelian kernel. When the kernel is $U(1)$ and the sign acts by complex conjugation, taking logarithms yields a twisted Dixmier--Douady obstruction under stated sheaf hypotheses. We identify its projective-operator interpretation when an additional representation is supplied, without attempting a classification of K-theory twists. We also investigate descent of differential-geometric structures and, under restricted-operator hypotheses, Schwinger cocycles and lifting gerbes for loop groups.

papers.title: The distribution of semi-integral points on a class of singular cubic hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $X_k$ be the cubic hypersurface defined by the equation $x^3-(y_1^2+\cdots+y_{4k}^2)z=0$. In this paper, we give an asymptotic formula for the counting function of semi-integral points on $X_k$. We also prove that this asymptotic formula agrees with Manin's conjecture for $\mathcal{M}$-points [Moe26a, Conjecture 1.4] on the $a$-invariant and the $b$-invariant.

papers.title: Discriminants of derivatives: square graphs and sums of squares
papers.abstract: The discriminants of the derivatives of a real-rooted polynomial are nonnegative polynomials in its roots, and we ask whether this nonnegativity can be certified algebraically in the root differences. We compare three such certificates: sums of squares, positive combinations of symmetrized monomials in squared root differences (the square-graph cone of Alexandersson and Shapiro), and sum-of-squares factorizations of the Hermite matrix of the derivative. We work in the terminal range, where the degree $r=n-k$ of the $k$-th derivative is fixed and the degree $n$ of the polynomial grows. For $r=3$ the discriminant lies in the square-graph cone for every $n$, and we prove the three-graph formula conjectured by Alexandersson and Shapiro. For $r=4$ the two cones separate: the discriminant belongs to the square-graph cone exactly for $4\le n\le22$, but it is a sum of squares for every $n\ge4$. The negative part is certified by an explicit linear functional, the positive part by a rational Gram certificate built from nine orbits of squares under the symmetric group. Thus the square-graph conjecture fails, already at $(n,k)=(23,19)$, while the sum-of-squares question has a positive answer for all $k\ge n-4$. Finally, we give explicit sum-of-squares factorizations of the Hermite matrices of the terminal cubic and quartic. The quartic factorization yields a uniform proof of the sum-of-squares property for all $n\ge4$, and we conjecture that such a factorization exists for every derivative; this is verified in the centered outlier limit through terminal degree six.

papers.title: Gaussian Processes with Sample Paths in Reproducing Kernel Banach Spaces
papers.authors: Toni Karvonen, Rasmus Kleist H{\o}rlyck S{\o}rensen
papers.abstract: We investigate the connection between Gaussian processes and Gaussian random elements in reproducing kernel Banach spaces. We show that the covariance operator of a weak second-order Radon probability measure on such a space is uniquely determined by a symmetric positive-definite function. In the Gaussian case, we characterize those functions that arise from covariance operators in terms of $\gamma$-radonifying operators. Building on these results, we extend Driscoll's theorem to the reproducing kernel Banach space setting.

papers.title: Benchmarking Bilevel Derivative-Free Optimization Algorithms
papers.authors: Charles Audet, Valentin Dijon, Youssef Diouane
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization involves an upper-level and a lower-level decision maker. The lower-level optimization problem is nested within the constraints of the upper-level one. A point is said to be admissible for the bilevel problem if it satisfies all constraints and is optimal for the lower-level decision-maker. Bilevel derivative-free optimization (BL-DFO) algorithms address bilevel optimization problems in which the upper-level is solved using a derivative-free optimization method, and an inexact method it used to solve the lower- level. In this context, existing BL-DFO benchmarking techniques often do not rigorously validate the admissibility of proposed solutions, and do not adequately account for the computational effort deployed by the upper- and lower-level solvers. This work proposes a benchmarking methodology for BL-DFO algorithms. A post-optimization procedure, named the refereeing procedure, is introduced to discard non-admissible points and ensures a fair comparison between the algorithms. The computational effort deployed by upper- and lower-level solvers is also taken into account into the overall computational cost. Numerical experiments illustrate the benchmarking methodology.

papers.title: On gcd-graphs over matrix rings
papers.abstract: Graphs defined over finite rings are well studied in the literature. The study of these graphs benefits from rich connections between several areas of mathematics, including number theory, algebra, combinatorics, and graph theory, and these connections often lead to interesting interactions between algebraic and combinatorial structures. In this article, we investigate gcd-graphs defined over matrix rings with coefficients in finite fields. We show that these graphs exhibit several interesting graph-theoretic properties. Along the way, we also prove some results on the structure of matrix rings, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of strong rarefaction waves to a parabolic-hyperbolic system arising from chemotaxis
papers.abstract: We are interested in the asymptotic behavior of solutions toward strong rarefaction waves for a parabolic-hyperbolic system arising from chemotaxis. Suppose that the Riemann problem to the corresponding inviscid system admits rarefaction waves. We show that if the initial data is a small perturbation of an approximate rarefaction wave, then the Cauchy problem has a unique global solution that converges to the rarefaction wave asymptotically in time. The stability results hold regardless of the wave strengths. The waves can be either a single rarefaction wave or a composite of two rarefaction waves. In the composite case, we separate the initial centers of the two approximate profiles to make their interaction error term small while retaining convergence to the prescribed Riemann wave. The proofs are based on the energy method, where the key observations are the monotonicity of the approximate rarefaction waves with respect to both space and time, and the appropriate replacement of spatial derivative of the hyperbolic component with the parabolic component in proper forms.

papers.title: Normalized solutions to an exponential growth Choquard equation driven by mixed local-nonlocal operator in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.authors: Nidhi Nidhi, L. Sharma, K. Sreenadh
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study the existence of normalized solutions to the
  mixed nonlinear Choquard equation with exponential growth
  \begin{equation}
  \left\{
  \mathcal{L}u+\lambda u
  =
  \Lambda (I_{\alpha}*F(u))f(u)
  \text{ in }\mathbb{R}^{2}; \;\;
  \int_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}|u|^{2}\,dx
  =
  a^{2},
  \right.
  \end{equation}
  where $\mathcal{L}=-\Delta+(-\Delta)^s$, $0<s<1$, $a>0$, $I_{\alpha}$ is the Riesz potential of order $\alpha\in(0,2)$, $\Lambda>0$, and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ arises as a Lagrange multiplier. The nonlinearity has critical exponential growth in the sense of the Trudinger-Moser inequality. Using variational methods, the associated Poho\v{z}aev manifold, and suitable Moser-type estimates, we establish the existence of a normalized solution of mountain-pass type with associated non zero Lagrange multiplier. Under an additional monotonicity assumption on the nonlinearity, we further show that the obtained solution is a normalized ground state. We also establish the regularity properties required for the proof of the corresponding Poho\v{z}aev identity.

papers.title: Signature Methods for Optimal Market Making
papers.authors: Alberto Gennaro, Thibaut Mastrolia, Francesca Primavera
papers.abstract: We propose a signature-based method to solve the optimal market-making problem under a mean-variance criterion. By exploiting signature linearization techniques, we reduce the market-making problem to a pseudo-linear optimization over the expected signature of an augmented market path, and we develop a signature algorithm named Sig-REINFORCE to learn the optimal bid and ask quotes. We test our method in two scenarios, in which market-order arrivals follow either a Poisson or a self-exciting Hawkes process, and we benchmark it against a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) baseline.

papers.title: Global shadow estimates and Hausdorff measure criteria in higher rank
papers.abstract: Patterson--Sullivan measures encode the distribution of orbits of discrete group actions near the boundary. We prove a global shadow lemma for Patterson--Sullivan measures associated to relatively Morse subgroups of higher-rank semisimple Lie groups. The estimate is uniform for shadows centered at arbitrary points in a Gromov model, including points deep in the cuspidal part, and expresses the contribution of each cusp in terms of peripheral growth. This extends the global shadow lemma of Stratmann--Velani for geometrically finite real hyperbolic groups. As applications, we establish local doubling and reverse doubling. Under Zariski density, we give necessary and sufficient criteria for Patterson--Sullivan measures to agree with the associated Hausdorff measures and to be Ahlfors regular. For symmetric linear forms, these criteria hold without Zariski density. We verify the criteria explicitly for cusped Hitchin representations and real-hyperbolic self-joinings.

papers.title: Mixed Third-Order Flux Laws for Dual Cascade in the Stochastic SQG Equation
papers.authors: Rongchang Liu, Kening Lu, Zexin Wang
papers.abstract: We study dual-cascade flux laws for the stochastic forced--dissipative surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equation on a large periodic box. For statistically stationary solutions, under a weak anomalous dissipation assumption, we derive rigorous mixed third-order structure-function laws for the dual cascade: a Yaglom-type law for the direct cascade of surface potential energy (SPE) and a mixed flux law for the inverse cascade of the Hamiltonian. We further establish complementary scaling laws: a cubic small-scale law for the Hamiltonian structure function and a large-scale vanishing law for the SPE structure function. In particular, both Hamiltonian laws appear to be new for SQG even as an explicit third-order structure-function relation. We also prove Onsager-type obstruction results showing that sufficiently regular stationary families cannot sustain the corresponding non-zero fluxes: $B^s_{3,\infty}$-regularity above the Onsager threshold $1/3$ rules out the direct SPE flux, while sufficient low-frequency Besov regularity rules out the inverse Hamiltonian flux. These results provide a rigorous formulation of the SQG dual-cascade phenomenology in a stochastic stationary setting.

papers.title: Commutative algebras satisfying univariate identities with vanishing Peirce polynomial
papers.authors: Daniel J. F. Fox, Vladimir G. Tkachev
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies $(2,3)$-palintropic algebras, a class of commutative algebras defined by the identity $(x^{2})^3 - (x^{3})^2 = 0$. This specific relation is the simplest generator of the $2$-dimensional space of minimal-degree evanescent identities in degree $6$, and encompasses several well-studied structures, including Jordan and medial algebras. The primary motivation for investigating these algebras lies in their trivial Peirce polynomials, which removes a priori restrictions on the spectrum of the multiplication operator associated with an idempotent. This paper reviews and further develops the theory of Peirce operators, Peirce polynomials, and second-order linearizations. It shows that despite the triviality of the Peirce polynomial, any idempotent $c$ admits well-behaved, explicit fusion rules for multiplication between its $\lambda$-Peirce spaces for $\lambda \neq \tfrac{1}{2}$. Furthermore, multiplication by a nonsingular idempotent is an algebra homomorphism. Finally, there are given concrete examples of $(2,3)$-palintropic algebras, together with applications of these algebraic structures to commutative polynomial maps.

papers.title: Dirichlet-Neumann waveform relaxation for heterogeneous heat equations: continuous and time discrete L2 analysis
papers.authors: Philipp Birken, Martin J. Gander, Niklas Kotarsky, Lu-di Lu
papers.abstract:
We consider two coupled linear heat equations on different spatial domains that interact through a lower dimensional interface. This models conjugate heat transfer. The problem is solved using Dirichlet--Neumann waveform relaxation. This allows us to couple separate codes for the subproblems, a so-called partitioned approach. Our overall goal is to develop more efficient partitioned methods, and to this end, we want reliable error estimates.
  We use an exponentially weighted Fourier technique to derive new error estimates in $L^2$ for finite time $T$ in both continuous and time-discrete settings. We identify an optimized relaxation parameter that guarantees superlinear convergence. Our new continuous estimate predicts linear convergence when $k^2/T$ is small, and superlinear when $k^2/T$ is large, with $k$ the iteration index. Our new time-discrete estimate closely mirrors its continuous counterpart for small $\Delta t$. Otherwise, we obtain linear convergence for large $k$. We also show that convergence is fast when the contrast is large, provided that the small physical parameter domain (e.g. air) is using the Dirichlet transmission condition, and the large physical parameter domain (e.g. steel) is using the Neumann transmission condition in the Dirichlet-Neumann waveform relaxation method. Numerical experiments confirm these findings, and we demonstrate the relevance on the analysis for a nonlinear conjugate heat transfer test case.

papers.title: A conformal reduction for the X-ADM mass
papers.abstract:
The X-ADM mass is a generalisation of the ADM mass for asymptotically flat manifolds, recently introduced by Mantegazza and Oronzio [arXiv:2602.11372], who proved a positive mass theorem for this quantity in dimension $3$ under a certain topological condition. In this article, we prove the X-positive mass theorem with rigidity in all dimensions $n\geq3$ without any topological restrictions.
  To this end, we first prove that the scalar curvature condition appearing in the X-positive mass theorem implies the metric is of positive Yamabe type. We then show that the X-ADM mass of the given metric is equal to the ADM mass of a scalar-flat representative in its conformal class plus a term that is explicitly non-negative. From this, the X-positive mass theorem follows from the standard positive mass theorem. As a corollary, we obtain the Riemannian mass--charge inequality of general relativity in all dimensions, which was previously only known for spin manifolds. Finally, we give a version of the X-positive mass theorem for a manifold with boundary.

papers.title: The Fock Space Dynamics of Causal Fermion Systems: Non-Abelian Gauge Fields
papers.authors: Claudio Dappiaggi, Felix Finster, Niky Kamran, Moritz Reintjes
papers.abstract: A limiting case is worked out in which the causal action principle for causal fermion systems describing Minkowski space gives rise to the linear Fock space dynamics of perturbative quantum field theory, including non-abelian gauge fields and Dirac fields.

papers.title: Integrability of a composition of functions
papers.abstract: The paper deals with the Riemann and Lebesgue integrability of functions. Sufficient conditions and criteria are stated for the integrability of a composition of functions. Relevant counterexamples are constructed based on Cantor's perfect sets and the Cantor staircase function. The main tool of research is Lebesgue's criterion for Riemann integrability.

papers.title: Weights and characters for affine Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: Weights play an essential role in the classification of simple modules for affine Hecke algebras. In this paper we show the extent to which weights determine simple modules and relate this to induction and restriction along isogenies. We also describe the behaviour of hermitian duals and unitarity under induction and restriction along isogenies.

papers.title: Regularity of Manhattan manifolds and exact dimensionality for relatively Anosov groups
papers.abstract: We establish several results about Patterson--Sullivan measures for relatively Anosov groups. First, we prove that these measures are exact dimensional with respect to visual metrics induced by Gromov models in the Groves--Manning quasi-isometry class. Under the additional assumption that the group is relatively Morse, we show that the associated scalar Cartan metric is Gromov hyperbolic and that the corresponding boundary premetric is a visual metric to which the exact-dimensionality theorem applies. Second, we prove that their Manhattan manifolds are $C^1$-regular, from which we deduce that the growth indicator is $C^1$-regular and strictly concave on the interior of the limit cone. This extends the case of Anosov representations by Kim--Oh--Wang. Our methods are dynamical, and we exploit the fact due to Kim--Oh and Blayac--Canary--Zhu--Zimmer that Bowen--Margulis--Sullivan measures for relatively Anosov groups are finite and mixing.

papers.title: Rigidity of multisections to the universal cubic plane curve
papers.abstract: We study the following question of Farb: For which positive integers n is it possible to choose n distinct points continuously on every smooth cubic plane curve? This paper is a continuation of the work of Banerjee-Chen. We prove that such choice is unique up to homotopy for n=27 (smallest open case), and does not exist for n=36k+18.

papers.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
papers.authors: Jiaoyang Huang, Zhonggen Su, Ruizhe Xu
papers.abstract: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.

papers.title: Normal form method of center-focus problem in piecewise-smooth systems and algorithm design
papers.authors: Xingwu Chen, Jiahao Li, Tao Li
papers.abstract: We investigate the normal form method in piecewise-smooth monodromic systems to distinguish center from focus and determine the order of focus as well as degenerate Hopf bifurcations. For the normal form of piecewise-smooth monodromic systems given in previous publications in the sense of topologically equivalence, we prove the algebraic equivalence between the Lyapunov constants of the original piecewise-smooth system and the coefficient series of its normal form. With this algebraic equivalence, we prefer to compute the normal form coefficient series to avoid cumbersome integrals of trigonometric functions in the computation of Lyapunov constants, and find the relations of foci of the piecewise-smooth system and its subsystems: among the orders and among the stabilities. Moreover, we design algorithms for computing the normal form coefficient series and combine them with the obtained stability relation to construct stabilizing switching signals for state-dependent switched nonlinear systems, one basic problem in the control theory.

papers.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
papers.abstract:
We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$.
  The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha)$, the {\em isosceles-$\beta$} shape, in which $3\alpha+2\beta = \pi$ and $\alpha$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree.
  The shape $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha+\beta)$ (where $3\alpha + 3\beta = \pi$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.

papers.title: Non-kinetic homotopy coherent actions on four-manifolds
papers.authors: Sungkyung Kang, JungHwan Park, Masaki Taniguchi
papers.abstract: We give the first example of a non-kinetic smooth homotopy coherent action of order two on a closed simply connected smooth four-manifold. This action is obtained by restricting a nontrivial smooth homotopy coherent action of the discrete circle group on a stabilized $K3$ surface. We also construct relatively non-kinetic smooth homotopy coherent extensions of boundary involutions over compact smooth $4$-manifolds. In addition, we exhibit boundary involutions that admit locally linear topological extensions but no smooth extensions over the same stabilized fillings. Nevertheless, we prove a Wall-type theorem showing that every free involution on a disjoint union of integral homology spheres extends smoothly over any simply connected smooth filling after sufficiently many stabilizations by $S^2\times S^2$.

papers.title: Congruence of Dirac operators with applications to generalized MIT bag models
papers.abstract: We highlight a simple congruence transform that shifts coupling parameters for Dirac operators with shell interactions. As one of the consequences, this leads to new observations concerning the self-adjointness and the infinite mass interpretation of generalized MIT bag models.

papers.title: Poincar\'e Beta Balls: Radial Laws, Hyperbolic Shell Metric Transforms, and Critical-Limit Regimes
papers.abstract: On a high-dimensional Poincar\'e ball, a Euclidean beta-type radial measure concentrates near a sphere, but hyperbolic distance amplifies the surviving radial spread, so the usual shell reduction loses part of the limiting metric. In each regime of the balance between this radial width and amplified angular separation, we determine the weak pyramid limit of the spaces rescaled at the order at which the transition between concentration and dissipation occurs. The four critical-limit regimes are the shifted-exponential railway pyramid, the diameter-at-most-one regime, the nonlinear Gaussian-transform regime, and the Gaussian regime. Each finite-branch railway mm-space generating the first pyramid has branches from a common center, a shifted exponential distribution along them, and paths between different branches through the center. We also give a sharp criterion for convergence to the diameter-at-most-one pyramid. The resulting classification identifies the precise critical scales and clarifies when angular and radial fluctuations contribute simultaneously to the limiting geometry.

papers.title: Green Cell-Free Massive MIMO for ISAC: Joint Cloud, Fronthaul and Radio Resource Allocation
papers.authors: Zinat Behdad, \"Ozlem Tu\u{g}fe Demir, Ki Won Sung, Pei Xiao, Cicek Cavdar
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a cross-layer end-to-end (E2E) resource orchestration framework for green cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with distributed multi-target detection. We propose a distributed sensing approach in which receive access points (RX-APs) compute local test statistics, which are aggregated at the cloud using weights based on sensing interference and channel quality. We derive the local maximum a posteriori ratio test (MAPRT) detectors under fully informed and partially informed operation, representing different levels of transmit-signal information at the RX-APs. We further characterize their processing and fronthaul requirements and derive a network power model incorporating radio transmission, AP and cloud processing, and fronthaul infrastructure. We formulate a mixed-integer non-convex problem that jointly optimizes transmit powers, AP modes, user equipment (UE) and sensing-area associations, RX-AP assignments, and active fronthaul and cloud resources subject to communication, sensing, power, processing-capacity, and fronthaul constraints. A two-stage iterative algorithm based on Big-M reformulation, convex- concave programming, penalty-based relaxation, and structured discrete recovery is developed. Numerical results show that the proposed E2E framework reduces total power by up to 50% compared with transmit-power-only optimization and by approximately 11-17% compared with joint radio optimization under full coordination, while maintaining detection probabilities above 0:95.

papers.title: The Follow-the-Leader scheme with non-monotone velocity
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the approximation of entropy solutions to a one-dimensional scalar conservation law via the so-called Follow-the-Leader particle scheme in case the velocity map is \emph{non monotone}. The result is based on a discrete maximum principle, on $BV$ estimates of the approximated density, and on the characterization of the limit as entropy solution in the sense of Kru\v zkov.

papers.title: Hypergraphs on Riemannian manifolds and their double homology
papers.abstract: In this paper, by constructing double homology for graded submanifolds of $\Delta$-manifolds, we study the double homology of hyper(di)graphs on Riemannian manifolds. With the help of the canonical projection $\pi$ from ordered sequences to their underlying unordered sets, we prove a commutative diagram of the double homology and a commutative diagram of the spaces of differential forms of hyper(di)graphs on Riemannian manifolds. Moreover, we give some relations between the fundamental group(oid)s of hyper(di)graphs on surfaces and the (pure) braid groups on surfaces by certain homomorphisms induced from $\pi$. As applications, we study the homotopy types of filtrations for packings and coverings of balls on Riemannian manifolds with hypergraph constraints, and we characterize regular maps on Riemannian manifolds by geometric realizations of the independence complexes and hypergraphs on the manifolds.

papers.title: On a boundary value problem related to radiative heat transfer
papers.abstract: We consider the boundary value problem $y''=\kappa^2y^n, y(0)=1, y(1)=0,$ relevant to radiative heat transfer, chemical reactions, etc. We use upper/lower envelopes to study the qualitative and quantitative dependence of its solution on parameters, and transform it into an easily solvable initial value problem.

papers.title: Two problems of SI-compact spaces
papers.abstract: Zhao and Ho use the irreducible open cover family respected with the Scott topology to introduce the SI-compactness. It has been proved that the SI-compactness is strictly stronger than compactness. In this paper, we prove that the arbitrary product of SI-compact spaces is always SI-compact which gives a positive answer for the question posed by Zhao and Ho. Furthermore, we show that the category of all SI-compact spaces is not a reflective full subcategory of TOP.

papers.title: Near-Rings and Skew Braces
papers.authors: Riccardo Aragona, Norberto Gavioli, Martina Iannaccone, Giuseppe Nozzi
papers.abstract: This paper provides a deeper analysis of Rump's correspondence between near-rings and skew braces. We show that, under a topological assumption on the structure of a near-ring, Rump's correspondence is invertible and it is always possible to construct an associated skew brace. Furthermore, we provide several examples where this topological assumption is fulfilled in well-known algebraic structures such as the Nottingham group, groups of triangular functions, iterated wreath products of arbitrary groups, and groups of IA-automorphisms of free nilpotent groups.

papers.title: Quantitative uniqueness for bi-Laplace equations with potentials
papers.authors: Long Teng, Zhiwei Wang, Jiuyi Zhu
papers.abstract: We study quantitative unique continuation for bi-Laplace equations \[\Delta^{2}u+V(x)u=0 \] by introducing some new weighted frequency functions. We establish quantitative three-ball inequalities and vanishing-order bounds for bounded and H\"older continuous potentials. Three-ball inequalities are built on rescaling invariant weighted frequency functions. The vanishing order results are shown by related, but different weighted frequency functions.

papers.title: Exponential Contraction for Underdamped Langevin Diffusions with Superlinear Forces
papers.abstract: We establish exponential contraction for underdamped Langevin diffusions with nonconvex confining potentials and possibly superlinear forces. The force satisfies a polynomial local Lipschitz bound with exponent $\ell\geq0$, and the potential has a lower bound of order $m\geq2$, with $3\ell<2m$. Under radial confinement and a potential--dissipation inequality, we construct an explicit weighted Kantorovich transportation cost in which the Markov semigroup contracts probability laws exponentially. The estimate holds for all nonnegative times, with prefactor one and an explicit positive rate, without a smallness condition on the local Lipschitz coefficient. The proof combines localized reflection--synchronous coupling with an exponential Lyapunov weight. A radius-dependent shift of the position--velocity difference balances the local force contribution to the distance drift, while distinct localization scales in position and velocity exploit the growth of the potential. Together, these choices yield a dissipative estimate for the weighted cost with a vanishing regularization error. The regularized couplings preserve the Langevin marginals, so passage to weak limits yields contraction for all initial laws with finite transportation cost. Consequently, the dynamics converge exponentially to the Gibbs measure within the corresponding finite-cost class. The assumptions include quartic double-well potentials of arbitrary amplitude. Numerical experiments for asymmetric quartic wells examine transportation between two initial laws and quantify the conservatism of the explicit rate.

papers.title: Categorification of the genus two DAHA
papers.authors: Semeon Arthamonov, Ievgen Makedonskyi, Daniil Sarafannikov
papers.abstract: We construct three derived endofunctors on the derived category of graded integrable representations of the current algebra of a flat degeneration of $D(2|1,\alpha)$, and prove that their classes in the Grothendieck group are the genus two Macdonald operators. Computing the graded $\operatorname{Ext}$ pairing explicitly, we deduce the self-adjointness of the genus two Macdonald operators and the orthogonality of genus $2$ Macdonald polynomials with respect to the certain skew-bilinear form.

papers.title: Strauss and Glassey exponents for semilinear wave equations with a non-effective and not scattering producing damping
papers.authors: Wanderley Nunes do Nascimento, Alessandro Palmieri
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study the Cauchy problems for a semilinear damped wave equation with a time-dependent coefficient for the damping term belonging to the class of non-effective damping terms with critical decay rates involving iterated logarithmic factors. As nonlinearities we consider both $|u|^p$ and $|u_t|^p$.
  Assuming nonnegative and compactly supported initial data, we establish the blow-up for weak solutions in the sub-Strauss range $1 < p \leq p_{\mathrm{Str}}(n)$ for the power of the nonlinear term $|u|^p$. The proof in the sub-critical case relies on an iteration frame for the space average of the solution, obtained by employing a time-dependent multiplier related to the coefficient of the damping term. On the other hand, in the limit case $p=p_{\mathrm{Str}}(n)$, we work with solutions of the homogeneous equation with separated variables, and we investigate the properties of a fundamental system of solutions for the corresponding time-dependent ODE, in order to derive an iteration frame for a suitable weighted space average of the solution. Finally, for the derivative type nonlinearity $|u_t|^p$ we prove the blow-up of weak solutions in the sub-Glassey range $1 < p \leq \frac{n+1}{n-1}$ by using a comparison argument for a suitable time-dependent function associated with the corresponding local in time solution.

papers.title: A problem for isolated singularities of surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbf R^n$ be a set of dimension $2$ with an isolated singular point $0$, such that $E-\{0\}$ is an orientable $\mathcal C^2$ submanifold of $\mathbf R^n$ of dimension $2$, and hence a Riemann surface with the conformal structure induced by the ambient metric. We study the extension of its conformal structure across $0$, under hypotheses that are metric rather than analytic. Denoting by $S(0,r)$ the sphere of radius $r$ centred at $0$, we call the singularity $0$ $\mathit{M\text{-}regular}$ if (i) the pair $(E-\{0\},\{0\})$ satisfies a Whitney condition (the radial direction becomes asymptotically tangent to $E-\{0\}$ at $0$) and (ii) the length of the spherical slice $S(0,r)\cap E$ is bounded above by a linear function of $r$ for small $r$ ($\mathit{metric\ decay}$). The main result (1989) is that an $M$-regular singularity is $\mathit{conformally\ point\text{-}like}$, that is, a punctured neighbourhood of $0$ in $E$ is conformal to the punctured unit disc $\Delta^*$, so that the conformal structure extends across $0$. The proof uses the modulus of rings (extremal length), which generalizes the classical planar technique to $2$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Two classes of surfaces are shown to be conformally point-like: all surfaces of revolution generated by a single $C^1$ curve, and orientable subanalytic sets of dimension $2$ with isolated singularities, for which $M$-regularity is proven directly from Hironaka's structure theory. In this case the metric decay condition follows from a direct estimate of the volume of the slices $S(0,r)\cap E$ (Lemma 7.5), based on Hironaka's Whitney theorem and Stasica's decomposition into $L$-analytic pieces. A further original result is a $C^\infty$ counterexample showing that a strict Whitney condition alone does $\mathit{not}$ imply the linear length bound: the two hypotheses defining $M$-regularity are independent.

papers.title: Hopf type theorem for surfaces of constant weighted mean curvature in Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We consider compact immersed surfaces of genus zero in a three-dimensional smooth metric measure space $(M^3,g,e^{-f}\mathrm{d}V_{g})$. We introduce a new weighted mean curvature and prove that any such surface whose weighted mean curvature is constant must be totally umbilical, provided that a condition relating the Ricci curvature of $M$ and the weight function $f$ is satisfied. We also give an application of this result to surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfying $|x|^{2} H + 2\langle x,\nu \rangle = c$.

papers.title: On the sum of least prime factors in short intervals
papers.abstract:
Let $p(n)$ denote the least prime factor of $n$ and $L_C(x)=Cx^{1/2}(\log x)^2$ with $C>0$. The sum of $p(n)/n$ over composite $n$ lying in the short interval $[x,\,x+L_C(x)]$, a question raised by Erd\H{o}s and Graham, is studied.
  (i) The constant $c=8$ in the mean asymptotic is estimated \[ S(x)=\sum_{{n<x,\ n\ \text{composite}}}\frac{p(n)}{n}=\frac{c\,x^{1/2}}{(\log x)^2}\Bigl(1+O\Bigl(\frac1{\log x}\Bigr)\Bigr) +O\Bigl(\frac{x^{1/3}}{\log x}\Bigr). \]
  (ii) For every fixed $C>0$, the window sums $\mu_C(x):=\sum_{x\le n\le x+L_C(x)}p(n)/n$ over composites have mean $4C$: $\frac1X\sum_{x\le X}\mu_C(x)=4C+O_C(1/\log X)$, and second moment $\frac1X\sum_{x\le X}(\mu_C(x)-4C)^2=O_C(1)$.
  (iii)Under the Maier-consistent bounded-fluctuation hypothesis, $\mu_C(x)=4C+O_C(1)$ holds uniformly in $x$, and the Erd\H{o}s--Graham question has an affirmative answer. Unconditionally, the uniform statement remains open; proving it would require resolving short-interval prime estimates at scale $(\log y)^2$.

papers.title: An Explicit Belyi Map for the Wiman Sextic and Cusp Forms for a Noncongruence Subgroup
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explicitly determine an algebraic Belyi function on a unique smooth projective model $\widetilde{W}$ of the Wiman sextic curve $W$ and describe its complex uniformization in terms of modular functions associated with a certain noncongruence subgroup $\Gamma_{\widetilde{W}} \subset {\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. As an application, we give a direct proof of the unbounded denominators conjecture for weight $2$ cusp forms with respect to $\Gamma_{\widetilde{W}}$. The conjecture is now known in full generality by the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang, following earlier progress including work of Dong, Lin, and Ng. Our proof, however, uses a degeneration of $\widetilde{W}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{5}$ together with explicit Puiseux series expansions and is substantially different from the methods employed in their work.

papers.title: Families of relative periodic orbits in the planar three-body problem via consecutive alignments
papers.authors: Joan Gimeno, Marc Jorba-Cusc\'o, Bego\~na Nicol\'as
papers.abstract:
Relative periodic orbits (RPOs) are solutions of the three-body problem that are periodic in a uniformly rotating reference frame and, in general, quasi-periodic in inertial coordinates. We present a numerical procedure for computing and continuing one-parameter families of RPOs of the planar Newtonian three-body problem.
  The method exploits consecutive syzygies, understood here as configurations in which the three bodies are aligned and their velocities satisfy the corresponding symmetry conditions. Matching the positions and momenta at two consecutive alignments reduces the computation of RPOs to a low-dimensional nonlinear problem. Its solutions are then numerically continued, and linear stability is determined from the nontrivial eigenvalues of the rotated monodromy matrix after removing the neutral directions associated with conserved quantities and continuous symmetries.
  The procedure is applied to several mass distributions and initial configurations, producing families of Poincar\'e, Hill, and binary-type solutions. These families exhibit transitions from nearly circular to highly eccentric motion, changes of stability near resonances and turning points, and absolute periodic solutions when the rotation angle is a rational multiple of 2{\pi}. In the Hill families, the continuation connects satellite configurations with circumstellar motion as the smallest body loses its gravitational binding to the intermediate body. Circumbinary and circumstellar configurations are also obtained in the binary regime.
  The results illustrate the dynamical diversity of RPOs and provide coherent three-body motions that can be used as prescribed trajectories in restricted four-body models.

papers.title: Fully fractional Schr\"odinger equations with memory: well-posedness via extension
papers.abstract: We study the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with memory $\Le^s u=\mu|u|^{p-1}u$ for $t>0$, where $\Le^s=(\partial_t-i\Delta_x)^s$, $0<s<1$, and the solution is prescribed for all $t\le0$. We identify a Hilbert space of histories and prove local well-posedness for $1<p\le p_*(s)=1+4s/(d+2-2s)$, with global solutions for sufficiently small histories at the critical exponent. We also establish the passage from this memory problem to the classical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation as $s\uparrow1$. For every fixed Schwartz history and $1<p\le1+4/d$, including the classical mass critical exponent, the memory solutions converge in $C([0,T];L^2\cap L^{p+1})$ to the classical solution with initial value $u_0(\cdot,0)$, for every finite $T$ below its maximal existence time. Thus the limiting evolution depends on the prescribed past only through its value at time zero. Our construction uses an oscillatory Poisson extension and an exact identity expressing the weighted $L^2$ norm of the lifted initial datum in terms of the history. This identity allows us to apply the boundary estimates of our earlier work to the memory problem. We recover $\Le^s$ as a weighted Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and establish the corresponding extension bounds on $L^2$ for $0<s\le\frac12$, and from $\operatorname{Dom}(\Le^s)$ to $L^2$ for $\frac12<s<1$.

papers.title: Relative $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules and $p$-adic differential equations
papers.authors: Hansheng Diao, Yong Suk Moon, Zijian Yao
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an affinoid rigid analytic space over a $p$-adic field, equipped with a suitable \'etale map to a unit polydisk. We provide a formalism of \emph{imperfect relative period rings} over $X$, which lie inside the corresponding perfect relative period rings constructed by Kedlaya--Liu. Then we establish a relative version of the Fontaine--Cherbonnier--Colmez equivalence between $p$-adic local systems on $X$ and \'etale $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules over such imperfect relative period rings, generalizing previous works of Andreatta--Brinon and others. Using this equivalence, we construct $p$-adic differential equations attached to de Rham local systems, carrying both geometric and arithmetic differential operators. This generalizes the work of Berger to the relative geometric setting. Along the way, we study a relative Fontaine--Sen theory on the decompletion of $\Gamma$-modules over the relative $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-period rings.

papers.title: On the Hilbert Series and Multiplicity of Generalized Binomial Edge Ideals
papers.abstract: In this article, we compute the Hilbert series of the generalized binomial edge ideal associated with the join of two graphs. Consequently, we compute the Hilbert series of complete $r$-partite graphs. Further, we show that if a vertex satisfies a certain degree condition, then some Hilbert coefficients remain unchanged upon its removal. This provides a reduction technique for computing them. As an application, we compute the dimension and multiplicity of several classes of graphs.

papers.title: The Shubin--Vakilian--Wolff Uncertainty Principle at Half Density
papers.abstract: Shubin, Vakilian, and Wolff proved a Fourier uncertainty principle for sets of sufficiently small local density at the reciprocal scale and asked whether every density below one is admissible. We answer this question negatively in dimension one by constructing sequences of pairs of $1/2$-density thin sets and unit vectors whose total position and Fourier mass outside these sets tends to zero. This obstruction persists for every scaled reciprocal profile $\rho_\kappa(x)=\min\{1,\kappa/|x|\}$, $\kappa>0$. On the other hand, for $0<\kappa\le1$, the uncertainty estimate holds whenever the density $$ \varepsilon<\frac{1}{2(1+32\kappa)}. $$ Thus the critical density tends to $1/2$ as $\kappa\downarrow 0$. The obstruction uses odd Gaussian packets to transfer norm bounds from a free-group model. The positive estimate uses a Fourier-complementary anti-Wick operator and quadratic straightening of the reciprocal geometry.

papers.title: A Local Proof of Langlands's Second Main Lemma for Local Epsilon Factors over Nonarchimedean Local Fields
papers.abstract: We give a local proof of Langlands's Second Main Lemma for local epsilon factors over nonarchimedean local fields. The lemma compares the induction expressions attached to compatible characters of distinct intermediate fields of prime degree in a bicyclic extension of prime-square degree. It is one of the main identities used in Langlands's construction of epsilon factors of local Weil representations. The proof builds on the work of Dwork, Lakkis, and Langlands. The main new point in the present paper is the wild dyadic case, i.e. biquadratic extensions over a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic two. This completes the proof of the Second Main Lemma, including the equal-characteristic case. Finally, together with the local proof of the First Main Lemma and Langlands's remaining reductions, we obtain a purely local construction of local epsilon factors envisioned by Langlands.

papers.title: Strategic Index Reconstitution: Differential Games, Closed-Loop Equilibria and Mean-Field Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study a continuous-time, multiasset trading game around index reconstitution, in which opportunistic traders have heterogeneous beliefs about the future index constitution and interact through transient cross-asset price impact and instantaneous execution costs. Opportunistic traders build inventory based on their individual beliefs about the future index constitution before a public announcement, adjust their positions to the revealed composition, and unwind them against the indexer's prescribed rebalancing trades at the implementation date when the new index composition takes effect. Under a no-price-manipulation condition, we construct a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium. Its affine feedback policies are computed from a non-standard matrix Riccati equation and linear ODEs whose number and dimensions are independent of population size. Under mean-field scaling, we construct a mean-field equilibrium and obtain quantitative convergence and approximate-Nash bounds. Numerical illustrations show that greater competition among opportunists dampens price swings around implementation and that opportunistic trading lowers the indexer's implementation shortfall unless price resilience is very low. Holding the average belief fixed, greater belief dispersion can increase gross trading volume without changing net aggregate opportunist holdings or price impact.

papers.title: Regular Sublattices, O Closed Ideals and Dedekind MacNeille Completions
papers.abstract: We study regular sublattices of lattices that satisfy the Join-Infinite Distributive Law (JID) under Dedekind MacNeille completion. Using order convergence, we identify the lattice of O-closed ideals with Crawleys completion, and compare it with the Dedekind MacNeille completion. When DM(L) satisfies (JID), this comparison yields extension results for lattice homomorphisms. In particular, if Y is a regular sublattice of a complete lattice L, and L and DM(Y) satisfy (JID), then the canonical extension lattice-embeds DM(Y) into L with join-regular image. We also give a sharp finite-dimensional obstruction: there exists an infinitely distributive regular sublattice of R3 whose Dedekind MacNeille completion is not distributive, and therefore cannot be lattice embedded in R3. In contrast, we prove that the inclusion of every join-regular sublattice of R2 with a least and a greatest element extends canonically to a lattice embedding of its MacNeille completion into R2.

papers.title: Transitive automorphism groups of maximal curves
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and let $X$ be a maximal curve of genus at least two over $\F_{q^2}$. We prove that the automorphism group of $X$ acts transitively on its rational points if and only if $X$ is the Hermitian curve, or $q=5$ and $X$ is the unique $\F_{25}$-maximal curve of genus $3$, namely the maximal Klein quartic. Together with the result of Giulietti and Korchm\'aros in characteristic two, this gives the classification for every prime power $q$. In particular, the Hermitian curve is the only maximal curve of genus at least two whose automorphism group is doubly transitive on its rational points.

papers.title: A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
papers.authors: Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(\Omega) \le \frac{\pi^{s-\frac{1}{2}}\Gamma\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)\Gamma\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partial\Omega)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

papers.title: Complete Self-Shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension with Positive Constant Scalar Curvature and $S\le 1$
papers.abstract: Let \(X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be an \(n\)-dimensional complete self-shrinker in arbitrary codimension \(p\ge 1\). Suppose that the scalar curvature \(R\) is a positive constant and that the squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form satisfies \(S\le 1\). We prove that \(S\equiv 1\) and that \(X\) is isometric to either the round sphere \(S^n(\sqrt n)\) or the standard generalized cylinder \(S^k(\sqrt k)\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\), \(2\le k\le n-1\). In particular, no new higher-codimension examples occur under these assumptions. The proof uses an algebraic lemma which yields a uniform positive lower bound for the Bakry--\'Emery Ricci curvature, together with the comparison theorem of Wei--Wylie, the equivalence of finite Gaussian volume and polynomial volume growth due to Cheng--Zhou, and the gap theorem of Cao--Li.

papers.title: Double-wells in a strong magnetic field: absence of tunneling for infinitely many values of the coupling constant
papers.authors: Kevin Buck, Charles L. Fefferman, Javier G\'omez-Serrano, Amaury Hayat, Jacob Shapiro, Michael I. Weinstein
papers.abstract: We prove the fixed-potential conjecture of Fefferman, Shapiro, and Weinstein for inversion-symmetric magnetic double wells. We construct a number $L_0>0$ and one smooth, compactly supported, nonpositive, nonradial single-well potential $v$, independent of both the coupling parameter $\lambda$ and the well displacement, such that for every fixed $L\ge L_0$ the associated magnetic double-well Hamiltonian has infinitely many exact degeneracies of its two lowest eigenvalues as $\lambda\to\infty$. The magnetic hopping coefficient also vanishes along an infinite sequence tending to infinity. The potential consists of a radial core and two small, reflection-related perturbations supported on one-sided quadratic cusps. Their log-flat profiles isolate two dominant hopping contributions, which we evaluate by steepest descent after inserting the radial ground-state asymptotics. The resulting asymptotic cosine expression, together with error bounds for the even--odd splitting, yields infinitely many exact eigenvalue crossings and changes of ground-state parity.

papers.title: A solution to a conjecture on the signless Laplacian spectral radius for $t$-color-critical graphs
papers.authors: Ming-Zhu Chen, Ya-Lei Jin, Peng-Li Zhang, Jian Zheng
papers.abstract: An induced matching is a matching that forms an induced subgraph. A graph is $t$-color-critical if removing some induced matching of size $t$ lowers its chromatic number, but removing any $t-1$ vertices does not. Let $F$ be a $t$-color-critical graph with $\chi(F)=r+1$. For sufficiently large $n$, Simonovits determined the unique edge-extremal $F$-free graph on $n$ vertices. Recently, Zheng, Li and Li [Linear Algebra Appl.\ 730 (2026) 546--565] conjectured that, for $t\ge 2$ and $r\ge 3$, the join $K_{t-1}\vee T_{n-t+1,r}$ uniquely maximizes the signless Laplacian spectral radius among all $n$-vertex $F$-free graphs when $n$ is sufficiently large. In this paper, we prove this conjecture. In contrast to the usual spectral arguments, our proof of this conjecture relies on two techniques of a rather different flavour. Our first technique is an analogue of Zykov symmetrization for the signless Laplacian matrix. Our second technique is an induction on $n$, from which we obtain the lower bound on the smallest entry of the Perron vector of a signless Laplacian spectral extremal graph rather than a structural statement.

papers.title: Sharp $L^2$ estimates for wave equations with non-integrable speeds
papers.abstract: We study the large-time behavior of the displacement for wave equations with non-integrable speeds and zero initial displacement. For initial velocities in $L^2\cap L^1$, we derive an $L^2$ upper bound under a weighted Poincar\'e inequality and symbol estimates up to order two on the propagation speed. The rate is determined by the speed and its time integral. For these speeds, an additional symbol estimate for the third derivative and the nonzero mean condition on the initial velocity give a lower bound of the same order, obtained without using an explicit formula for the Fourier multiplier. At the endpoint $a(t)=(1+t)^{-1}$, the sharp rate is $t(\ln t)^{-\frac{n}{4}}$. The estimates apply to polynomial, logarithmically modified, oscillating, and exponential-type speeds.

papers.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for unregularized Vlasov-Riesz-Fokker-Planck systems
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for the unregularized repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck system on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$. For product initial data and potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$, we obtain an algebraic convergence rate for the $k$-particle marginals on a time interval independent of the particle number. The constants grow at most exponentially in $k$. The three-dimensional Coulomb case gives every rate $N^{-b}$ with $0<b<1/3$. The assumptions on its limiting solution hold for weighted Sobolev data with a Gaussian velocity moment and, on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a polynomial spatial moment. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law, auxiliary particle equations, and weighted BBGKY estimates. An $L^1$ estimate and pointwise exponential energy bounds control the remainder flux in weighted $L^q$. For correlated initial data satisfying pointwise energy and marginal error bounds, the comparison extends to $0<s<d-1$.

papers.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
papers.abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.

papers.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic half-wave equation on the torus
papers.abstract: We construct global solutions of the defocusing cubic half-wave equation on the torus whose $H^s$ norms grow exponentially for every $1/2<s<3/2$. Such solutions exist at every positive mass. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first example of a genuine infinite cascade for a defocusing fractional nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the torus. In particular, our result resolves an open question posed by G\'erard and Grellier concerning the existence of unbounded Sobolev trajectories for the defocusing cubic half-wave equation on the torus.

papers.title: Resilience of rainbow Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs
papers.authors: Elad Aigner-Horev, Dan Hefetz, Yury Person
papers.abstract:
We prove that every spanning subgraph $H$ of an $n$-vertex $(p,\beta)$-bijumbled graph, satisfying $\delta(H)\geq(1/2+\varepsilon)pn$, where $\varepsilon > 0$ is arbitrarily small yet fixed, admits a rainbow Hamilton cycle under any globally $\mu pn$-bounded colouring, provided that $\beta\leq cpn$ and $pn\geq M$, where $\mu$, $c$, and $M$ are positive constants depending solely on $\varepsilon$; in particular, $pn$ may be taken to be a sufficiently large constant. This answers a question of Coulson, Keevash, Perarnau and Yepremyan for random graphs and extends it to deterministic pseudorandom hosts.
  In fact, we prove that $H$ admits at least $(apn)^n$ rainbow Hamilton cycles, where $a > 0$ is a constant depending solely on $\varepsilon$. If $pn\geq D\log n$, then, upon fixing a coloured $H$, retaining each edge independently with probability $D\log n/(pn)$ preserves rainbow Hamiltonicity asymptotically almost surely. The logarithmic degree requirement is needed only for this percolation conclusion.
  All three conclusions also hold with rainbowness replaced by avoidance of prescribed pairs of edges, provided that each edge has at most $\mu pn$ conflicting partners. Our proofs use spread measures and the lopsided local lemma.

papers.title: Norms of the Hilbert Matrix Operator on Some Analytic Function Spaces
papers.authors: Puyu Cui, Zhaopeng Lin, Yufeng Lu, Shanli Ye
papers.abstract: For $\mathcal H:\mathcal B^\alpha\to\mathcal B^\alpha$ with $1<\alpha<2$, we obtain an exact norm representation. In particular, the norm is given by an explicit Gamma-function formula for $1<\alpha\leq3/2$, whereas for $3/2<\alpha<2$ it strictly exceeds the corresponding Gamma-function expression. For $\mathcal H:\mathcal B^\alpha\to\mathcal B^\alpha_{\log}$, we determine the exact norm: it is equal to $3/2$ for $1<\alpha\leq4/3$ and is given by an explicit Gamma-function formula for $4/3<\alpha<2$. We also determine the exact norm of $\mathcal H:H^1\to H^1_{\log}$ and show that it is equal to $\pi$. Finally, for $0<\alpha<1$, we determine the exact norm of $\mathcal H:H^\infty_\alpha\to\mathcal B^{\alpha+1}$, which is given by an explicit Gamma-function formula.

papers.title: Solubility from a disconnected common-divisor graph on $p$-regular conjugacy-class sizes
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $p$ be a prime. We prove that if the common-divisor graph on the nontrivial conjugacy-class sizes of $p$-regular elements of $G$ is disconnected, then $G$ is soluble. This settles the remaining case identified by Camina and collaborators. Their structure results provide an abelian normal $p'$-subgroup $M$. We choose a noncentral $r$-element $x\in M$, with $r\ne p$, such that $[G:C_G(x)]$ is coprime to $pr$, and show that $C_G(x)/M$ is a $\{p,r\}$-group. Thus $C_G(x)/M$ is a Hall $\{p,r\}$-subgroup of $G/M$. The separation between the two graph components then implies that every $p$-regular conjugacy-class size in $G/M$ has all its prime divisors in $\{p,r\}$. A theorem of Dolfi and Lucido, together with Burnside's $p^a q^b$-theorem, yields the solubility of $G/M$ and hence of $G$.

papers.title: Moment Ambiguity and the Limits of Robust Stochastic Optimization
papers.authors: Andr\'es Cristi, Matteo Russo, Jiechen Zhang
papers.abstract:
We study fundamental information-theoretic limits of robust stochastic optimization when the distribution is known only through its exact moment sequence. We develop a unified framework that produces families of distinct distributions sharing all moments yet inducing radically different optimal decisions, thereby establishing strong impossibility results for a range of decision problems under moment ambiguity.
  Our binary and $N$-way moment-matching constructions separate quantiles, threshold regions, and online selection opportunities while preserving every moment. For the newsvendor problem, moment equivalence causes quantile ambiguity, inducing any fixed or randomized order quantity to fail arbitrarily badly. For revenue maximization, no deterministic or randomized posted pricing scheme can secure a nontrivial approximation relative to the full-information benchmark.
  For the secretary problem with cardinal observations, the optimal robust success probability under exact moment disclosure is the classical finite-horizon value $s_m$, even for i.i.d. observations. This value converges to $1/e$, compared with the full-information limit of approximately $0.5801$ due to Gilbert and Mosteller (J. Am. Stat. Assoc., 1966).
  We also recover and expand upon the recent impossibility result of Correa et al. (STOC, 2026) for prophet inequalities with moment knowledge. For every fixed $r\ge1$, exact moment knowledge can yield at best a $\Theta(1/\log m)$ competitive ratio, even when competing against relaxed benchmarks based on expected $r$-th order statistics or when the algorithm is allowed to select $r$ items.

papers.title: Classification of $U(\mathfrak h)$-Free Modules over the Heisenberg-Virasoro type Lie superalgebra via Polynomial Shift Operators
papers.authors: Yan Kong, Haibo Chen, Yucai Su
papers.abstract: Let \(\mathcal L\) be the Heisenberg-Virasoro type Lie superalgebra whose even part is the twisted Heisenberg-Virasoro algebra and whose odd part is an abelian ideal. We classify \(\mathbb Z_2\)-graded \(\mathcal L\)-modules that are free of super-rank \(1|1\) over \(U(\mathfrak h)=\mathbb C[L_0,F_0]\). Using polynomial shift operators, we express the defining relations as functional equations for the matrix entries of the generators.
