Assuming the rank one classification for the even subalgebra, we show that, up to parity reversal, every module with nontrivial odd action belongs to a triangular family \(\Omega^+(\lambda,\beta,d)\), whereas every module with trivial odd action is a direct sum of two rank-one modules for the even subalgebra. We determine the graded isomorphism classes: within the triangular family, the coupling polynomial \(d\) is invariant up to multiplication by a non-zero scalar. We also describe canonical proper submodules and show that every module in the classification is reducible. In particular, we provide a new realization of the Heisenberg-Virasoro type Lie superalgebra using $2\times2$ matrices with entries associated with polynomial shift-differential operators.

papers.title: Obstructions to the ampleness of invariant jet differentials on complete intersections
papers.abstract:
We introduce the analogue, for invariant jet differentials, of the principal symbol of a differential operator: the component of maximal degree in the highest derivative. The top symbol identifies a canonical quotient bundle of the Demailly--Semple bundle $E_{k,m}T^*_X$, with values in jet differentials of lower order, and together with the Br\"uckmann--Rackwitz vanishing theorem it gives a non-ampleness criterion for $E_{k,m}T^*_Z$ on complete intersections $Z\subset\PP^N$. On the Demailly--Semple tower the top symbol is the restriction to a thickening of the vertical divisor, inside the singular jets.
  The criterion applies in orders $3$ and $4$: $E_{3,5q}T^*_X$ is not ample on any smooth hypersurface $X\subset\PP^4$, and $E_{4,m}T^*_X$ is not ample for $m\ge7$ with $m\equiv0,1,2\pmod 7$ on any smooth hypersurface $X\subset\PP^5$ of degree at least $2$. This contradicts the Diverio--Trapani conjecture at its own threshold.

papers.title: Entrywise nonnegativity of the inverse relative gain array in dimension six
papers.abstract: We prove that $(G\circ G^{-1})^{-1}$ is entrywise nonnegative for every real symmetric positive definite matrix $G$ of order at most six. Its entries are strictly positive exactly within the connected components of the nonzero-entry graph of $G$. An explicit rational example of order seven establishes sharpness. We give two complementary structural proofs. The analytic proof combines a trace obstruction with continuation of positive column forms and a bordering identity. The algebraic proof establishes a stronger four-dimensional polarized inequality through an explicit ten-square polynomial certificate. A common framework relates biquadratic positivity, column forms, positive semidefinite precision loads, and inverse relative gain array nonnegativity in consecutive dimensions. Further consequences include exact load-deficit identities, polynomial sum-of-squares certificates with the covariance fixed, and a reverse Schur--Horn majorization inequality with the same sharp dimension bound. In every dimension, sufficiently large powers of the inverse relative gain array are doubly stochastic.

papers.title: Systematic Codes Correcting Two Deletions with Three Redundant Symbols over Large Alphabets
papers.abstract: We construct systematic $q$-ary codes correcting two deletions with three redundant symbols over polynomial-size alphabets. For every information length $n\ge2$, our first construction has length $n+3$ over an alphabet of size $q=2^s<2^{32}n^7$ for some integer $s$, with polynomial-time encoding and decoding. A cardinality bound of Liu and Xing implies that three redundant symbols are necessary, so the construction is optimal in this measure. We also establish the existence of systematic codes with the same redundancy over alphabets of size $O(n^4)$, leaving efficient encoding and decoding at that alphabet scale open. For a single burst of at most two adjacent deletions, we give a polynomial-time systematic construction with three redundant symbols over a power-of-two alphabet of size $q<(n+2)^4$. A converse bound for adjacent deletions shows that three redundant symbols are again optimal for $n\ge2$.

papers.title: Non-freezing of the proximity digraph and non-pseudostable convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann--Krause models: Counterexamples to conjectures and results of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo
papers.authors: Peter Hegarty, Damiano Ognissanti, Edvin Wedin
papers.abstract: In 2012, Mirtabatabaei and Bullo studied heterogeneous Hegselmann--Krause models of opinion dynamics, where different agents may have different confidence or influence bounds. They conjectured that opinion vectors always converge, a fundamental problem that remains open. In support of this main conjecture they gave some partial results and made some auxiliary conjectures. Here we give counterexamples to two of these auxiliary conjectures, and even to one theorem in their paper. We explain why these disproved conjectures and false theorem nevertheless likely remain valid for almost all initial opinion vectors. In the last section (Section 7), we describe the role of AI in the production of the results in this paper.

papers.title: Rank-sensitive vertex bounds for semidefinite lifts
papers.abstract:
We study how the ranks of factors in a positive semidefinite slack factorization constrain its size. We bound the number of low-rank vertex factors in any fixed factorization, and use this to determine the asymptotic order of the minimum factorization size under any fixed bound on vertex-factor ranks: $\Theta(n\log n)$ for permutahedra $\Pi_n$ and $\Theta(\log N)$ for regular $N$-gons. In the rank-one case this gives the order of the minimum dimension of a space of real functions on the vertices in which every facet slack is a sum of squares, with no symmetry or degree restriction. For unrestricted lifts, the bound gives $\mathrm{xc}_{\mathrm{PSD}}(\Pi_n)\ge n+\log_3 n-O(1)$, and shows that a permutahedron factorization of linear size would need vertex factors of rank $\Omega(\log n)$ at all but a vanishing fraction of vertices.
  We also prove that every polytope of real positive semidefinite rank at most four has at most twelve vertices, and construct explicit size-four lifts for every square-symmetric octagon, so eight is attained. The upper bound combines a count of the polygon corners reached by curves of rank-one factors with incidence constraints on factor ranks. Whether eight is the maximum remains open.

papers.title: Biharmonic Lagrangian surfaces with constant Gaussian curvature in $2$-dimensional complex space forms
papers.authors: Yu Fu, Yanru Luo, Cezar Oniciuc
papers.abstract: Constant curvature is one of the most fundamental intrinsic conditions in submanifold geometry. Investigating the existence and classification of biharmonic submanifolds under intrinsic curvature constraints is generally difficult, since the biharmonic equation is expressed in terms of extrinsic data. In this paper, we obtain a complete classification of proper, that is non-minimal, biharmonic Lagrangian surfaces with constant Gaussian curvature in 2-dimensional complex space forms. As a consequence, we classify the proper biharmonic Lagrangian surfaces with flat normal bundle and prove that pseudo-umbilical biharmonic Lagrangian surfaces are necessarily minimal.

papers.title: A continuous-time limit for particle swarm optimization
papers.authors: Pascal Bianchi, Radu-Alexandru Dragomir, Yerkin Yesbay
papers.abstract: Particle swarm optimization (PSO) is a popular class of gradient-free methods for global optimization. We study a continuous-time model for momentum-free PSO with personal-best memory and global-best interaction. Unlike previous models which rely on smooth approximations, we keep the original discontinuous personal- and global-best processes. We study the small-step limit and show that weak limit points satisfy a stochastic differential inclusion: personal-best variables obey a relaxed record condition, while fast switching of the global-best selector leads to a convexified interaction. We then give conditions under which the true original selectors are recovered. Under suitable regularity and nondegeneracy assumptions, Brownian noise allows us to identify the personal-best processes with the latest record positions of the limiting trajectories and to prove that the particle attaining the global best is unique at almost every time. The resulting continuous-time dynamics retain both selection rules without smoothing them.

papers.title: Distinguishing graphs with simple spectrum by homomorphism counts
papers.abstract: We study which graph classes determine every graph with simple spectrum up to isomorphism by homomorphism counts from their members. We show that such a class has unbounded treewidth and Euler genus and contains a graph with the complete graph on seven vertices as a minor. To prove these conditions, we construct pairs of non-isomorphic cospectral graphs with simple spectrum, each bipartite, nonsingular and of maximum degree at most six. The construction attaches rooted trees to Cai-Furer-Immerman graphs and preserves homomorphism indistinguishability over every minor-closed class. We then prove that subcubic homomorphism counts determine every graph whose adjacency matrix has kernel dimension at most one. This extends the known result for nonsingular graphs and applies to all graphs with simple spectrum. We also prove that two graphs have the same subcubic homomorphism counts if and only if they have the same number of vertices and there is a bijective linear isometry between the images of their adjacency matrices that intertwines the adjacency operators and preserves the coordinatewise trilinear forms. Finally, we prove that homomorphism counts from the single-vertex graph and from subdivisions of any sequence of connected cubic graphs have the same distinguishing power as subcubic homomorphism counts if every complete graph is a minor of some member of the sequence.

papers.title: A Local Proof of Langlands's First Main Lemma for Local Epsilon Factors over Nonarchimedean Local Fields
papers.abstract: We give a complete local proof of Langlands's First Main Lemma for local epsilonfactors over nonarchimedean local fields. The proof builds on Dwork's p-adic calculations and Langlands's formulation of the local method. The present paper reformulates these calculations in a common normalization and extends the argument to equal characteristic. A more systematic treatment of stationary parameters and conductor cases is intended to make the calculations easier to follow. The author has also completed a local proof of Langlands's Second Main Lemma. Together with the present result and Langlands's remaining reductions, this gives a complete proof of the local construction of local epsilon factors envisioned by Langlands.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for $p$-adic Congruences and $p$-adic Interpolations of Sequences
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we treat the problem of determining when a sequence $\{c_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ with the exponential generating function $F(t)$ satisfies the congruence $c_{n+\ell p^k}\equiv c_n \pmod{p^{k+r}}$ for large $n$ and when its canonical interpolating functions are locally analytic. This type of congruence is often observed for several number-theoretic or combinatorial sequences, such as Bernoulli numbers, Euler numbers, and Fibonacci numbers. Traditionally, such congruences are proved by using $p$-adic integrations.
  In this paper, we present another approach to this problem. Instead of using $p$-adic integrals, we investigate an algebraic structure of the set of generating functions and establish some conditions on $F(t)$ that are equivalent to or sufficient for the congruence and smoothness of the interpolating functions. We also provide concrete applications of our framework to Genocchi numbers, generalized Euler numbers, and so on, which are outside the scope of the typical $p$-adic integration method.

papers.title: Lie weights for CM curves and unipotent Selmer dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove an equidistribution result for Galois characters in the graded Lie components $L_n$ associated to the $\mathbf{Q}_p$-fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve $X$ over a number field $k$ with geometrically CM Jacobian. That is, we consider the $p$-adic completion of a fixed character lattice, where we define measures $\mu_n$ counting normalized character multiplicities in $L_n$, and show that $(\mu_n)_n$ weakly converges to the Haar measure. The key idea to prove convergence is to write the Fourier coefficients of $\mu_n$ in terms of traces of operators on $L_n$ induced by symplectic operators on the Tate module, and control them with a known symplectic character formula, followed by Weyl's criterion for compact abelian groups. Our main arithmetic application is to combine equidistribution with the Iwasawa-theoretic method of Coates--Kim and a compactness argument for moving analytic loci, giving a dimension inequality for unipotent Selmer schemes: $\dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}H^1_f(G_{k,T},U_n)< \dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}\prod_{v\mid p}H^1_f(G_v,U_n)$ for all sufficiently large $n,$ with the quotient having limit superior at most $1/2.$ This answers a particular case of a conjecture by Kim, from which the finiteness of $X(\mathbf{Q})$ can be recovered when $k=\mathbf{Q}.$

papers.title: Self measurable embeddings of mapping class groups
papers.abstract: Given a finite-type orientable surface without boundary, outside of a few low-complexity surfaces, we show that any measurable embedding of the associated mapping class group into itself is a measure equivalence. This is a measure-theoretic analog to the result of Ivanov and McCarthy that mapping class groups are co-Hopfian.

papers.title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
papers.abstract: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert-Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.

papers.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
papers.abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $\Lambda_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partial\Lambda_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question remains open. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{\pi^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $\Lambda_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

papers.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
papers.abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a magma-operad (non-associative partial combination, restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.

papers.title: A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations
papers.authors: Jui-Yun Hung, Jiakun Liu, Neil Trudinger
papers.abstract: We give new proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation and the constant quadratic Hessian equation, based on the two-point maximum principle. The arguments require only one differentiation of the equation. For the Monge-Amp\`ere equation, the inhomogeneous term is assumed to be positive and continuously differentiable. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.

papers.title: $2$-large sets are sets of nil-Bohr recurrence
papers.abstract:
A set $S$ of positive integers is $2$-large if every two-coloring contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every such set meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass.
  We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood $B$ of $0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, restricting the common difference to $B$ increases the extremal number for $k$-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of $1+\varepsilon$, provided $k$ is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra
papers.abstract: We completely classify aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra $\mathcal{W}$ up to outer conjugacy. As a technical ingredient, based on the works of Connes, Herman--Ocneanu, Kishimoto, and Sato, we introduce a notion of weak stability for automorphisms of simple separable monotracial C$^*$-algebras. We also consider automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type and the Jiang--Su algebra. In particular, we classify aperiodic ``UHF-absorbing'' automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type up to outer conjugacy.

papers.title: Multi-dimensional centered rarefaction waves of gas dynamics with vacuum states
papers.abstract: We establish the local-in-time structural stability of two centered rarefaction waves bounding a vacuum region for the two-dimensional isentropic Euler equations with $p(\rho)=k\rho^\gamma$, for $\gamma\in(1,1.3]\cup\{\frac75,\frac53\}$. For general sufficiently small perturbations of the planar Riemann data, allowing nonzero vorticity, we construct an entropy solution that is continuous for positive time and whose five regions are separated by four characteristic surfaces. The conservative solution has uniform spatial $W^{2,\infty}$ bounds on each time slice of the central region in coordinates $(x_1/t,x_2)$; for $\gamma=7/5,5/3$, we also obtain spacetime $W^{2,\infty}$ regularity in $(t,x_1/t,x_2)$. The proof develops characteristic geometry directly for the symmetric first-order Euler system and uses two overlapping characteristic charts to separate matching with the exterior flow from estimates uniform up to vacuum. Fixed commutators without sound-speed weights exhibit a first-order null structure, while subtraction of explicit approximate solutions produces damping that cancels the leading antidamping bulk terms in the energy identity. An explicit analysis of the initial-slice ODEs identifies fractional powers and logarithmic terms at zero sound speed. The logarithmic coefficients couple vorticity to tangential variation of the initial data, revealing an obstruction to higher spatial regularity even when the powers of the sound speed have integer exponents. This analysis determines the finite approximation order used to close the energy and geometric estimates in the stated range. These ingredients provide the geometric and energy framework for the forthcoming second paper of this series, which will use finite evolving profiles to treat the full range $\gamma\in(1,\frac53]$.

papers.title: Scaling Limits of Density Fluctuation Fields of the Symmetric Partial Exclusion Processes Approaching the Zero Range Process
papers.abstract:
We study equilibrium fluctuations for the symmetric partial exclusion process (SPEP) on the one-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, an interacting particle system in which each site is occupied by at most $\alpha$ particles. We assume that the jump rate is decomposable and that the instantaneous current admits a gradient form. Our aim is to study the scaling limit of the density fluctuation field of the SPEP starting from an invariant measure and to derive the corresponding stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE).
  A distinctive feature of our setting is that the maximum number of particles per site depends on the scaling parameter $n$ as $\alpha=\alpha_n \propto n^a$ for some $a>0$, so that the model interpolates between the partial exclusion process ($\alpha <\infty$) and the symmetric zero range process (SZRP, $\alpha = \infty$). Under the diffusive rescaling in which the lattice spacing is $1/n$ and time is accelerated by a factor $n^2$, we prove that the density fluctuation field converges to the solution of the stochastic heat equation.
  The limiting SPDE coincides with the one obtained for the SZRP. A key ingredient in the proof is the convergence, under a suitable rescaling, of the partition function of the reversible measure of the SPEP to that of the SZRP. This convergence implies that expectations of a wide class of local functions under the reversible measure of the SPEP converge to the corresponding expectations under the reversible measure of the SZRP, and provides a rigorous sense in which the SPEP approximates the SZRP as $n\to\infty$.

papers.title: Cwikel estimates and Weyl's laws for $L\log L$ potentials on quantum tori
papers.abstract:
We prove an $L\log L$-endpoint Cwikel estimate on quantum tori $\mathbb T_\theta^d$, i.e., for every $d\geq 2$ and $x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$, \begin{equation*}
  \big\|(1-\Delta)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\lambda(x)(1-\Delta)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\big\|_{\mathcal{L}_{1,\infty}} \leq C_d \Norm{x}_{L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)}, \end{equation*} where $\lambda(x)$ is the left multiplication by $x$. Our argument actually gives an abstract weak Hilbert--Schmidt estimate for multiplication operators in finite von Neumann algebras whose $L_2$-spaces admit orthonormal bases of unitaries. As a consequence, it yields a critical Sobolev embedding $W_2^{d/2}\hookrightarrow\exp(L_2)$ on quantum tori. When $\theta=0$, our method also gives a simpler proof of the $L\log L$ Cwikel estimate on classical tori.
  As an application, we use the $C^*$-algebraic principal symbol map to prove Weyl's laws for sandwich operators \[
  S(1-\Delta)^{-d/4}\lambda(x)(1-\Delta)^{-d/4}T, \] where $x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$ and $S,T\in\Pi$, the $C^*$-algebra generated by $\lambda(C(\mathbb T_\theta^d))$ and Fourier multipliers with continuous homogeneous symbols of degree zero. We also prove a semiclassical Weyl's law for critical Schr\"odinger operators with $L\log L$ potentials.

papers.title: Dual-Inertial Bregman Methods with Energy-Based Safeguarding
papers.abstract: We develop dual-inertial Bregman proximal methods for convex optimization and analyze their convergence through an exact signed-drift representation. For unrestarted iterations, one-sided directional curvature control yields a last-iterate $\cO((1+\log k)/k^2)$ rate, improving to $\cO(k^{-2})$ under weighted summability. A computable energy-based safeguard guarantees a global $\cO(N^{-1})$ objective-gap bound, counting all proximal oracle calls. Under a stepsize condition and local quadratic growth with suitable kernel regularity, the safeguarded methods restart finitely and eventually converge linearly. Numerical experiments illustrate the methods on entropy regression and nonnegative least squares.

papers.title: Strong Lefschetz property of the Kirchhoff algebra of the complete tripartite graph $K_{1,1,n}$
papers.abstract: By Whitney's 2-isomorphism theorem, the cycle matroids of two graphs are isomorphic if and only if one graph can be transformed into the other by finitely many applications of two operations: separation or identification at a cut-vertex, and twisting. The complete tripartite graph whose vertex set is the disjoint union of two singletons and an $n$-element set is invariant, up to isomorphism, under these operations. In this paper we prove that the Macaulay inverse system (the Kirchhoff algebra) determined by the basis generating polynomial of the cycle matroid of such a graph has the strong Lefschetz property over a field of characteristic $0$. The proof reduces the non-degeneracy of the higher Hessians to the ranks of disjointness matrices of families of subsets (the Gottlieb--Wilson theorem) and to the representation theory of the symmetric group in relation to the Johnson scheme.

papers.title: Local Extrema and Infinite Derivatives of the Delange Function of Base 3
papers.abstract: The Delange function of base $3$ is the continuous function $T(x)=\sum_{j\ge0}3^{-j}\tau(3^jx)$ of Takagi type, where $\tau(x)=2\min\{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathbb{Z}),1/3\}$. Multiplied by $3^n$, its values at the points $m/3^n$ are the smallest numbers $\xi_n(m)=2(nm-S_3(m))$ of edges leaving a set of $m$ vertices in the ternary Hamming cube $Q_n^3$, where $S_3(m)=\sum_{j<m}s_3(j)$ and $s_3$ is the ternary digit sum. Both facts are known. We show that the local minima of $T$ are exactly the ternary rationals $m/3^n$, and that the local maxima are exactly the points $(m+1/2)/3^n+k$ with integers $k$, $m$, $n$ such that $n\ge0$, $0\le m<3^n$ and $s_3(m)=n$. We also characterize, in terms of the ternary digits $\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots$ of $x$, when $T$ has an infinite derivative at $x$ from one or both sides. At a ternary rational the right derivative is $+\infty$ and the left derivative is $-\infty$. At every other point, the right derivative is $+\infty$ exactly when $\sum_{j\le n}(1-\xi_j)\to+\infty$. The condition for the left derivative to be $+\infty$ is stronger and also involves the lengths of the maximal strings of zeros among the digits. For the value $-\infty$ the two sides are exchanged and the roles of zeros and twos are swapped. In particular, $T$ has an infinite derivative at every rational point that is not a ternary rational and whose period has different numbers of zeros and twos. We also determine the maximum of $\xi_n(m)$ over every block of sizes $a3^k\le m\le(a+1)3^k$, describe by the ternary digits of $h$ the sizes $h$ for which the $h$-extra edge connectivity of $Q_n^3$ equals $\xi_n(h)$, and compute the Fourier coefficients of $T$ and its variation at each level. Finally, we determine the level set at height $3/4$, which has dimension $\log2/\log9$, and show that no level set has a larger upper box dimension and that $\{x\in[0,1]:T(x)=y\}$ is finite for almost every $y$.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant and admissible univalent Blaschke pairs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the class of polynomials $P$ of degree at least $2$ with $P(0)=0$, $P'(0)=1$, let $S(P)=\min_{P'(c)=0}|P(c)/c|$ and let $\mathcal{M}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}}S(P)$ be Smale's mean value constant. Smale proved that $\mathcal{M}\le4$, observed that $\mathbb{M}\ge 1$, and asked whether $\mathcal{M}=1$. We show that $\mathcal{M}$ coincides with $$ \mathcal{B}=\sup\frac1{B(0)}, $$ the supremum running over pairs $(W,B)$ in which $W$ is a normalised univalent map of the standard unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ and $B$ is a finite Blaschke product with $B(0)>0$ such that $WB$ is locally univalent in $\mathbb{D}$. Smale's question is therefore a problem in univalent function theory. We also introduce the degree-restricted constants $\mathcal{B}_d$ for $B$ with $\mathrm{deg} B \le d$ and show that $$1.1018586788\ldots=\sqrt{\frac{8081}{6656}} \le \mathcal{B}_1 < \sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}=1.1832159566\ldots$$ This implies that $\mathcal{M}>1.1018$ and we also show that there are polynomials of arbitrarily large degree with $S(P)>1.1018$. The polynomial construction behind these results also settles Problems 1A and 1B of Smale's 1981 paper. For $P\in\mathcal P$ and an integer $k\ge2$ let $S_k(P)=\min_{P'(c)=0}|P^{(k)}(0)/k!|^{1/(k-1)}|P(c)|$. Smale proved, by L\"owner's coefficient estimate for inverses of univalent functions, that $\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}S_k(P)\le C_k^{1/(k-1)}<4$, where $C_k$ is the $k$-th Catalan number and he asked whether the constant $4$ (Problem 1A), or the constant $2=C_2$ for $k=2$ (Problem 1B), can be reduced. We prove that $\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}S_k(P)=C_k^{1/(k-1)}$ for every $k\ge2$. Hence the constants $4$ and $2$ cannot be reduced and the answers to both problems are negative.

papers.title: Characterisations for coarse embeddability via quasi-locality and Schur multipliers
papers.authors: Kang Li, Jiawen Zhang, Jingming Zhu
papers.abstract: We establish three new characterisations of coarse embeddability into Hilbert space for discrete metric spaces of bounded geometry in terms of escaping quasi-local couplings, Schur multipliers, and operator norm state localisation. As applications, we prove that if a sparse metric space of bounded geometry is coarsely embeddable into Hilbert space, then every ghost projection in the quasi-local algebra is compact, while we also provide a counterexample to the converse implication. Finally, we characterise coarse embeddability into Hilbert space via the relative Haagerup property for the quasi-local algebra, and investigate its relation to coarse embeddability into $\ell^p$ for $p>2$.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional coherent sheaf
papers.abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles, and let $\mathcal{E}_X$ and $\mathcal{E}_Y$ be exceptional coherent sheaves on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $\mathcal{E}_X^\perp\simeq \mathcal{E}_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.

papers.title: On Stopping Sets and Continuous-Time Decision Trees
papers.abstract: We study stopping sets and continuous-time decision trees (CTDTs) for Poisson point processes. We prove that every $\mu$-continuous CTDT has an explicit exploration representation: between successive discoveries, the explored set grows according to a deterministic rule depending on the points already observed. If $\mu$ is diffuse, we prove that the points are revealed one by one almost surely; this need not be imposed as a separate assumption. We also allow atoms of $\mu$, in which case all points at one location are revealed together. For diffuse $\mu$, we also prove that a locally bounded stopping set that reveals at most one Poisson point is attainable by a $\mu$-continuous exploration. More generally, an increasing sequence of locally bounded stopping sets, each revealing at most one additional point, can be attained by a single exploration viewed at successive stopping times. Finally, we prove the spatial Markov property of the Poisson point process without assuming that the stopping set contains finitely many points or admits a finite approximation. The proof is based on a general criterion for characterizing conditionally Poisson point processes using moment measures, and uses the multivariate Mecke formula on the complement of the stopping set.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
papers.abstract: This is the third of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on simple unstable theories. The Pauli group of quantum error correction, with anticommutation as its relation, has a simple unstable theory, like the random graph. Forking and the Kim--Pillay independence theorem acquire a meaning in stabilizer codes: forking recognizes logical errors, and the independence theorem glues syndromes.

papers.title: Hardy-Sobolev-Maz'ya inequalities for $\boldsymbol{1<p<2}$
papers.authors: Avas Banerjee, Micha{\l} Kijaczko, Vivek Sahu
papers.abstract: We establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$ for singularities supported on affine subspaces and for arbitrary domains. We first prove a Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality for singularities supported on affine subspaces of arbitrary codimension $1\leq k<N$, showing that the deficit in the sharp Hardy inequality controls a suitable weighted Sobolev norm. Combining the same convexity estimate with the one-dimensional approach of Frank and Loss in [9], we also establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on arbitrary domains with the mean distance to the boundary and thereby solve a problem posed in [9]. These results complete the previously unresolved subquadratic range $1<p<2$ and, together with the known results for $p\geq 2$, provide a unified Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya theory for all $1<p<N$ associated with plane singularities and general domains.

papers.title: Unconditional Bounds for Two, Three and Four Consecutive Moderate Gaps between Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.authors: C\'esar Ang\'on, Erick Ross, Ze Sen Tang, Boyang Zhao
papers.abstract: We prove unconditional positive-proportion results for consecutive moderate gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function. More precisely, for every fixed \(0<c\leq 1/4\), the lower asymptotic densities, normalized by \(N(T)\), of the occurrences of two, three, and four consecutive gaps, each of length at least \(2\pi c/\log T\), are at least \(0.3450014\ldots\), \(0.1812517\ldots\), and \(0.0175021\ldots\), respectively. Here, zeros are ordered by ordinate and counted with multiplicity, and \(N(T)\) denotes the number of nontrivial zeros with ordinates in \((0,T]\). These bounds address the corresponding cases of a question of Gonek and Sahay. The proof combines the methods of Alp\"oge--Furman and Lamzouri with local spectral estimates and cluster counting.

papers.title: Dynamic Programming for Value-at-Risk Markov Decision Processes in Continuous Spaces
papers.authors: Xian Chen, Erick Delage, Weikai Wang
papers.abstract: Value-at-Risk (VaR) is a widely adopted quantile-based risk measure in practice, yet incorporating VaR objectives into Markov decision processes (VaR MDPs) remains a longstanding challenge. Recent work has derived dynamic programming equations for VaR MDPs in finite state and action spaces but left the case of more general spaces unresolved. This paper establishes, for the first time, the validity of these equations in continuous spaces, for both finite- and infinite-horizon settings. Such cases naturally arise in many real-world dynamic decision-making problems. As an application, we study an optimal execution problem with a VaR objective and demonstrate that our framework enables the characterization of optimal dynamic strategies, resolving an open question in the field.

papers.title: Contractible Closed Reeb Orbits on Prequantization Bundles under Weak Index Conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the multiplicity of contractible closed Reeb orbits on prequantization circle bundles. Building on the existing multiplicity result Theorem 1.3 for closed Reeb orbits on prequantization $S^1$-bundles, we weaken the index assumptions by requiring only that the supporting contact form has no contractible periodic Reeb orbits with mean Conley-Zehnder index zero and no contractible good periodic Reeb orbits with Conley-Zehnder index 0, and we obtain a lower bound for the number of geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits carried by contact forms $\alpha$ on a prequantization $S^1$-bundle under certain natural topological assumptions (Theorem 1.6). In dimension five we further relax the index assumptions and show that, under a mild index condition imposed only on simple contractible periodic orbits and the same topological assumptions on the prequantization $S^1$-bundle, every non-degenerate supporting contact form carries at least $\dim H_*(B;\mathbb{Q})$ geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits (Theorem 1.11), in agreement with the conjectural lower bound for prequantization bundles.

papers.title: A nontopological triangulated category which is $\theta$-dg enhanced
papers.abstract: For every nonzero commutative ring $R$ and infinite cardinal $\theta$, we construct a nontopological triangulated category over $R$, whose thick subcategories generated by $<\theta$ objects admit $R$-linear dg enhancements, while the scalar action of $R$ is faithful.

papers.title: A conservative reduced collision model for the Boltzmann equation
papers.abstract: The evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is one of the major computational bottlenecks in solving the Boltzmann equation owing to the high dimensionality and the nonlinear structure of the collision term. In this work, a conservative reduced collision (RC) model is developed within the discrete velocity framework. The bilinear collision operator is approximated through a kernel tensor preassembled with the problem-dependent reduced bases for the distribution function and the collision term. Consequently, online evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is reduced to tensor contractions. Exact discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy is enforced by constructing the collision basis in the orthogonal complement of the space spanned by the discrete collision invariants. Several numerical experiments validate the efficiency of this RC model.

papers.title: On one-dimensional pressureless Euler--Poisson systems: existence for non-semiconvex interaction potentials
papers.authors: Andrew Xie, Emmanuel Alayande, Christopher Chun, Yusen Li, Rohan Mawalkar, Adrian Tudorascu, Adam Van
papers.abstract: One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are repulsive at short range and attractive at long range are useful simplified models that describe biological aggregation. In the current work we employ new techniques to treat compactly supported solutions in the case where the potential is $C^1$ and satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions although it is not necessarily semiconvex, as required in previous work. Central to this approach are uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system, which requires the potential be only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. In the semiconvex case, these bounds also yield convergence of time-shifted trajectories to an eternal solution. The tradeoff, just as in the case of repulsive Euler-Poisson, is that we cannot claim that the emerging solutions for non-semiconvex potentials are sticky.

papers.title: Mixed Chern curvature on complete flags
papers.abstract: We prove that the complete flag manifold SU(m)/T m-1, with m >= 3 and its standard complex structure, admits no invariant Hermitian metric with constant mixed Chern curvature when the coefficient of the holomorphic sectional curvature is nonzero. This extends the preceding nonexistence result for a particular Wallach metric on SU(3)/T2 to all invariant Hermitian metrics and to complete type-A flags of arbitrary dimension. Curvature evaluations on holomorphic root spheres contradict a necessary trace identity, covering both Kahler and non-Kahler invariant metrics and excluding both zero and nonzero curvature constants.

papers.title: A double-logarithmic lifespan bound for axisymmetric Euler equations with a small initial swirl
papers.authors: Zijin Li, Xu Xiao, Linbin Yang
papers.abstract: We study the axisymmetric incompressible Euler equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a small initial swirl. Fix $s>7/2$, and let $\boldsymbol{v}_0\in H^s(\mathbb{R}^3)$ be axisymmetric and divergence-free. If $\varepsilon=\|{\nabla\times(v_{0,\theta}\boldsymbol{e}_{\theta})}\|_{L^\infty}$ is sufficiently small, then the lifespan $T_*$ of the corresponding $H^s$ solution satisfies $$ T_{*}\geq\frac{C_s}{1+\|{\boldsymbol{v}_0}\|_{H^s}} \left[ \log\log (\varepsilon^{-1}) \right]^{3/7}\,. $$ This removes the assumption by Danchin (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 141:1979-1993, 2013) that the domain must be distant from the axis of symmetry. Moreover, even for $\boldsymbol{v}_0\in H^3$, our result improves the fourfold iterated-logarithmic lower bound for the lifespan obtained by Li and Zhou (Z. Angew. Math. Phys. 75:219, 2024) to a threefold iterated-logarithmic bound.

papers.title: Simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalences for tensor categories
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate monoidal derived equivalences between tensor categories with infinitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects. We introduce the notion of a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence and prove that a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence gives rise to a tensor equivalence. In addition, we investigate which tensor categories have the property that every monoidal derived equivalence between them is necessarily simple-shifted, and we establish some sufficient conditions for this property. As a corollary, we show that a monoidal derived equivalence between pointed tensor categories implies a tensor equivalence between them.

papers.title: Kurdyka-{\L}ojasiewicz-based convergence analysis with approximate weakly convex subdifferentials: bundle, quadratic penalty, and moving balls approximation methods
papers.authors: Jiefeng Xu, Guoyin Li, Ting Kei Pong
papers.abstract: The Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) property has been widely used for establishing global sequential convergence and analyzing local convergence rate of optimization algorithms. Most existing analysis frameworks rely on the construction of a suitable KL potential function such that along the sequence generated, it admits sufficient descents and its exact subdifferentials are suitably controlled by successive changes of the iterates. Nevertheless, a handful of important algorithms, such as bundle methods and quadratic penalty methods, are not known to have potential functions verifying the aforementioned properties, rendering their convergence analysis out of the reach of existing KL-based convergence analysis template. In this paper, we develop a new convergence analysis framework to extend the applicability of KL-based analysis. Our framework is built on a weakly convex KL potential function $\psi$. It allows approximate sufficient descents, the use of diminishing stepsizes, and controls on enlarged subdifferentials of $\psi$ known as the $\varrho$-weakly-convex-$\varepsilon$-subdifferentials. We illustrate the usefulness of our framework by establishing the global sequential convergence and analyzing the local convergence rate of some recent variants of bundle method, quadratic penalty method and moving balls approximation method. Specifically, we show that these methods fall under our framework by presenting explicit and natural choices of $\psi$, and derive suitable choices of model parameters, penalty parameters and constraint shrinkage parameters, respectively, for establishing their global sequential convergence and local convergence rate based on the KL property and exponent of $\psi$.

papers.title: On stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a general decomposition for regular closed semilinear sets, derived from a detailed study of their topological boundary. As an application, we characterize stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces over an ordered field, extending previous results of Hoffmann, Tran, and Ye.

papers.title: Convergence of the critical probabilities for stopping near the top of a random walk
papers.abstract:
Let \((S_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a Bernoulli random walk with \(P(X_i=1)=p\) and \(P(X_i=-1)=q=1-p\), and let \(M_n=\max\{S_0,\ldots,S_n\}\). We consider the semi-best selection problem of maximizing \(P(M_N-S_	au\le1)\) over stopping times \(	au\le N\). Allaart showed that the optimal decision in the critical state \((n,1)\) is determined by critical probabilities \(p_n\), and conjectured that \(p_n	o1/2\). In this note, we prove this conjecture. For every fixed \(p<1/2\), the stopping value converges to \(
u=1-(p/q)^2\), while the continuation value converges to \(2p
u\). Since \(2p
